data.title: Architectural and mathematical correctness
Correct ModelArray stacking semantics
data.body:
## Goal
- Make stacking create a leading axis while preserving every source array shape and model.
- Keep concatenation behavior explicit instead of hiding it behind stack terminology.

## Acceptance Criteria
- StackModelArrays requires equal non-empty shapes and returns [count]+shape.
- Model ordering and metadata copying are preserved.
- Shape mismatch, nil arrays, and empty input have deterministic errors.
- README examples and behavioral tests describe true stacking.

## Validation Gates
- go test -run 'ModelArray|Stack'
- go vet ./...

data.title: Make passivity results mathematically honest
data.body:
## Goal
- Distinguish finite-grid passivity evidence from analytic certification.
- Preserve compatibility while preventing sampled checks from presenting themselves as proofs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Results disclose whether they are sampled or certified and retain the checked frequency range/grid.
- State-space and FRD checks use correct Hermitian-part eigenvalue criteria for MIMO systems.
- Tests cover narrow-band or out-of-range counterexamples and invalid grids.
- Documentation states the exact guarantee.

## Validation Gates

- go vet ./...

data.title: Implement basis-invariant modal truncation
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace state-index deletion with a real ordered modal/Schur reduction workflow.
- Preserve complex-conjugate blocks and descriptor-system correctness or reject unsupported cases explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Mode selection controls retained modal blocks rather than source coordinates.
- Similarity-equivalent realizations retain the same selected poles and equivalent reduced responses.
- Complex conjugate pairs are never split; unstable-mode policy is explicit.
- Tests use coupled non-symmetric systems and compare pole/response invariants.

## Validation Gates
- go test -run 'Modal|Modred'
- go test -race -run 'Modal|Modred'
- go vet ./...

data.title: Assemble physical port connections into dynamics
data.body:
## Goal
- Make physical connections and grounding alter the assembled equations rather than only validate metadata.

- go test -race -run 'Physical|Assembly|Port'
- go vet ./...

data.title: Deep numerical architecture and performance
Replace inverse-based DARE with a generalized Schur solve
data.body:
## Goal
Make the discrete algebraic Riccati solver robust when A is singular or ill-conditioned by owning the full generalized symplectic-pencil workflow inside the Riccati module.

## Context
The current DARE path explicitly forms inverse-transpose(A), which rejects solvable singular-A problems and amplifies conditioning errors. SLICOT SB02OD uses an ordered generalized-Schur/deflating-subspace method, and the pinned Gonum fork provides the required Dgges/Dtgsen-class machinery.

## Acceptance criteria
- The implementation no longer computes an explicit inverse of A.
- Persistent tests cover singular-A and ill-conditioned, non-symmetric DARE cases with fixed values produced by an independent oracle.
- The returned X is symmetric, the scaled Riccati residual meets the existing tolerance policy, and the closed-loop eigenvalues are strictly inside the unit circle for stabilizing cases.
- Existing CARE/DARE APIs, workspace reuse, error semantics, and allocation expectations remain compatible.
- Focused benchmarks show no material regression on existing representative DARE sizes.

## Validation gates
- Run focused Riccati tests and oracle fixtures.
- Run focused before/after DARE benchmarks through benchstat.
- Run go fix ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -v -count=1.

data.title: Deepen the frequency-sweep evaluator
data.body:
## Goal
Make frequencyEvaluator own backend selection and reusable sweep workspaces so repeated frequencies do not rebuild transfer-function realizations unnecessarily.

## Context
Profiles show newTFWorkspace dominates allocation in FreqResponse and tuning. The evaluator currently converts a state-space model to transfer functions for multi-point sweeps, while single-point evaluation uses a reusable state-space solve. The LFT kernel also performs one duplicate diagonal multiply.

## Acceptance criteria
- frequencyEvaluator selects an evidence-backed state-space or transfer-function kernel based on model/grid shape, with the decision hidden from callers.
- Sweep workspaces are allocated once per response operation and reused across frequencies.
- The duplicate LFT diagonal multiply is removed.
- Persistent parity tests cover both selected kernels, non-symmetric A, continuous/discrete models, descriptor models, delays, and LFT responses.
- Numerical error is no worse than the current implementation against the existing reference behavior.
- Focused FreqResponse and LFT benchmarks show lower allocations and no material time regression across representative small and larger systems.

## Validation gates
- Run focused frequency tests.
- Run focused before/after frequency and LFT benchmarks through benchstat.
- Run go fix ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -v -count=1.

data.title: Add generalized-Schur DARE for singular and ill-conditioned models

data.body:
## Goal
Make the discrete algebraic Riccati solver robust when A is singular or ill-conditioned while preserving the fast path for well-conditioned models.

## Context
The former DARE path rejected solvable singular-A problems. An always-generalized implementation fixed that but caused a material pure-Go QZ allocation and runtime regression. The Riccati module now owns a condition-based kernel choice: the existing symplectic Schur reduction for well-conditioned A and a SLICOT/SciPy-style extended symplectic pencil for singular or poorly conditioned A.

## Acceptance criteria
- Singular and poorly conditioned A use an ordered generalized-Schur deflating-subspace solve.
- Well-conditioned models retain the established fast Schur kernel behind the same private owner.
- Persistent tests cover singular-A cross-term and ill-conditioned, non-symmetric DARE cases with fixed values produced by an independent SciPy oracle.
- The returned X is symmetric, the scaled Riccati residual meets the existing tolerance policy, and the closed-loop eigenvalues are strictly inside the unit circle for stabilizing cases.
- Existing CARE/DARE APIs, workspace reuse, and error semantics remain compatible.
- Focused benchmarks show no material regression on existing representative DARE sizes.

## Validation gates
- Run focused Riccati tests and oracle fixtures.
- Run focused before/after DARE benchmarks through benchstat.
- Run go fix ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -v -count=1.

## Completion note
- Added a private discrete-stable-subspace owner that chooses the regular or generalized kernel from the reciprocal condition estimate of A.
- Implemented the extended symplectic pencil, QR input-column deflation, ordered generalized Schur solve, and generalized eigenvalue recovery.
- Added singular cross-term and ill-conditioned non-symmetric SciPy oracle fixtures and corrected the cross-term residual helper.
- Ten-sample benchstat: n=10 timing unchanged; n=50 +2.37%; allocation counts unchanged and bytes decreased slightly.

## Goal
Make frequencyEvaluator own backend selection and reusable sweep workspaces so short sweeps avoid rebuilding transfer-function realizations while long sweeps keep polynomial-evaluation throughput.

## Context
Profiles showed newTFWorkspace dominated FreqResponse allocation, but always using direct state-space solves materially slowed longer grids. Persistent kernel benchmarks established a crossover governed primarily by state count times frequency count. The evaluator now owns that choice and falls back to transfer-function evaluation if a direct sweep encounters a pole.

## Acceptance criteria
- frequencyEvaluator selects the state-space or transfer-function kernel from an evidence-backed work limit hidden from callers.
- State-space sweep workspaces are allocated once per response operation and reused across frequencies.
- Persistent parity tests cover both selected kernels, a non-symmetric A, delay phases, descriptor evaluation, continuous/discrete behavior, and pole fallback.
- Numerical error is no worse than EvalFr within the established tolerance.
- Focused FreqResponse benchmarks show lower allocations and runtime for short sweeps with no material regression for longer, delayed, or LFT sweeps.

## Validation gates
- Run focused frequency tests.
- Run focused before/after frequency and LFT benchmarks through benchstat.
- Run go fix ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -v -count=1.

## Completion note
- Added private state-space and transfer-function sweep kernels under frequencyEvaluator and a conservative state-count by frequency-count work policy.
- Added transfer-function fallback when a short direct sweep reaches a pole, preserving multi-frequency behavior.
- Added persistent kernel-crossover and public short-sweep benchmarks plus parity coverage for both kernels and all delay forms.
- Ten-sample benchstat for the 10-state, 8-frequency case: runtime -42.19%, bytes -85.74%, allocations -94.44%. Long, delayed, B747, and LFT sweeps were unchanged within noise.
- The duplicate LFT multiply noted during initial planning was already absent after synchronizing with origin/main, so no LFT code change was needed.

# Unify complex singular-value evaluation

## Goal
Give the frequency-analysis numerical module one reusable singular-value implementation and make tuning goals consume flat response storage without per-frequency matrix cloning.

## Context
tuning_goal.go duplicated complex singular-value logic using mat.SVD and Values(nil), while frequency_svd.go already owned reusable buffers for Sigma and FRD operations. The duplicate path allocated heavily and could drift numerically.

## Acceptance criteria
- One internal complex-SVD workspace owns singular-value evaluation for Sigma, FRD, and tuning goals.
- Tuning consumes stride-correct flat frequency-response slices without constructing a new matrix per frequency.
- Persistent tests compare maximum singular values against Gonum SVD over rectangular, rank-deficient, scaled, and non-symmetric complex matrices.
- Existing tuning-goal values and tolerances are preserved or improved.
- Focused tuning benchmarks show lower allocations and no material time regression.

## Completion note
- `complexSVDWorkspace` now owns full and maximum singular-value evaluation for Sigma, FRD, and tuning goals.
- Tuning reads frequency-major response blocks directly and allocates only weighted matrix products when weights are present.
- Scale normalization prevents overflow and underflow in Gram formation; persistent Gonum-oracle tests cover rectangular, rank-deficient, non-symmetric, `1e-150`, `1e150`, and vector `1e200` inputs.
- Ten-sample benchstat results: MIMO weighted gain time -52.11%, bytes -30.91%, allocations -80.91%; dynamic weighted MIMO time -53.25%, bytes -14.61%, allocations -66.07%; SISO time -7.93% with unchanged allocations.

## Validation gates
- Focused frequency-SVD and tuning tests passed.
- Focused before/after tuning benchmarks compared through benchstat.
- `go fix ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -v -count=1` passed.

# Batch all-input step and impulse responses

## Goal
Make `timeResponsePlan` simulate all input channels in one state propagation pass for step and impulse responses.

## Context
Step and Impulse allocated an input history and called Simulate once per input. That repeated dispatch, intermediate allocation, and output assembly. The planner now owns discretization, delays, output layout, and the all-input simulation policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Step and Impulse use a batched all-input kernel where applicable, with delay or exceptional paths safely routed through equivalent behavior.
- The public row ordering `j*p+i`, time grids, feedthrough behavior, continuous/discrete semantics, and delay semantics remain unchanged.
- The kernel uses stride-aware raw storage and preallocated buffers.
- Persistent parity tests cover non-symmetric MIMO systems, continuous and discrete models, gain-only systems, feedthrough, and delays.
- Focused MIMO benchmarks show fewer allocations and lower runtime; SISO has no material regression.

## Completion note
- `timeResponsePlan` now owns standard-input response policy and batches delay-free, standard multi-input systems with contiguous input-major state buffers.
- SISO, descriptor, zero-output, and delayed/internal-delay systems retain the established `Simulate` path.
- Independent-simulation parity tests cover non-symmetric continuous and discrete MIMO models, feedthrough, gain-only models, delays, Step, Impulse, and output row ordering.
- Ten-sample benchstat results: MIMO Step time -50.29%, bytes -70.51%, allocations -66.49%; MIMO Impulse time -50.27%, bytes -70.51%, allocations -66.49%. SISO Step and Impulse were about 2% faster with unchanged allocation counts.

## Validation gates
- Focused response tests passed.
- Focused before/after SISO and MIMO Step/Impulse benchmarks compared through benchstat.
- `go fix ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -v -count=1` passed.

# Make physical assembly own matrices once

## Goal
Move physical-model copy and validation ownership into `physicalAssemblyPlan` so assembly crosses one ownership boundary instead of cloning components and aggregate matrices repeatedly.

## Context
The connected path copied every component, copied into aggregate matrices, then copied the aggregate again through the public Descriptor constructor. The synchronous assembly plan can validate borrowed inputs while building an owned aggregate result directly.

## Acceptance criteria
- The plan produces an independently owned Descriptor model with no mutable aliasing to component matrices or port metadata.
- Redundant component and final aggregate clones are removed through an internal validated ownership-transfer seam.
- Constraint assembly uses stride-aware raw storage rather than repeated At/Set calls in hot loops.
- Persistent mutation tests prove that changing source components after assembly cannot change the result, and changing the result cannot change sources.
- Existing constraint, port, and validation behavior is unchanged.
- Focused physical-assembly benchmarks show fewer allocations and no material time regression.

## Completion note
- The synchronous plan validates and borrows component inputs, then creates the result at the aggregate-matrix ownership boundary.
- Internal `newDescriptorOwned` validates dimensions and descriptor shape while adopting plan-owned matrices; public `NewDescriptor` retains defensive copies.
- Augmented matrices and constraint rows now use stride-aware raw storage.
- Mutation tests cover matrices, signal metadata, and port metadata in both source-to-result and result-to-source directions.
- Ten-sample benchstat results for eight connected components: time -30.96%, bytes -38.00%, allocations -29.00%.

## Validation gates
- Focused physical-assembly tests passed.
- Focused before/after assembly benchmarks compared through benchstat.
- `go fix ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test -v -count=1` passed.

# Integrate the numerical architecture and performance audit

## Goal
Close the audit with repository-wide correctness, static-analysis, and benchmark evidence, and record why other routines remain unchanged.

## Context
The codebase-wide inventory found five evidence-backed opportunities. Most remaining solver time is inside LAPACK/BLAS calls with existing reusable workspaces; changing those without a demonstrated bottleneck would increase risk without an architectural payoff.

## Production routine-family classification

### Changed after measurement or oracle failure
- Riccati and optimal-control kernel: `riccati.go` now routes singular or poorly conditioned DARE problems through an extended symplectic pencil and ordered generalized Schur decomposition while retaining the fast regular path.
- Frequency sweep: `frequency.go` now owns the state-space versus transfer-function kernel decision and reusable short-sweep workspace.
- Complex singular values and tuning: `frequency_svd.go` and `tuning_goal.go` share one scaled, reusable complex-SVD owner and flat frequency-response storage.
- Standard time responses: `response.go` owns Step/Impulse policy and batches delay-free MIMO propagation while retaining established exceptional paths.
- Physical assembly: `physical_assembly.go` and the internal seam in `state_space_utils.go` establish one validated matrix-ownership boundary.

### Existing deep owners; intentionally unchanged
- Core model, validation, domain, descriptor, metadata, and sampled layouts: `ss.go`, `descriptor.go`, `errors.go`, `names.go`, `time_domain.go`, `signal_metadata.go`, `sampled_data.go`, `sampled_response.go`, `sampled_signal.go`, `doc.go`.
- Delay representation, conversion, topology, and safe feedback: `delay.go`, `delay_bank.go`, `delay_conversion_policy.go`, `delay_topology.go`, `delay_visibility.go`, `pade.go`, `thiran.go`, `feedback_lft.go`, `safe_feedback.go`, `wellposed.go`.
- Interconnection and generalized-model workflows: `connect.go`, `interconnection_topology.go`, `lft.go`, `generalized.go`, `loopsens.go`, `sumblk.go`.
- Conversion and realization workflows: `augstate.go`, `canon.go`, `conversion_plan.go`, `convert.go`, `inv.go`, `poly.go`, `polynomial_channel.go`, `pzmap.go`, `realization_policy.go`, `transfer.go`, `transform.go`, `zpk.go`.
- Matrix equations, decompositions, balancing, reduction, and zeros: `balance.go`, `ctrbobsv.go`, `eigdecomp.go`, `gramian.go`, `lyapunov.go`, `matlog.go`, `matrix_equation_problem.go`, `minimal.go`, `modal_reduction.go`, `modsep.go`, `prescale.go`, `qr_colpivot.go`, `rq_rowpivot.go`, `sminreal.go`, `ssbal.go`, `stability.go`, `stabsep.go`, `staircase.go`, `zeros.go`. Profiles place the remaining cost in LAPACK/BLAS kernels; these routines already centralize workspace, policy, or result construction.
- Frequency and robust analysis outside the changed sweep/SVD paths: `energy_policy.go`, `frd.go`, `freqrestest.go`, `loop_analysis.go`, `margin.go`, `norms.go`, `nyquist.go`, `passivity.go`, `rlocus.go`.
- Simulation and time-response analysis outside standard-input batching: `gensig.go`, `simulate.go`, `response_info.go`; delay dispatch and general input histories remain cohesive and benchmark-stable.
- Estimation, identification, local approximation, and random models: `covar.go`, `covariance_policy.go`, `ekf.go`, `linearize.go`, `local_approx.go`, `observer.go`, `random.go`, `sysid.go`.
- Controllers and synthesis outside DARE: `controller.go`, `controller_observer_policy.go`, `h2syn.go`, `hinfsyn.go`, `lqg.go`, `pid.go`, `pidtune.go`, `smith.go`, `synthesis_partition.go`, `tunable.go`, `tuning.go`.
- Collections and matrix utilities: `model_array.go`, `matutil.go`; ModelArray inherits the Step improvement without a second implementation.

This classification accounts for all 97 production Go files.

## Accuracy evidence
- SciPy/SLICOT-style generalized-pencil DARE tests cover singular A with cross term and ill-conditioned non-symmetric A; regular cases retain the existing ordered-Schur path.
- Frequency kernels agree for non-symmetric continuous/discrete systems and all delay forms, with pole fallback preserving prior behavior.

data.title: HinfSyn ignores D22: add loop shift for nonzero D22
data.body:
## Goal
- HinfSyn returns a correct controller when the generalized plant has D22 ≠ 0 (proper, non-strictly-proper plants; Tustin-converted discrete plants). Today it silently designs for D22 = 0.

## Context
- hinfsyn.go:25-28 unpacks D11, D12, D21 from partitionGeneralizedPlant but never reads gp.D22. h2syn.go:37-40 at least rejects D22 ≠ 0.
- newController (synthesis_partition.go:83) always builds K with D = 0.
- Standard fix (Zhou/Doyle; MATLAB hinfsyn): synthesize K0 for the plant with D22 = 0, then K = K0 (I + D22 K0)^-1 (well-posedness: I + D22 DK0 invertible; DK0 = 0 so always well-posed for the current solver).
- Tests today only cover D22 = 0 (hinfsyn_test.go).
- Consumer: process-lab mixed-sensitivity / partitions H∞ dock guards D22 ≠ 0 until this lands (process-lab ergo NJXS66).

## Acceptance Criteria
- HinfSyn with D22 ≠ 0 returns K such that LFT(P, K) is stable and HinfNorm(LFT(P, K)) ≤ γ(1+tol).
- H2Syn: either same loop shift or keep rejecting with a named error; document which.
- D22 = 0 results are unchanged (bitwise-identical controllers on existing tests).
- Doc comment states the D22 handling.

## Validation Gates
- Run: go test ./... -run 'HinfSyn|H2Syn' with a new test: SISO plant with direct feedthrough (e.g. G = (s+2)/(s+1)) in a mixed-sensitivity P; assert closed-loop stability and norm ≤ γ, and that the pre-fix code fails it.

data.title: Add Augw/Mixsyn mixed-sensitivity generalized plant
data.body:
## Goal
- Augw(G, W1, W2, W3) builds the mixed-sensitivity generalized plant P (z1 = W1·e, z2 = W2·u, z3 = W3·G·u, y = e = r − G·u); Mixsyn(G, W1, W2, W3) = Augw + HinfSyn returning K, CL and γ.

## Context
- MATLAB precedent: augw / mixsyn. Any weight may be nil (omitted rows).
- HinfSyn inverts D12ᵀD12 without regularization: for strictly proper G, only W2's feedthrough fills D12, so W2 = nil must fail clearly (or document ε·I). W3·G must be proper.
- MIMO: weights may be scalar (applied as scalar×I) or square per channel.
- Depends on the D22 loop-shift task when G has direct feedthrough (D22 = −D_G).
- Consumer: process-lab H∞ mixed-sensitivity dock (would otherwise build augw in its own studio package).

## Acceptance Criteria
- P partition sizes and names (w, z, y, u) correct for SISO and 2×2.
- Mixsyn on a textbook example (e.g. Skogestad & Postlethwaite 2.8) gives γ within tolerance of the published/MATLAB value; closed loop stable; σ(S) ≤ γ/|W1| etc.
- Errors: improper W3·G, missing D12 rank, discrete/delay plants.

## Validation Gates
- Run: go test -run 'Augw|Mixsyn'; benchmark Mixsyn at plant orders 2, 10, 30.

data.title: HinfSyn central controller missing D21 B1' X term (closed loop exceeds gamma)
data.body:
Pre-existing bug found while fixing FOUJZQ. Fix ships in PR #173 commit 2e9f5b2 (pending coordinator approval to merge).
Repro: HinfSyn on mixed-sensitivity plant for G=(s+2)/(s+1), W1=1/(s+0.1), W2=0.1, D22 zeroed -> gamma 0.087, HinfNorm(LFT(P,K)) = 1.7e7. Also B1D21'!=0 variants of TestHinfSyn_Simple exceed gamma slightly (1.4153 vs 1.4142).
Cause: hinfsyn.go Ak omitted Zp*L*ginv2*D21*B1'*X (Zhou/Doyle general D11=0 formula).

data.title: HinfSyn ignores D11 ≠ 0
data.body:
hinfSolveRiccatis uses DGKF D11=0 formulas; D11 only sets bisection lower bound sigma_max(D11). With D11 != 0 bisection accepts gamma ~ sigma_max(D11) and the returned K's closed loop exceeds it.
Repro: mixed sensitivity G=1/(s+1), W2=0.1, v=r-y. W1=0.5/(s+0.005) (D11=0): gamma 0.234777 = ||LFT||inf OK. W1 biproper makeweight DC 100, HF 0.5, crossover ~0.5 rad/s (D11=0.5): gamma 0.5000004 but ||LFT||inf 0.606. 2x2 plants: 18-95% excess.
Files: hinfsyn.go, synthesis_partition.go. Source: process-lab ergo VDO5WS.
Fix: Glover-Doyle general formulas (ZDG ch.17 Thm 17.1).

data.title: HinfSyn D11=0 path accepts spurious Riccati solutions at jw-axis eigenvalues
data.body:
solveHamiltonianRiccati sorts eigenvalues by wr<0 with no imaginary-axis tolerance. When H has jw-axis eigenvalues (gamma below the Riccati threshold), rounding (wr ~ +-1e-16) can yield sdim == n and a spurious PSD 'solution', so bisection accepts infeasible gammas.
Evidence: in the D11 != 0 fix (branch fix-hinfsyn-d11), plant A=[-0.5 1;-2 -1], B=[1 0 0;0 1 1], C=[1 0;0 .5;1 1], D=[0 0 0;0 2 1;0 1 0] was 'feasible' at scattered gamma in [0.65,0.9] (true opt 0.904) until a 1e-9 relative axis check was added (hinfAxisTol). The D11 = 0 path (hinfSolveRiccatis) still passes axisTol=0 to keep results bitwise identical; it likely has the same exposure.
Fix: pass hinfAxisTol in hinfSolveRiccatis too after checking a D11=0 repro; accept bitwise changes.

data.title: HinfNorm overestimates norm of high-order closed loops
data.body:
HinfNorm overestimates the H-inf norm of a high-order stable closed loop.
Repro (controlsys branch fix-hinfsyn-d11, test fixtures randomHinfTestPlant(100,2,7) + mixedSensitivityPlant(G,1,0.01,0,0.1)): HinfSyn gamma 0.3940623 (matches SLICOT SB10AD 0.3940621); LFT(P,K) (202 states) swept in numpy (dense log grid + fine grid near 6.74 rad/s) peaks at 0.39406228; HinfNorm returns 0.5745636 at omega 6.742. Biproper W1 variant: numpy 0.6639667, HinfNorm 0.7758776.
Cause: hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs trusts near-axis Dgees eigenvalues (threshold sqrt(eps)*max(gamma,|lambda|)) without verifying sigma_max(G(jw)) at candidate frequencies; unbalanced Dgees on 404x404 may also be inaccurate. This is process-lab KHPJPC repro 2 (not a HinfSyn bug).
Fix idea: Bruinsma-Steinbuch-style verification: evaluate sigma_max at candidate w and midpoints; certified lower bounds only.

data.title: FreqResponse sweeps lose accuracy for high-order models (TF conversion)
data.body:
FreqResponse (and Sigma, Bode, which call it) switches every delay-free sweep with more than 80/n points to a transfer-function (polynomial) conversion (frequency.go useStateSpaceSweep, directFrequencySweepWorkLimit = 80). For n >= 41, any sweep of 2+ points goes through the polynomial path, which is catastrophically inaccurate at high order.
Evidence: 204-state closed loop from randomHinfTestPlant(100,2,7) mixed sensitivity (branch fix-hinfsyn-d11): Sigma on a 51-point grid reported sigma_max 0.5746 at 6.74 rad/s; the pointwise state-space solve and numpy both give 0.3941. HinfNorm now uses FreqResponsePointwise (PR #174), but Sigma/Bode/FreqResponse users still get wrong curves for high-order models.
Fix idea: use Hessenberg-form state-space sweep (O(n^2) per frequency) instead of TF conversion; drop the TF path for n above a small threshold.

data.title: HinfNorm reads pointwise sigma noise as a peak on non-minimal near-optimal closed loops
data.body:
controlsys v1.7.0 HinfNorm (pointwise sigma, confirmed crossings) returns ~7e-6 relative above the true norm on a near-optimal HinfSyn closed loop whose LFT realization is non-minimal and ill-conditioned at low frequency. v1.6.1 HinfNorm returned the true value on the same loop (same K, same gamma).

Repro (process-lab internal/studio, TestHinfMixedSensitivityMIMOWeightsScalingAndH2/"strict W1, W2 off"):
- G: A=[-1 .2 0; 0 -2 .5; .1 0 -3], B=[1 0; 0 1; .5 .5], C=[1 0 .2; 0 1 0], D=0 (3 states, 2x2)
- mixed sensitivity v = r - y, W1 = 1/(s+0.01) (strict, D11=0), W2 = 1e-3 (tiny control penalty), W3 off
- HinfSyn gamma = 0.03195497394; K.D = 0
- HinfNorm(LFT(P,K)) = 0.03195519835 @ w = 0.004927 (excess 7.0e-6)
- Pointwise sigma of the closed-loop realization jitters +-1e-5 at w < 0.02 (0.03195485..0.03195519), and the batched Sigma sweep differs from pointwise by ~5e-5 there.
- Frequency-domain LFT from P(jw) and K(jw) separately: 0.0319549783 flat over w in [0, 0.1] (excess 1.4e-7) -> the true norm meets gamma.
- Balreal(LFT) fails (gramian not PD: non-minimal); MinimalRealization (n=10) gives 0.03195624 @ w=0 (4e-5 excess) -> worse.
Impact: process-lab tests assert norm <= gamma(1+1e-6); this case needs 1e-5 (upstream uses 1e-5 for ill-conditioned loops). Studio's 1% product tolerance unaffected.
Suggestion: evaluate sigma with a better-conditioned closed loop (e.g. staircase/ssbal before sweep, or accept crossings only when confirmed by a refined evaluation), or document achievable accuracy.
Files: controlsys hinfnorm.go.

data.title: HinfNorm under-reports peak on ill-conditioned closed loops
data.body:
## Problem
HinfNorm returned a value 8.6e-6 relative below a dense EvalFr sweep peak on a closed loop with ~1e-6 rad/s dynamics and ||K|| ~ 1e4. Its Hamiltonian imaginary-axis test appears to miss crossings.

## Evidence
Plant: generalized P in TestHinfSyn_ControllerMeetsGammaNearSingularEdge (hinfsyn_test.go). Build the central controller at gamma = 0.5074089765548706 (the bisection edge, before hinfControllerBackoff) and close with LFT:
- arm64: HinfNorm/gamma-1 = 3.19e-7; 200k-point log sweep 1e-8..1e3 rad/s peak/gamma-1 = 8.92e-6 at w=3.5e-6
- amd64: HinfNorm/gamma-1 = 1.71e-6; sweep 8.08e-6
At gamma(1+1e-4) HinfNorm and sweep agree (-1.68e-7), so only ill-conditioned loops are affected.

## Notes
Found while fixing process-lab 3FFQZL (fixed by building K off the edge). Distinct from process-lab 2H6SLA (HinfNorm perf). Files: norms.go HinfNorm, hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs/candidatePeak.

data.title: Correct impulse-invariant C2D initial sample
data.body:
## Outcome
Make impulse-invariant C2D match MATLAB sampled impulse responses, including the k=0 sample.

## Evidence
convert.go DiscretizeImpulse sets Bd=Ts*Ad*B but leaves D unchanged. For H(s)=1/(s+1), MATLAB returns Ts*z/(z-exp(-Ts)); existing code yields Ts*exp(-Ts)/(z-exp(-Ts)), losing h(0). Proper direct-feedthrough semantics must be checked against MATLAB; sampled impulses cannot represent a Dirac delta. Source: https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/2173087-how-does-c2d-method-compute-the-matrices-ad-and-bd-for-both-zoh-and-foh-as-method ; official impulse scaling: https://www.mathworks.com/help/releases/r2023a/pdf_doc/control/rn.pdf

## Done when
Canonical impulse C2D returns the correct Ts*C*B feedthrough and all sampled dynamic impulse values, preserves names/source, and defines direct-feedthrough/delay behavior against reference evidence. No migration required. Internal-delay unsupported cases are explicit.

## Check
Persistent analytic scalar/non-symmetric MIMO fixtures compare Ts*C*exp(A*k*Ts)*B from k=0 onward. Validate documented delay cases and direct feedthrough; no roundtrip-only oracle.

## Repro
For continuous 1/s, DiscretizeMatched(0.1) inserts a z=-1 zero and uses a midband real-part gain; existing coefficients are 0.06366198(z+1)/(z-1), instead of MATLAB's forward Euler 0.1/(z-1).
For 11/(s*(s+1)), MATLAB's published matched output is approximately 0.05234(z+1)/((z-1)*(z-0.9048)); controlsys inserts two z=-1 zeros, also misnormalizes singular DC gain.
## Files/evidence
convert.go DiscretizeMatched/matchedGain/matchedGainFallback. Repro source /tmp/matched-proof.go. MATLAB docs pid2 matched IFormula=ForwardEuler: https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/pid2.html . Independent MATLAB-executed source fixture: https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/2175248-one-zero-is-missing-in-the-result-of-c2d-function-uses-matche . Correct conventional artificial-zero count is max(relative degree-1,0); preserve leading low-frequency term when DC singular.
## Done
Correct matched root and gain conventions; analytic independent integrator and singular-DC second-order fixtures, regular-DC proper and biproper cases. Ensure reverse matched restores intended continuous response.

data.body:
Outcome: Match MATLAB ZOH D2C negative-real-pole order without expanding unrelated positive or conjugate-pair modes.
Repro: d2cZOHRealExtension in convert_reverse_hold.go doubles all n rational states. Discrete diag(.8,-.8), B=[1,1], C=[1,1], D=0 requires three continuous real states; current result has four. Existing sampled responses are correct but unnecessary states violate ordinary MATLAB method parity and waste performance/memory.
Done when: retain original n states first, add only rank of negative spectral subspace where a well-conditioned real extension exists; return actual initial-state map and preserve named inputs/outputs. Near-branch/ill-conditioned cases need explicit error or documented verified fallback, not false minimal-order claims. Avoid any added work on common positive-pole fast path.
Check: independent mixed-positive/negative nonsymmetric and defective-pole fixtures, conjugate pairs near negative branch, expected state counts, nonzero initial-state sampled responses and source immutability. New rare-path benchmark latency/allocations. Reference: https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.d2c.html
Possible implementation: original real extension has A=[ReL,-ImL;ImL,ReL], B=[ReLb;ImLb]. Orthogonal basis Q spanning ImL lets compress lower alias states only, retaining all original states first. Select rotation angle so existing nonnegative conjugate pairs don't cross the logarithm cut; verify invariant-subspace/reconstruction residuals before compression.

data.title: Support fractional internal feedback delays in ZOH and modified FOH conversion
data.body:
## Reproduction
Construct scalar New(A=-1,B=1,C=1,D=0,Dt=0). SetInternalDelay([]float64{.15},B2=.2,C2=1,D12=0,D21=0,D22=0). DiscretizeWithOpts(.1,C2DOptions{Method:C2DMethodZOH}) and Method:C2DMethodFOH both return ErrFractionalDelay: fractional internal feedback delay 0.15 is unsupported. Tested live 2026-10-02; .24 and .35 also rejected. Tau=.2 succeeds.

## Files and cause
conversion_delay.go discretizeInternalModel rejects every non-Tustin internal Tau not integer sample multiple. conversion_plan.go discretizeInternalDelay also rejects fractional external delays when an internal feedback delay is present. The existing external-delay ZOH/FOH algorithms cannot be applied to a closed feedback loop without defining sampled internal signal interpolation.

## Independent evidence
https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ug/continuous-discrete-conversion-methods.html (ZOH Method for Systems with Time Delays): MATLAB decomposes internal tau=k*Ts+rho, absorbs fractional rho into the augmented rational model, discretizes that model, and preserves k as internal discrete delay. This is approximate for feedback delays. FOH documents the same delay treatment. This is a documented support gap; no locally executed MATLAB coefficient fixture is available.

## Done when
- Support arbitrary positive fractional internal LFT Tau for ordinary proper SISO/MIMO models using documented ZOH/modified-FOH internal-delay approximation; do not silently round or substitute Pade.
- Combine existing internal delays with fractional external I/O delays. Validate mixed delays, zero integer remainder, non-symmetric MIMO dynamics and legal feedback feedthrough.
- DelayModeling delay/state preserve response and expected state/history contracts. Report approximation; no false exactness/state mapping.
- Independent sampled/internal-channel fixtures plus MATLAB fixture if available; preserve source/names. Benchmark latency/alloc on representative delay counts and keep no-delay fast paths unchanged.

data.title: Match MATLAB conversion Thiran maximum-order and integer-remainder semantics
data.body:
## Reproduction
Scalar New(A=-1,B=1,C=1,D=0,Dt=0), InputDelay=[]float64{.24}, DiscretizeWithOpts(.1,C2DOptions{Method:C2DMethodTustin,ThiranOrder:3}) returns ErrFractionalDelay with ThiranDelay: delay 2.4000 samples < order-0.5 = 2.5 (unstable). MATLAB documents a stable order3 thiran(2.4,1) with denominator [1,.5294,-.04813,.004159] and reversed numerator. Same normalized delay.
For Tau=.02, Ts=.1, ThiranOrder3 should use order ceil(.2)=1; current helper forces order3 and rejects. For Tau=.54, Ts=.1, maxOrder3 documented integer remainder ceil(5.4)-3=3 with filter effective delay2.4; existing ThiranDelay uses round(5.4)-3=2, filter delay3.4, yielding different coefficients and integer split.

## Files and evidence
conversion_delay.go applyConversionThiran -> delay_bank.go buildSampleDelayChannel -> thiran.go ThiranDelay; current helper interprets maximum conversion order as fixed order and enforces too restrictive D>=N-.5. Exact explicit-order stability condition is D>N-1, and ceil(D) satisfies it for fractional D.
Official coefficient formula and numeric reference: https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/thiran.html ; ThiranOrder is a maximum and integer/filter split described at https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/c2doptions.html and https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ug/continuous-discrete-conversion-methods.html . Note conversion guide prints max in one filter-order equation despite surrounding maximum-state contract; use standalone thiran coefficient definition and max-order description, validate independently.

## Done when
- Conversion chooses N=min(ceil(D),ThiranOrder), integer remainder max(0,ceil(D)-N), and effective D remainder; integer delays remain exact.
- Fix incorrect minimum stable effective-delay rejection where necessary. Do not silently promise arbitrary high-order numerical conditioning.
- Cover delay shorter than requested max order, D2.4 published coefficient fixture, D5.4 integer split, tiny delay, multiple channels, delay/state modeling and matched/Tustin callers. Verify source immutability/response independently; measure representative allocations/latency.

data.title: Apply Thiran filters to internal feedback delays during Tustin conversion
data.body:
## Reproduction
Scalar New(A=-1,B=1,C=1,D=0,Dt=0). SetInternalDelay([]float64{.15},B2=.2,C2=1,D12=0,D21=0,D22=0). DiscretizeWithOpts(.1,C2DOptions{Method:C2DMethodTustin,ThiranOrder:3}) always returns ErrFeedbackDelay: Thiran filters for internal feedback delays are unsupported. Tau=.24/.35 also rejected; ThiranOrder0 succeeds by rounding.

## Files and independent evidence
conversion_delay.go discretizeInternalModel unconditionally rejects Tustin+positiveThiranOrder for any internal delay. MATLAB explicitly applies the same Thiran treatment to input, output, AND internal delays: https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ug/continuous-discrete-conversion-methods.html (Tustin Approximation for Systems with Time Delays), https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/c2doptions.html . DelayModeling delay represents filter memory as internal unit delays; state mode adds filter states.

## Proposed focused implementation
Discretize existing augmented rational model using canonical Tustin/prewarp. Build per-internal-channel bounded Thiran filter with exact integer remainder. Close model around filter bank using existing lower LFT, converting filter states to unit internal delays for delay mode and retaining states for state mode. Preserve external delays and source names. Do not modify canonical Tustin coordinates or negative-pole reverse helper. Requires conversion Thiran maximum-order repair first.

## Done when
- Positive ThiranOrder supports scalar/multiple internal feedback delays, mixed integer/fractional channels, zero integer remainder, non-symmetric MIMO; guard singular resulting instantaneous loop.
- Delay/state representations agree with independent lower-LFT transfer formula H11+H12*Delta*(I-H22*Delta)^-1*H21 on separate frequencies. Use published Thiran coefficients, prewarp response matching for rational part, analytic DC gain, source immutability.
- Approximation and initial-history limitations stay explicit; no unsupported state-map claim. Benchmark against rounded internal-delay path and no-delay path; preserve no-delay performance.

data.title: Remove phantom states from Append of zero-state internal-delay models
data.body:
## Reproduction and evidence
Append two zero-state unit-gain SISO models with LFT delay memory (e.g. conversionStateAsDelay(Thiran filter) provides a zero-state model). Expected n=0 since rational blocks have no states; observed n=1. connect.go Append internal-delay branch allocates A,B,C with max(n,1) but never resizes or clears them before returning. Dims uses A rows and sees a phantom state. Repeated Append causes extra zero poles and state-order mismatch. Independent MIMO Thiran conversion fixture expected original n2 in DelayModeling delay but obtained n5 from three bank assemblies. Fractional response may remain equal because the extra state is unobservable; state mappings, order/parity and performance are wrong.

## Scope and files
connect.go Append (~line559) internal-delay branch; persistent zero-state interconnection test needed. Use valid nonempty LFT matrices with B2/C2 zero rows/columns and positive Tau, n=0, and append against zero-state gain plus another delayed zero-state model. Preserve delay transfer matrix/names and source immutability.

## Done when
No fabricated rational states for zero-state delayed Append; correct zero-dimensional B2/C2, non-symmetric multichannel response independent of direct product/blockdiag and correct state count. Benchmark allocations/latency before/after; no unrelated interconnection changes.

Found during assigned Thiran conversion work. Not repaired there; conversion bank assembly avoids the defective Append branch.

## Done when
Approximate each residual fractional path by bounded Thiran filter with exact integer remainder, preserve common input/output delay metadata and supported internal feedback composition. Validate independent per-channel transfer response, names, delay/state modes and source immutability. Preserve no-delay fast path; benchmark representative MIMO path counts/orders. Do not silently round nondecomposable paths or claim lossless approximation.

Existing external/internal Thiran fixes DTAQWL/LUV3WY handle decomposable input/output delays and internal feedback delay channels; this broader path lifting is separate.

data.title: Accept stable short delays in explicit-order ThiranDelay
data.body:
## Reproduction
ThiranDelay(.24,3,.1) rejects D2.4 as unstable because thiran.go requires D>=N-.5. A third-order Thiran filter is stable for D>N-1, and MATLAB publishes stable thiran(2.4,1) denominator [1,.5294,-.04813,.004159]. ThiranDelay(.02,1,.1) also rejects despite exact stable first-order coefficient (1-.2)/(1+.2)=2/3 (pole -2/3). Explicit fixed filter order is distinct from conversion maximum-order policy.

## Evidence/files
thiran.go ThiranDelay minimum-delay guard and docstring; thiran_test.go existing too-small tests. Independent primary formula/fixture https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/thiran.html and cited Laakso/Valimaki Splitting the Unit Delay. Current C2D fixes use a conversion-only bounded-order helper and therefore avoid this standalone defect; public helper intentionally not changed concurrently.

## Done when
Correct explicit-order stability boundary with integer-degenerate filter cases treated consistently; stable D2.4/N3 and D.2/N1 accepted, below-boundary cases rejected; published coefficient/allpass/pole and near-boundary tests. State dimension/input argument semantics explicit; measure representative latency/allocations. Do not mix MATLAB automatic/max-order conversion policy into the explicit-order API.

data.title: Reduce Thiran bank composition overhead in C2D
data.body:
## Evidence
Tustin+Thiran external delay (bench_test.go BenchmarkDiscretizeWithOpts_Thiran) 2.52us->4.09us, 3.46KiB->8.19KiB, 74->160 allocs vs main 1bb229f after MATLAB split/LFT delay modeling (DTAQWL). data.title: Feedback/Connect/BlkDiag delay semantics
data.body:
Probes: a4 (TestProbeFeedback*, TestProbeConnect*, TestProbeBlkDiag*, TestProbeZeroStateLFT, TestProbeSetDelayModelZeroState, TestProbeLoopsens*), a1 TestProbe*ZeroDelayApprox*.
- Feedback (feedback_lft.go:6-9,:317) hoists plant InputDelay outside loop; must be inside (internal delay). TestFeedback_LFT_InputDelay / TestFeedbackKeepsInputDelay (connect_test.go:1709,:1866) assert wrong semantics — rewrite with response oracle.
- Connect (connect.go:1372,:1527) hoists Input/OutputDelay of externally selected channels even when Q loops through them.

data.title: Place wrong poles with complex open-loop pair
data.body:
Probes: a3 TestProbePlace, TestProbePlaceRepeatedMinimal, TestProbeExtra.
controller.go:277-311,:379: natural 2x2 Schur block assigned from one pool entry; real target placed twice, other skipped (nDone+=2). Place([[0,1],[-1,0]],[0;1],{-1,-2}) → {-1,-1}; some MIMO cases unstable, no error. Assert eig(A-BK) == requested for real/complex/repeated, SISO/MIMO, non-symmetric A.

data.title: Estimator/LQG option and descriptor handling
data.body:
Probes: a3 TestProbeLqgOptsLeak, TestProbeKalmdOpts; a1/a2 Estim/Reg probes.
- Lqg (lqg.go:26-36) passes regulator opts.S into Kalman Riccati; shared opts.Workspace overwrites kRes.K/X.

data.title: Descriptor/LFT/delay field loss in structural ops
data.body:
Probes: a1 (Select*, Reduce*, SS2SS, Xperm*, TransferFunction*, TFStateSpace*, ZPK*), a4 TestProbeStructural, TestProbeSelect, a2 Isproper, a5 SelectByIndex empty.
- SelectByIndex/SelectByName (names.go:246-321) drop IODelay and LFT; n==0 branch drops all delays; empty selection / SelectByName(nil,nil) panics (names.go:282).
- Reduce/MinimalRealization (minimal.go, realization_policy.go:34 result keeps only Delay): drop Input/OutputDelay and LFT; staircase ignores B2/C2. Reject or handle augmented model; make policy helper keep or refuse fields.
- SS2SS/StateTransform/Xperm (transform.go:41-53): transform LFT.B2→T·B2, C2→C2·T⁻¹; Xperm permutes StateName.
- System.TransferFunction (transfer.go:238) drops Input/OutputDelay (fold via TotalDelay) and LFT (error). TF.StateSpace static path drops tf.Delay. ZPKModel/TF.ZPK silently drop delays → error.
- Isproper (transfer.go:692) always true for descriptors.

data.title: Descriptor/stability correctness in analysis
data.body:
Probes: a2 (Zeros, Stabsep/Modsep), a1 Stabsep/Modsep/SingularPerturbation, a5 IsStable/H2Norm/Covar, a3/a5/a6 Covar, a4 TestProbeNorms.
- MIMO Zeros/ZerosDetail/Pzmap (zeros.go:50-81) ignore E; use pencil.
- Stabsep/Modsep (eigdecomp.go:15-28) split on eig(A) not (A,E); results drop E.
- IsStable (ss.go:124) and Stabsep (stabsep.go:10) use tol=0; on-axis eigenvalues from non-normal A count stable. Use one relative tolerance shared with IsStabilizable.
- H2Norm (norms.go:32) ignores internal delays (continuous with D12ΔD21≠0 → Inf; discrete wrong); static gain with D=0 returns +Inf.
- Covar continuous D≠0 must be Inf/error (fix covar test that asserts 0.75); Covar static gain panics (no n==0 path).
- Discrete SingularPerturbation (balance.go ~390-450) uses A22⁻¹; needs (I−A22)⁻¹ (Modred/Balred). Balred order==n should be no-op.
Do NOT touch HinfNorm accuracy (GH3MO7/TI6YYN).

data.title: Time responses, DCGain and Damp
data.body:
Probes: a6 (Impulse, GenSig, StepDiscreteFinalSample, StepInfo*), a3 (StepInfo, StepAutoHorizon*, MiscAnalysis), a2 DCGain, a4 (LFTDC, BandwidthLFT, PidtuneDelay, Initial*, StepLongDelay), a5 2b/2f/4c.
- DCGain (response.go:362-419): discrete uses I−A not E−A; singular-A fallback ignores E; ignores internal delays (n==0 returns D). Bandwidth/Pidtune fallback depend on it.
- Continuous Impulse (response.go:291) uses dt-wide pulse; y(0) must be C·B, no half-sample shift.
- Sample counts int(x/dt)+1 drop final sample (gensig.go:16, response.go:132,:160); continuous auto-dt derived from auto tFinal not user's.
- Auto horizon tFinal=7/minWn ignores damping and delays; z=0 pole gives tFinal=0; no cap on steps (stiff → 1e11). Step(+Inf) panics, Step(NaN) silent.
- GenSig square wave rounding (gensig.go:35).
- StepInfo: Settled always true without SteadyStateValue; PeakTime picks last sample of flat peak (response_info.go:156 >=); validate options (limits order/range, NaN thresholds).
- Damp discrete z=0 → ζ=1, τ=0 (response.go ~643).
- Discrete Simulate with x0 and OutputDelay doesn't delay free response (simulate.go:236-252); continuous Initial with fractional OutputDelay extrapolates x0; non-decomposable IODelay x0 dim error.

data.title: Identification and legacy Pidtune
data.body:
Probes: a6 (ERAEvenLength, FitProcessSteadyStateStartWithDelay + controls, IOStateSpaceDelayedExcerpt, PidtuneDiscretePhaseMargin), a3 TestProbePidtune.
- ERA (sysid.go:28,:44) even-length Markov sequence zeros last H1 block.
- FitProcess (process_identification.go:665) and IdentifyIOStateSpace (ss_identification.go:308-316) treat pre-record input as 0 when model has delay; need input history / estimate delay-line state.
- Legacy Pidtune (pidtune.go:123) uses continuous C(jω) for discrete plants; use discrete controller response.

data.title: Margin/AllMargin crossing and grid
data.body:
Probes: a3 TestProbeMargins, a4 TestProbeMargin, a5 (2a,2d,2e).
- phaseCrossings (margin.go:142,:243) treats 0° wrap as −180° crossing (unstable 10/(s+1)^5 reports GM +31 dB).
- PM not wrapped for large delays (margin.go:233).
- Grid ignores delays (misses crossover at 32 rad/s for τ=0.05), absolute [1e-4,1e4] clamp breaks time-scaled loops, z=0 pole → NaN grid, misses crossover exactly at Nyquist.
Fix margin grid inside margin.go; do NOT edit frequency*.go (sweep agent). Bode/Sigma/Nichols auto-grid issues (z=0 NaN, no Nyquist cap) are a separate deferred task.

data.title: Kalman/Kalmd/Lqr-policy silently ignore plant delays
data.body:
Repro: sys with SetInputDelay/SetOutputDelay/SetDelay/SetInternalDelay; Kalman(sys, Qn, Rn, nil) and Kalmd(...) return the delay-free gain without error or note.
Files: observer.go (Kalman, Kalmd), controller_observer_policy.go (newControllerObserverPolicy).
Evidence: newControllerObserverPolicy only checks n>0 and descriptor E; no HasDelay check. Lqg now rejects delays (PR for 3E6U66), Estim propagates InputDelay, Reg rejects; Kalman/Kalmd are left inconsistent.
Decision needed: reject delays (ErrDelayUnsupported) or document that gain is for delay-free part (MATLAB-like). Related design call: 5MNS63.

data.title: FixedInputReduction corrupts internal-delay (LFT) models
data.body:
Repro: a4 probe TestProbeMisc (scratchpad a4/zz_probe_test.go:1920). sys = pLFT (2x2, one internal delay, D12 2x1, D21 1x2); r, _ := sys.FixedInputReduction(map[int]float64{1: 0}, ""); r.FreqResponse(...) fails "FreqResponse: D12 2×2 != 2×1: dimension mismatch" for dt=0 and dt=0.1.
File: state_space_utils.go:84 (FixedInputReduction). Result LFT blocks are inconsistent with the reduced model dims (likely D12/D21 not resliced, or offset column handling wrong for LFT).
Expected: result equals selecting the free input columns of the original response (oracle frOracle sub-matrix), incl. D21 column removal; or reject LFT models clearly.
Found while fixing D5UZFJ; out of scope there.

data.title: FRDMargin: -180 crossings only at literal -180, PM unwrapped
data.body:
FRDMargin (frd.go:511-595) detects phase crossovers via (ph0+180)*(ph1+180)<=0 on the unwrapped Bode phase, so crossings of -540, -900... (e.g. FRD of 10/(s+1)^5 with delay, or any loop whose phase passes -540) are missed, and PM = 180+phAtCross is not wrapped to (-180,180] (large delays give PM like -337 deg). Interpolation is linear in w rather than log w.
Fix to match AllMargin (margin.go after WGI5MI): wrapped offset sign change with |a-b|<180, PM wrapped.
Repro: build FRD from a System with InputDelay=30, A=-1,B=1,C=2 on a dense grid [1e-2,5]; compare FRDMargin vs Margin(sys) (PM 22.82 deg @1.732).
Files: frd.go FRDMargin, frd_test.go.

data.title: Zeros/Stabsep/Modsep for singular-E descriptors
data.body:
Repro: E singular, e.g. E=[1 2 0;0 1 1;1 3 1], A=[-1 2 .5;-.5 -3 1;.3 .7 -2], B=[1 0;0 1;1 -1], C=[1 .5 0;0 1 -1], D=0 (probe a2 TestProbeSingularE).
After X36GIN, Zeros/ZerosDetail/Pzmap, Stabsep and Modsep return ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular for singular E (previously silently wrong). Nonsingular E works via ToExplicit.
Work: Zeros needs a generalized system-pencil staircase (SLICOT AG08BD) or a Mobius-shift reduction to explicit; Stabsep/Modsep need ordered generalized Schur (Dtgsen) + generalized Sylvester (Dtgsyl) with infinite modes kept as the polynomial/improper part.
Files: zeros.go, eigdecomp.go.

data.title: IsStable/HinfNorm ignore internal delays when judging stability
data.body:
Repro: probe a4 TestProbeNorms dt=0.1 lft: pTwoByTwo discrete + SetInternalDelay(tau=3, B2=[1;.5], C2=[.3 1], D12=[.2;0], D21=[0 .1], D22=.1). absorbInternalDelay(sys).Poles() has 1.12 (unstable; impulse response grows to 1e196) but sys.IsStable()=true (checks A only) and HinfNorm returns finite 12.28.
IsStable (ss.go), energy policy requireStable, HinfNorm, HSV, Gram, Balreal ignore LFT internal delays when judging stability. Discrete: absorb internal delays exactly before pole test. Continuous: needs delay-system stability (or reject).
X36GIN fixed H2Norm/Covar only (discrete absorbed; continuous rejected/Inf).

data.title: freqresp TF fallback double-counts Input/OutputDelay after TransferFunction folds total delay
data.body:
Depends on branch fix/audit-field-loss (YAJGKZ). That PR makes System.TransferFunction fold ALL external delays (Delay + InputDelay + OutputDelay, via TotalDelay) into TransferFunc.Delay and reject internal (LFT) delays with ErrDelayNotRepresentable.

frequency.go frequencyEvaluator.sweepInto fallback (around line 268-280 on fd179f1):
    res, err := e.sys.TransferFunction(nil)
    tf = res.TF
    delayTF = effectiveIODelayMatrix(e.sys, e.p, e.m, false)   // Input/Output only
    tf.evalInto(s, dst)                                         // now already applies total delay
    applyIODelayMatrixAtS(..., delayTF)                         // -> Input/OutputDelay applied twice

Fix: after YAJGKZ merges, drop delayTF (TF already carries the total delay), or call the new internal sys.rationalTransferFunction(nil) and apply delaySS (total) instead. The fallback only runs when the pointwise solver fails at a frequency, so it is rarely hit; no current test covers it. LFT systems reaching the fallback now get an error instead of a silently delay-free TF.

Not fixed in YAJGKZ because frequency.go / the FreqResponse sweep is owned by another agent (6FISAR, fix/hessenberg-sweep-accuracy). Merge-order dependency: whichever of the two PRs merges second must reconcile this.

data.title: Covar ignores external delays (cross-covariance wrong)
data.body: Covar (covar.go) ignores InputDelay/OutputDelay/Delay (IODelay). Output covariance of stationary process: Cov(y_i[k-d_i], y_j[k-d_j]) = R_ij(d_j-d_i) != R_ij(0) when output delays differ; per-channel input delays likewise change cross terms of correlated W. Diagonal unaffected. Repro: discrete 2-output model, OutputDelay=[0,3], compare Covar to impulse-sum oracle with delayed responses. Fix: absorb external delays (discrete exact; continuous reject or Pade) before Lyapunov, or reject. Found while fixing X36GIN.

data.title: Continuous Impulse with internal delays fed by u (LFT D21≠0) uses 1/dt pulse
data.body:
Found while fixing BNHWGV (branch fix/audit-time-response).

Impulse on continuous models now samples C·e^{At}·B exactly via the step response of (A, A·B, C, C·B) (response.go impulseAsStepModel). That rewrite is skipped when LFT.D21 ≠ 0 (u feeds a delay line directly: a Dirac enters the delay, re-emerges at τ as a state jump B2·D21 and a Dirac in y/z), and when a descriptor has singular E. Those fall back to the old ZOH pulse of height 1/dt, which puts D/dt into y(0) and is O(dt) wrong.

Repro: trMIMO(t,0) (response_test.go) with SetInternalDelay([0.5013], B2=0, C2=[0.3 1], D12=[0.7;-0.4], D21=[1 0], D22=0); Impulse(sys,2).Y(0,0) = 13.7 (=0.2/dt), want C·B(0,0)=1 (MATLAB drops the Dirac D part).

Fix idea: represent the delayed Dirac train analytically (state jumps B2·(D22^k)·D21 at k·τ) or extend the derived model with an impulse-into-delay-line channel. Files: response.go (Impulse, impulseAsStepModel), simulate.go.

data.title: Continuous free response with fractional internal delays is approximate (Initial/Lsim x0)
data.body:
Found while fixing BNHWGV (branch fix/audit-time-response).

BNHWGV made continuous Initial/Lsim free responses exact for models without internal delays (closed-form C·e^{A(t−τo)}·x0, output delays shifted exactly; input/IO delays ignored for the free part). Models with internal delays (LFT) still go through DiscretizeZOH, whose fractional-delay handling holds/interpolates w and is O(dt) inaccurate for the free response.

Repro (worst error 9.3e-3 at dt=0.0146): trMIMO(t,0) with SetInternalDelay([0.5013], B2=0, C2=[0.3 1], D12=[0.7;-0.4], D21=0, D22=0); x0=[1,-0.5]; Initial(sys,x0,2). Oracle: y = C e^{At}x0 + D12 C2 e^{A(t−τ)}x0 for t≥τ.
Same mechanism makes continuous step/lsim responses of LFT models with τ not a multiple of dt approximate.

Files: response.go (Initial, Lsim), conversion code for continuous LFT ZOH discretization.

data.title: ZeroDelayApprox drops descriptor E
data.body:
Found while fixing BNHWGV. delay.go ZeroDelayApprox builds the Δ=I closure with newNoCopy(Aa,Ba,Ca,Da,Dt) and never copies sys.E, so a descriptor model with internal delays returns an explicit model with the wrong dynamics (A treated as E⁻¹A). DCGain's new singular fallback avoids it by calling ToExplicit before ZeroDelayApprox, but other callers (FreqResponse comparisons, Pidtune/Bandwidth fallbacks, tests) are exposed.
Repro: NewDescriptor(A,B,C,D,E≠I,0) + SetInternalDelay(...); compare ZeroDelayApprox(sys).EvalFr(s) with EvalFr of the delay-free descriptor closure C(sE−A−B2·(I−D22)⁻¹C2)⁻¹... at a few s.
Fix: copy E (result.E = copyDescriptorE(sys.E)) and add a test. File: delay.go:2005.

data.title: Zeros of internal-delay (LFT) models: define semantics
data.body:
System.Zeros/ZerosDetail ignore LFT internal delays (B2/C2/D12/D21/D22) in both the SISO (zeros.go sisoZeros, via TransferFunction of the delay-free part) and MIMO (zeros.go mimoZeros, Rosenbrock/staircase on A,B,C,D only) paths. The result is the zeros of the delay-free (u->y) block, not of the delayed system, with no error or documentation.

Found while fixing YAJGKZ (fix/audit-field-loss): System.TransferFunction now rejects internal delays with ErrDelayNotRepresentable; sisoZeros was explicitly kept on the delay-free part (LFT stripped) to stay consistent with mimoZeros. Decide: reject with ErrDelayNotRepresentable, or document "zeros of the delay-free part" (MATLAB-like?), and apply consistently to SISO + MIMO. Repro: fieldLFT fixture in realization_policy_test.go; sys.Zeros() succeeds and ignores the LFT channels. Also note mimoZeros ignores descriptor E (may be covered by fix/audit-analysis-descriptor).

data.title: Dedupe FRDMargin and Margin crossing helpers (after #193, #199)
data.body: After PlantControl/controlsys#193 and #199 merge: frd.go helpers frdWrapDeg/frdCrosses/frdCrossFrac/frdInterpOmega duplicate margin.go phase-wrap/crossing helpers from #193. Merge into one owner so FRDMargin and Margin share crossing semantics. Tests: TestFRDMargin_WrappedCrossings, TestAllMargin_CrossoverContract must stay green.

data.title: Poles/Zeros of internal-delay models ignore LFT delay loop
data.body:
Poles() (ss.go) returns eig(A) for models with LFT internal delays, ignoring B2/C2/D22. MATLAB pole: continuous internal delays -> poles of zero-delay approximation (set tau=0; error on singular algebraic loop); discrete delays are finite-dimensional (absorbed z^-k shift states).
Repro: discreteLFTDelayFixture(t, []float64{1, 0.5}) in ss_test.go (branch fix/audit-delay-stability): lft.Poles() spectral radius <1 while hand-absorbed A has pole ~1.12.
IsStable/HinfNorm/HSV were fixed in SZVDCQ by absorbing on a local copy; Poles/Zero/Damp themselves unchanged (pole count would change for discrete). Decide MATLAB-consistent semantics and update Poles/Zero/Damp/Dcgain consumers.
Files: ss.go Poles, zeros, damp.

data.title: DiskMargin/pidtune: support continuous delayed loops via exact frequency stability
data.body:
After SZVDCQ, DiskMargin on a continuous loop with delays (sensitivity has internal delay) returns ErrContinuousInternalDelay (previously returned a wrong Ms computed from A only, ignoring the delay loop). MATLAB diskmargin supports delayed loops. Needs a delay-aware closed-loop stability test (Nyquist encirclement on exact frequency response, or DDE spectral method) plus H-inf peak from the exact frequency response.
Also pidtune (pid_tuning.go TunePID) uses "sampled-frequency-only" stability for any delayed plant; discrete delayed plants could now use closed-loop IsStable exactly (internal delays absorbed).
Repro: margin_test.go TestDiskMargin_LFTSystem (L=10/(s+1) e^{-0.01s}, true alpha>0).
Files: margin.go DiskMargin, pid_tuning.go TunePID.

data.title: Norm(sys,Inf) errors on unstable models; MATLAB norm returns L-inf peak
data.body: MATLAB norm(sys,Inf) doc (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.norm.html): "For all systems, norm returns the L-inf norm, which is the peak gain without regard to system stability." Here Norm(sys, Inf) (norms.go) maps to HinfNorm, which returns ErrUnstable for unstable models. Decide whether Norm(Inf) should return the L-inf peak (no imaginary-axis poles) while HinfNorm keeps the stability gate. Pre-existing; noticed while fixing SZVDCQ.

data.title: Lqg noise model differs from MATLAB lqg (G=B,H=D vs G=I,H=0)
data.body:
Lqg (lqg.go) designs its estimator via Kalman with noise entering the plant inputs (G = B, H = D; Qn m x m). MATLAB lqg(sys,QXU,QWV) uses x' = Ax + Bu + w, y = Cx + Du + v (G = I, H = 0; QWV is (n+p)x(n+p)). After PR for 5MNS63, Kalman honours H = D, so Lqg on plants with D != 0 now differs from both the old behaviour and MATLAB lqg.
Decide: keep the library noise model (document mapping in Lqg doc) or switch Lqg to MATLAB (G = I, H = 0) semantics.
Files: lqg.go, controller_observer_policy.go (estimator), lqg_test.go.
Evidence: https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/ss.lqg.html model section.

data.title: System.Isproper always true; wrong for improper descriptors
data.body:
transfer.go:692 `func (sys *System) Isproper() bool { return true }` ignores descriptor E.
Repro (probe a2 TestProbeSingularE): E=[0 1;0 0], A=I, B=[0;1], C=[1 0], D=0, dt=0 -> G(s)=-s (EvalFr(2i)=-2i), yet Isproper()==true.
MATLAB isproper: false when the descriptor model has a polynomial (improper) part; isproper(sys,'elem')/[isp,sysr]=isproper(sys) can also reduce to an explicit model.
Fix: for singular E, decide properness via the index/infinite structure (e.g. infinite eigenvalues of (A,E) that are controllable+observable with nilpotent index >1 => improper; staircase/SVD compression: E=diag(Σ,0) then A22 invertible => proper). Test with improper and singular-but-proper (index-1) descriptors, both dt.
Files: transfer.go.

data.title: SISO Zeros drop cancelled invariant zeros (MIMO/singular-E keep them)
data.body:
zeros.go: explicit and invertible-E SISO models use sisoZeros = roots of the minimal TF numerator (locked by architecture_deepening_test.go TestArchitectureZerosUsePolynomialRootSemantics, #88), while MIMO and singular-E SISO models (descriptorZeros, fix/audit-singular-e) return invariant zeros of the system pencil, which include zeros cancelled by poles.
MATLAB tzero doc: returns invariant zeros; "If sys is a minimal realization, the invariant zeros coincide with the transmission zeros" (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.tzero.html).
Repro: New(A=[-1 1;0 -2], B=[0;1], C=[1 1], D=0) -> Zeros() = [] (TF cancels (s+2)); routing the same system through mimoZeros/staircase gives [-2] (rank drop of [A-sI B; C D] at s=-2).
Decide: route SISO through the pencil (matches tzero; update the #88 architecture test) or document SISO = transmission zeros consistently (then singular-E SISO should also drop decoupling zeros).
Files: zeros.go, architecture_deepening_test.go.

data.title: Time responses of proper singular-E descriptor models (Step/Impulse/Initial/Lsim)
data.body:
Continuous Step/Impulse/Initial/Lsim on a descriptor model with singular E error with ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular (conversionStandardForm/ToExplicit reject singular E). MATLAB simulates proper singular-E dss models (index reduction to an explicit model plus feedthrough; improper models error with "Cannot simulate the time response of improper models").
Repro: trMIMO(t,0) (response_test.go) with E=[1 0;0 0]; Step(sys,2) -> error.
Pinned by TestTimeResponseSingularDescriptorErrors (fix/audit-impulse-lft); update that test when implementing.
Files: response.go, state_space_utils.go (ToExplicit), descriptor.go (conversionStandardForm).
Found while fixing KVSADK.

data.title: Ssbal balancing loop uses unscaled norms
data.body:
Noticed while fixing sweep balancing (branch fix/hessenberg-sweep-accuracy). ssbal.go Ssbal computes rowNorm += |a_ij|*d[j] and colNorm += |a_ji|*d[j] against the ORIGINAL A each iteration, with B rows/C cols unscaled, so the norms do not reflect the current D^-1 A D, B, C; convergence/result differs from SLICOT TB01ID. A correct Osborne loop on [A B; C] now exists as balancedRealization.balance in frequency_hessenberg.go (plantcontrol.org/v1/controlsys) and could back Ssbal. Add a test comparing row/col norms of the result for a badly scaled model.

data.title: descriptor FreqResponse not balanced/refined
data.body:
After fix/hessenberg-sweep-accuracy (controlsys 9f36142), explicit models use balanced dense GEPP / refined Hessenberg, but descriptor (E != nil) sweeps still go through evalFrSSInto + cSolveInPlace: no state balancing, cmplx.Abs pivoting. Before balancing, explicit models with diagonally badly scaled realizations had pointwise errors O(1)-1e3 vs a well-scaled twin (randomSweepModel kinds scaled/cascade in frequency_sweep_property_test.go, e.g. seed=234 cascade); the same failure should reproduce on a descriptor twin (E = I scaled the same way). data.title: audit error-free transforms for Go FMA fusion
data.body:
Go may fuse a*b+c into FMA across statements (spec permits; arm64 does). In fix/hessenberg-sweep-accuracy a Dot2 TwoProduct (p := a*b; err := FMA(a,b,-p); TwoSum(s,p)) silently broke until written p := float64(a*b). data.title: Simulate/Step/Impulse reject discrete descriptor models (incl. internal delays)
data.body:
Found while doing HY7U5M (branch fix/freqresp-descriptor). Simulate calls newDescriptorPolicy(sys).requireStandard("Simulate") so every discrete descriptor (E != I) model, with or without internal delays, errors ErrDescriptorUnsupported; Step/Impulse/Lsim on discrete descriptors inherit that. Continuous descriptors work in Step/Impulse only when E invertible (auto-discretize goes through ToExplicit); singular E errors ErrDescriptorSingular.
Repro: absorbScopePlant(t, 1, true, true).Simulate(u, nil, nil) -> "Simulate: operation does not support descriptor systems".
Scope: (a) invertible E: ToExplicit (already handles LFT B2) then simulate - small; (b) singular E: needs DAE handling (Weierstrass/Kronecker split into slow + algebraic/impulsive parts, causality check) - large.
