data.title: TransferFunction loses accuracy on badly scaled / high-order models (no balancing)
data.body:
Found in ELN5IG root cause. rowRealizationConverter (transfer.go) runs staircase + per-row Hessenberg on raw A without diagonal balancing. On the 18-state Pade cascade (absorbScopePlant(t,0,false,false) + absorbScopeCases[0].apply(scale 0.125) + replaceContinuousDelays(sys,5)) den rows that must be identical differ 1.7e-6 relative and TF eval errs 5e-7; pre-balancing A,B,C with Dgebal(lapack.Scale) (exact power-of-2 similarity) drops this to 9.5e-14. On stiff chains (diag -lo*(hi/lo)^(i/(n-1)), superdiag 0.3*(i%3+1), n=20, 1e-3..1e3) TF eval error is 0.36 raw, 5e-5 balanced; n=30 is O(1) either way (polynomial form inherently ill-conditioned).
FreqResponse no longer uses the TF sweep (Hessenberg now), but TransferFunction/DCGain-limit/Margin users of TF still see it. Suggest: balance in convert(); document conditioning limits; test with stiffChain helper in frequency_hessenberg_test.go.

(Moved from process-lab ergo 6PQZLN.)

data.title: Prescale misapplies Dgebal PermuteScale output
data.body:
prescale.go calls impl.Dgebal(lapack.PermuteScale, ...) on A but treats scale[] as a pure diagonal scaling for B and C. With PermuteScale, scale[j] holds permutation indices for j outside [ilo,ihi] and A is permuted, but B/C are neither permuted nor correctly scaled.
Repro: A=[[-1,100,0.001],[0,-2,1000],[0,0,-3]], B=[1;2;3], C=[1 1 1], D=0; Prescale(sys) gives StateScale [1 1 2] (the 2 is a permutation index) and EvalFr(1i) of result 172.2-15211.2i vs original 322.2-30361.2i with in/out scales 0.5/0.5 (not a consistent rescaling).
Fix: use lapack.Scale, or apply permutations to B rows / C cols; add a test that Prescale result == diag(outScale)^-1... G diag(inScale) relation on a triangular A.

(Moved from process-lab ergo SALCRR.)

data.title: SS2SS/Xperm ignore LFT B2/C2 (internal-delay models)
data.body:
transform.go SS2SS: transforms A,B,C via sys.Copy() but leaves LFT.B2 (n×N) and LFT.C2 (N×n) untransformed; only requireStandard, no delay check. Xperm calls SS2SS so it inherits the bug. Response changes for any model with internal delays.
Repro: A=[[-1,2],[0,-3]], B=[1;1], C=[1 0], D=0, LFT{Tau:[0.5], B2=[1;0], C2=[0 1], D12=D21=D22=0}; T=[[2,1],[0,1]].
EvalFr(1i): orig 0.69187-1.12346i, SS2SS result 0.69594-1.01173i.
Fix: B2 -> T*B2, C2 -> C2*T^-1 (also E -> T*E*T^-1 if descriptor ever allowed). Test vs independent LFT FR oracle (scratchpad a4 frOracle).

data.title: 2x2 Schur block eigenvalues lose imag part (discriminant cancellation)
data.body:
schurEigenvaluesRaw (eigdecomp.go:265) and schurBlock2x2Eig (controller.go:539) compute disc = tr*tr - 4*(a*d - b*c). For standardized Schur blocks (a==d from Dgees/Dtrexc) with |a| >> sqrt(|bc|) this cancels catastrophically, fused (arm64 FMA) or not.

Repro (package-internal test): t := []float64{1e8, 1, -1, 1e8}; schurEigenvaluesRaw(t,2) -> [1e8+0i 1e8+0i], schurBlock2x2Eig(t,2,0) -> 1e8+0i. Correct: 1e8 +/- 1i.

Callers: canon.go:242, modal_reduction.go:56,143, eigdecomp.go:155,187 (decomposeBySchur), controller.go:304,376 (pole placement 2x2 assignment).

Fix: use gonumLapack.Implementation{}.Dlanv2(a,b,c,d) (handles scaling, already imported in transfer.go), or p:=(a-d)/2; disc:=p*p+b*c with scaling. Test vs closed form, e.g. a=d=1e8,b=1,c=-1 and non-standardized blocks.
Found during 2RT2NP FMA audit.

data.title: FreqResponse/EvalFr performance regression in v1.13.x (up to +63% vs v1.13.0)
data.body:
## Problem
v1.13.1 (PR #204, fix/hessenberg-sweep-accuracy) made frequency responses accurate but slower than v1.13.0 (go1.27.1, M1 Pro, benchstat n=8, ±18–27% noise from concurrent agents):

| Benchmark | vs v1.13.0 |
|---|---|
| FreqResponse | +63% |
| B747Lateral | +56% |
| EvalFr_N4 | +53% |
| Bode_LargeMIMO | +35% |
| Sigma_SISO | +33% |
| ModelArrayFreqResponse | +29% |
| FreqResponseWithDelay | +25% |
| Bode | +24% |
| Nyquist | +21% |
| Sigma_MIMO | +7% |
| Margin_SISO | +4% |
| ShortSweep | ~ |

v1.13.0 itself (PR #189) was already +32–40% on B747Lateral, Sigma_SISO, Bode_LargeMIMO and +20% ModelArrayFreqResponse vs v1.12.2 (other sweeps faster). Note v1.12.2/v1.13.0 speed came from inaccurate paths (polynomial TF sweep; unbalanced/unrefined Hessenberg), so the baseline for "fast" must stay accurate.

## Where the time goes (from the PR)
- Whole-system Osborne balancing of [A B; C] per call (balancedRealization.balance, frequency_hessenberg.go).
- Per-point dense GEPP on the balanced system when n ≤ 20·max(m,1) or ≤ 2 points; otherwise Hessenberg + one step of iterative refinement per frequency.
- EvalFr / FreqResponsePointwise now always balance + dense GEPP (+53% EvalFr_N4), plus Validate() at entry (+9 ns).

## Goal
Recover speed without losing accuracy: sweep vs pointwise and vs the refined oracle must stay ≤1e-12 normwise on testdata/sweep_accuracy_series_hinf.json and the randomized property test (frequency_sweep_property_test.go); no tolerance loosening.

## Ideas (measure each)
- Cache/skip balancing: detect already-balanced realizations cheaply; reuse balancing across a model-array / repeated calls on the same System; cheaper convergence criteria.
- EvalFr single point: skip balancing when scaling ratios are mild; avoid allocations (workspace pooling).
- Refinement only when a cheap residual/condition estimate says it's needed (per frequency), not always.
- Re-tune the dense/Hessenberg crossover on representative coupled models (benchDenseSys) incl. MIMO and delays; consider blocked Hessenberg solves across frequencies.
- Profile Bode_LargeMIMO and B747Lateral first (pprof), report allocations.

## Downstream
Process Lab (plantcontrol.org/private/process-lab) pins v1.13.1; model-design evidence (sigma/Bode/margins), PID tuning, analysis and H∞ design (HinfNorm verification, cf. process-lab ergo 2H6SLA) call these paths — measure page latency there too.

data.title: HinfNorm: return Inf/Inf for unstable models per MATLAB hinfnorm
data.body:
MATLAB hinfnorm (https://www.mathworks.com/help/robust/ref/dynamicsystem.hinfnorm.html): unstable sys -> ninf = Inf, fpeak = Inf (no error).
controlsys HinfNorm (norms.go) returns ErrUnstable instead (documented as deviation in PR for 6CNWCK).
Deferred because DiskMargin (margin.go ~L423) branches on errors.Is(err, ErrUnstable) and margin.go was being edited on a sibling branch (KFBUQL).
Fix: HinfNorm unstable -> (Inf, Inf, nil); update DiskMargin to key on IsInf(Ms); update tests norms_test.go TestHinfNorm_Unstable, TestNorms_UnstableNonMinPhase, TestHinfNorm_DiscreteInternalDelay.

data.title: AllMargin/Margin/Bandwidth crossings are grid-bounded, not analytic
data.body:
margin.go: AllMargin/Margin/Bandwidth (and pidtune findCrossoverFreq) detect crossings by sampling marginFreqs, which derives its range from pole natural frequencies only (autoBodeFreqs: 0.1x min .. 10x max, ignores zeros), then refine within a bracket. Crossovers outside the grid are silently missed; one exactly at the edge hinged on last-sample rounding.
Repro: K/(s(s+1)) with K = wc*hypot(wc,1), wc = 12 -> AllMargin reported no gain crossover (grid ends at 10). TestPidtune_PI_CustomCrossover (wc=10) only passed by rounding luck: exact 20log10|L(j10)| = +1.9e-15 dB, old TF gave -9.6e-16.
Mitigation in branch fix/audit-tf-balance (BLYSOP): marginFreqs pads the grid a decade each side (TestAllMargin_CrossoverAtGridEdge). Still grid-bounded: crossings > 100x max pole freq or between dense features are missed.
MATLAB allmargin computes crossings exactly (solve |L(jw)|=1 and phase=-180 analytically / via polynomial or Hamiltonian-like root finding). Do the same.

schurEigenvaluesRaw (eigdecomp.go:265) and schurBlock2x2Eig (controller.go:539) compute disc = tr*tr - 4*(a*d - b*c). For standardized Schur blocks (a==d from Dgees/Dtrexc) with |a| >> sqrt(|bc|) this cancels catastrophically, fused (arm64 FMA) or not.

Repro (package-internal test): t := []float64{1e8, 1, -1, 1e8}; schurEigenvaluesRaw(t,2) -> [1e8+0i 1e8+0i], schurBlock2x2Eig(t,2,0) -> 1e8+0i. Correct: 1e8 +/- 1i.

Callers: canon.go:242, modal_reduction.go:56,143, eigdecomp.go:155,187 (decomposeBySchur), controller.go:304,376 (pole placement 2x2 assignment).

Fix: use gonumLapack.Implementation{}.Dlanv2(a,b,c,d) (handles scaling, already imported in transfer.go), or p:=(a-d)/2; disc:=p*p+b*c with scaling. Test vs closed form, e.g. a=d=1e8,b=1,c=-1 and non-standardized blocks.
Found during 2RT2NP FMA audit.

Cross-ref: gonum ergo IVC3VO (Dlanv2 regression tests). gonum Dlanv2 verified correct on the failing case (1e8±1i).

data.title: C2D/DiscretizeZOH of proper singular-E descriptor via properExplicitForm
data.body:
conversionStandardForm (descriptor.go) -> ToExplicit rejects singular E, so DiscretizeZOH/C2D of a proper singular-E dss model errors ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular. MATLAB c2d accepts proper dss models (reduces algebraic part, see dss2ss doc).
Repro (branch fix/audit-descriptor-sim): desc, _ := index1Descriptor(t, 0, false) (descriptor_test.go); desc.DiscretizeZOH(0.1) -> error.
Fix: route conversionStandardForm through sys.properExplicitForm() (added in fix/audit-descriptor-sim) when E singular; document that state coordinates change (state names dropped). Time responses already bypass this by reducing at entry.
Files: descriptor.go conversionStandardForm, convert.go, conversion_matched.go.

data.title: DiskMargin uses skew sigma=1 (1/||S||inf), MATLAB default is sigma=0
data.body:
margin.go DiskMargin computes alpha = 1/||S||inf with GainMargin [1/(1+a), 1/(1-a)] and PM = 2 asin(a/2). That is the sigma=1 (sensitivity-based) disk.
MATLAB diskmargin (https://www.mathworks.com/help/robust/ref/dynamicsystem.diskmargin.html) defaults to balanced skew sigma=0: alpha_max = 1/||S + (sigma-1)/2||inf = 1/||S - 1/2||inf = 1/||(S-T)/2||inf, F = (1 + a(1-sigma)/2 d)/(1 - a(1+sigma)/2 d), GM = [(2-a)/(2+a), (2+a)/(2-a)].
Repro: L = 2/(s+1): ours alpha = 1/||S||inf, MATLAB alpha = 1/max|S-1/2|; values differ.
Decide: switch default to sigma=0 (behaviour change for all callers, update tests/docs) and/or add sigma option. Delayed path (KFBUQL, diskMarginDelayed + delayLoop.peakSensitivity in delay_nyquist.go) computes the same ||S||inf and must move with it.
Files: margin.go (DiskMargin, diskMarginFromPeak), delay_nyquist.go, margin_test.go.

data.title: internal-delay LFT freq response unbalanced (cInvertInto on raw sI-A/sE-A)
data.body: freqResponseLFT/evalFrLFTInto (frequency.go) for internal-delay models, explicit and descriptor, still forms the full resolvent (sI-A)^-1 / (sE-A)^-1 via cInvertInto with no state balancing and cmplx.Abs pivoting, unlike the delay-free path (balancedDense, PR on fix/audit-balance-descriptor, I3FTEJ). Expect the same spurious-singular / accuracy loss on diagonally badly scaled realizations (randomSweepModel kinds scaled/cascade in frequency_sweep_property_test.go) once an internal delay is added. Repro: take a scaled descriptor from randomSweepModel(rng, sweepBadlyScaled, 0, true) seed=14, add an internal delay (e.g. via Feedback with a delayed block), compare FreqResponse to the oracle on the twin. Fix idea: balance [|A|+|E| B1 B2; C1 C2] (balancedRealization.balance) before the LFT solve and solve rather than invert.

data.title: Ssbal: MATLAB parity for descriptor models and condT
data.body: MATLAB ssbal supports descriptor models (scales E like A by the same similarity, abcbalance on [|A|+|E| B; C 0]), a condT bound on cond(T), and a permutation from balance. controlsys Ssbal (ssbal.go) rejects descriptors (requireStandard) and has no condT or permutation. Decide whether to add descriptor + condT parity; balancedRealization.balance(t) in frequency_hessenberg.go already handles E. Sources: R14 toolbox/control/control/@ss/ssbal.m help, toolbox/shared/controllib/abcbalance.m.

data.title: HinfNorm: certify sampled peak with one Hamiltonian probe instead of 33-step bisection
data.body:
## Problem
HinfNorm (norms.go, v1.13.1) spends ~32 Hamiltonian Schur decompositions (4n×4n Dgees for a 2n closed loop) per call even when its 50-point sampled lower bound (hinfLowerBound) already equals the peak. gammaHigh starts at 2·gammaLow and only ever halves; every mid test returns "no imaginary eigenvalues", so it bisects log2(1/1e-10) ≈ 33 times. Process Lab H∞ design verification is 80–90% this one call.

## Evidence (Process Lab perf/hinfnorm-verify, go1.27.1, M1 Pro)
Process Lab BenchmarkHinfSyn (internal/studio/model_design_benchmark_test.go): randomHinfPlant(order,2,7), makeweight(100,0.5,0.5), W2=0.1, augw, HinfSyn, LFT → closed loop n=24/44/64 for order 10/20/30; verify/order=N = HinfNorm(closed).
Profile design/order=30: HinfNorm 70.6% of total (90% of design), hasImagEigs 69.8%, Dgees 78.6% (Dhseqr/Dlaqr5 + Dgehrd). Trace at order 10: lo=0.904007451407 fixed for all 34 iterations; hi halves 1.808 → 0.9040074515.

## Prototype (scratch only, not committed)
Probe gammaLow·(1+tol/2) once before the doubling loop; if no imaginary-axis eigenvalues, it is a certified upper bound within tol:
    tol := 1e-10
    gammaHigh := math.Max(gammaLow*2, 1e-10)
    if probe := gammaLow * (1 + tol/2); gammaLow > 0 && !ws.hasImagEigs(probe) {
        gammaHigh = probe
    }
(and the same probe after candidatePeak raises gammaLow — Boyd–Balakrishnan style). Norms identical to 10 significant digits; controlsys `go test -run 'Hinf|Norm|Sigma'` and Process Lab ./internal/studio tests pass with it.
benchstat n=10 interleaved (machine load ~140, so ±100% noise; allocs deterministic):
  verify/order=10  43.4ms → 4.05ms (-91%), allocs 2837 → 285
  verify/order=20  352ms  → 29.4ms (-92%), allocs 38885 → 2557
  verify/order=30  1163ms → 106ms  (-91%), allocs 69499 → 4222
  design/order=30  -76%, allocs 87.3k → 16.0k
Quiet-machine single run: HinfNorm order 30 333ms → 38ms (~32 → 3 Schur).

## Done when
HinfNorm certifies the upper bound via probe(s) near gammaLow (BB/Bruinsma–Steinbuch quadratic convergence) so a well-sampled peak takes O(1) Hamiltonian eigs; tolerance stays 1e-10 relative; add a test counting/benching Hamiltonian evaluations on a peak-at-sample case and keep MATLAB-validated norm tests green. Consider also a ws reuse for the requireStable/Poles eig.

data.title: Descriptor/I-O-delay parity: Prescale, SS2SS, Xperm, Ssbal
data.body:
MATLAB supports descriptor models in prescale, ss2ss (TAT⁻¹, TB, CT⁻¹, TET⁻¹) and xperm (permute E like A), and ssbal/xperm/ss2ss preserve I/O delays (InputDelay/OutputDelay/IODelay only touch a,b,c,e).

controlsys:
- Prescale (prescale.go), SS2SS, Xperm call requireStandard → ErrDescriptorUnsupported for any non-identity E (pinned in architecture_runtime_test.go TestRuntimeArchitectureTransformationsRejectDescriptorWorkflows).
- Ssbal (ssbal.go) and Prescale call requireDelayFree, so pure I/O delays are rejected although the diagonal state scaling commutes with them. realizationTransformPolicy.result copies Delay but not InputDelay/OutputDelay.

Repro: Prescale(NewDescriptor(A,B,C,D,E,0)) with E=diag(2,1) → ErrDescriptorUnsupported. Ssbal of sys with SetInputDelay([1]) → "does not support delayed systems".

data.title: D2C zoh/foh and C2D impulse reject internal delays (MATLAB d2c/c2d support them)
data.body:
Found while fixing F6G6QK (branch fix/audit-c2d-singular-e).

MATLAB d2c/d2d and c2d('impulse') accept ss models with internal delays (integer-sample delays map exactly to tau=k*Ts).

data.title: FreqResponse/DCGain at a pole: Inf for explicit models, ErrSingularTransform for internal-delay/descriptor
data.body:
## Problem
Evaluating exactly at a pole on the imaginary axis (or z=1 / unit circle) gives different contracts depending on realization (v1.13.1, also v1.12.2 for FreqResponse):

- Explicit SS 1/(s^2+1): FreqResponse([0.5,1,2]) -> H(j1) = +Inf+NaNi, err nil. ModelArray.FreqResponse same.
- Explicit integrator 1/s: DCGain -> +Inf, err nil; FreqResponse([0]) -> err nil (Inf).
- Same pole inside a model with internal delays (LFT): FreqResponse -> "controlsys: singular complex matrix: ... ErrSingularTransform".
- DCGain of an integrating model with internal delays: v1.12.2 returned +Inf, v1.13.x returns "DCGain: ... ErrSingularTransform" (new dcGainByEvaluation path). Bandwidth (margin.go) and TuningGoal tracking (tuning_goal.go) propagate that error; for explicit models Bandwidth treats Inf DC as "unbounded" (returns 0, nil).

Callers must special-case both Inf/NaN and ErrSingularTransform for the same mathematical situation.

## Repro
Process Lab flow: Source -> Sum(+-) -> Lag(1) -> exact Delay 0.3 -> back to Sum; Lag -> Transfer 1/(s^2+1). FreqResponse at omega=1 errors; remove the delay loop and it returns Inf.

## Ask
Pick one contract (Inf/NaN entries like MATLAB freqresp, or a typed error for both) and apply it across explicit, descriptor and LFT evaluation, DCGain and Bandwidth. Document it on FreqResponse/DCGain.

## Downstream
Process Lab maps ErrSingularTransform and non-finite sweep gains to a usage error (perf/controlsys-v113-impact branch, frequencyResponseError in internal/studio/analysis_frequency.go).

MATLAB supports descriptor models in prescale, ss2ss (TAT⁻¹, TB, CT⁻¹, TET⁻¹) and xperm (permute E like A), and ssbal/xperm/ss2ss preserve I/O delays (InputDelay/OutputDelay/IODelay only touch a,b,c,e).

Repro: Prescale(NewDescriptor(A,B,C,D,E,0)) with E=diag(2,1) → ErrDescriptorUnsupported. Ssbal of sys with SetInputDelay([1]) → "does not support delayed systems".
Found while fixing LXJA23 (Ssbal descriptor + condT).

Note (2026-10-04): the realizationTransformPolicy.result Input/OutputDelay part is already fixed in PlantControl/controlsys#195 (YAJGKZ). | ModelDesignEvidence order=10 2x2 | 1.24 ms | 1.59 ms | +28% |
| ModelDesignEvidence order=10 4x4 | 8.18 ms | 8.56 ms | +5% |
| Analysis frequency, SS order=30 4x4 (Bode/sigma) | 2.57 ms | 6.38 ms | +148% |
| Analysis frequency, SS order=10 2x2 | 0.40 ms | 0.59 ms | +47% |
| Analysis frequency, PID loop 3rd-order rational | 206 us | 230 us | +12% |
| Analysis loop/robustness/dynamics, exact-delay loops, PID design+review, ModelStudy evidence | | | ~ (within noise) |

B/op is 13-47% lower and allocs 3-42% lower on all frequency paths. Profile of ModelDesignEvidence order=30 2x2: 62% of CPU in FreqResponse -> balancedDense.evalInto (dense GEPP per point; n=30 <= 20*m keeps the dense tier for 2-input models, 200 points).
Not regressed (n=10, noisy): PID tune/retune, H-inf/LQG redesign + HinfSyn design, identification ARX/N4SID, sheet study review, parameter sweep, simulation, model conversion, web dock renders.
Absolute latencies stay < 20 ms per interaction, so not user-blocking; the regression is concentrated in moderate-order MIMO evidence (n in 10..40, m=2..4), i.e. the dense-tier crossover. Process Lab-side mitigation filed: process-lab ergo QHZJK6 (evaluate each response once per interaction).

## Problem
Evaluating exactly at a pole on the imaginary axis (or z=1 / unit circle) gives different contracts depending on realization (v1.13.1, also v1.12.2 for FreqResponse):

- Explicit SS 1/(s^2+1): FreqResponse([0.5,1,2]) -> H(j1) = +Inf+NaNi, err nil. ModelArray.FreqResponse same.
- Explicit integrator 1/s: DCGain -> +Inf, err nil; FreqResponse([0]) -> err nil (Inf).
- Same pole inside a model with internal delays (LFT): FreqResponse -> "controlsys: singular complex matrix: ... ErrSingularTransform".
- DCGain of an integrating model with internal delays: v1.12.2 returned +Inf, v1.13.x returns "DCGain: ... ErrSingularTransform" (new dcGainByEvaluation path). Bandwidth (margin.go) and TuningGoal tracking (tuning_goal.go) propagate that error; for explicit models Bandwidth treats Inf DC as "unbounded" (returns 0, nil).

Callers must special-case both Inf/NaN and ErrSingularTransform for the same mathematical situation.

## Repro
Process Lab flow: Source -> Sum(+-) -> Lag(1) -> exact Delay 0.3 -> back to Sum; Lag -> Transfer 1/(s^2+1). FreqResponse at omega=1 errors; remove the delay loop and it returns Inf.

## Ask
Pick one contract (Inf/NaN entries like MATLAB freqresp, or a typed error for both) and apply it across explicit, descriptor and LFT evaluation, DCGain and Bandwidth. Document it on FreqResponse/DCGain.

## Downstream
Process Lab maps ErrSingularTransform and non-finite sweep gains to a usage error (perf/controlsys-v113-impact branch, frequencyResponseError in internal/studio/analysis_frequency.go).

Queued 2026-10-04: start after COJINT (fix/audit-lft-freq-balance, stacked on #218) reports; stack on that branch. Resolve per MATLAB (freqresp/dcgain at a pole return Inf, not an error). Also touches DCGain (#196) and Bandwidth (#193).

data.title: peakGain: doubling loop never certifies gammaHigh on lightly damped models (gamma-scaled near-axis threshold)
data.body:
## Problem
hasImagEigs flags eigenvalues as near-axis when |Re λ| < sqrt(eps)·gamma·max(1,|λ|/gamma). The threshold grows with gamma, so at large gamma every Hamiltonian eigenvalue of a lightly damped mode (|Re λ| ≈ ζω0) counts as "imaginary". peakGain's doubling loop (norms.go, `for range 50 { if !ws.hasImagEigs(gammaHigh) ...; gammaHigh *= 2 }`) then never finds an upper bound: it runs all 50 doublings (gammaHigh ~1e16–1e20) and the bisection hits its 100-iteration cap. The bisection itself treats these as spurious (candidatePeak < mid → gammaHigh = mid); the doubling loop does not.

## Repro
Seed 20261004 trial 0 of TestPeakGain_CertifiedMatchesBisection (norms_test.go, branch fix/audit-hinf-certify): continuous, n=4, m=2, p=1, ζ=1.05e-5 resonance at ω≈1.2338. Peak 59538.2167701532. Trace of the pre-V6U2NM bisection: doubling reaches 1.42e16 with cands [0 1.2338 1.2338 0.6169 ...] and candidatePeak 59538 at every level; 122 Hamiltonian Schur decompositions total. 26 of 120 random models (ζ ∈ [1e-5,1e-2]) take 36–140 evals for this reason. Results are still correct to 1e-10; this is cost only.

## Suggested fix
In the doubling loop, apply the bisection's rule: if hasImagEigs(gammaHigh) but candidatePeak < gammaHigh, accept gammaHigh as upper bound (or raise gammaLow when candidatePeak ≥ gammaHigh). Or make the near-axis threshold independent of gamma for |λ| ≪ gamma. Coordinate with GH3MO7/TI6YYN (imag-eig test semantics).

Files: norms.go peakGain, hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs.

data.title: descriptor dense freq tier exceeds 1e-12 on weakrows discrete near-pole model
data.body:
Delay-free descriptor FreqResponse (balancedDense, frequency_hessenberg.go, from #212/#218) is 1.01e-12 normwise vs the refined oracle (oracleResponse, frequency_sweep_property_test.go) on a weakrows/descriptor/discrete model, above the 1e-12 the randomized descriptor test enforces. Found while fixing COJINT (branch fix/audit-lft-freq-balance).

Repro (helpers in frequency_sweep_property_test.go on that branch):
  kind := sweepWeakRows; rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(161, uint64(kind)))
  n := 1+rng.IntN(40); m, p, N := 1+rng.IntN(4), 1+rng.IntN(4), 1+rng.IntN(3)   // n=9 m=1 p=1 N=2
  aug, twin := randomSweepRealization(rng, kind, 0.05, true, n, m+N, p+N)
  take the p x m block (first m inputs, first p outputs, no internal delay) and compare newBalancedDense(...).evalInto vs oracleResponse on the same block over logspace(-3, log10(pi/dt), 60) stride 5:
  worst 1.01e-12.

Evidence:
- identical error with augmented balance, delay-free balance, and no balance at all (weakrows is unscaled: stressed == twin), so it is GEPP forward error, not balancing.
- discrete pole at 1-slow, slow~1e-4, |z-p|~1.6e-4 at w~2.5e-3: kappa*eps ~ 1e-12.
- existing TestFreqResponseDescriptorSweepRandomized worst over its 480 draws is 5.8e-13 on weakrows/desc/dt=0.05 (doesn't draw this model).
- COJINT's internal-delay variant excludes weakrows for this reason; reinstate it once this is resolved (e.g. one step of extra-precision refinement in the dense tier, or a documented accuracy class).

## Problem
hasImagEigs flags eigenvalues as near-axis when |Re λ| < sqrt(eps)·gamma·max(1,|λ|/gamma). The threshold grows with gamma, so at large gamma every Hamiltonian eigenvalue of a lightly damped mode (|Re λ| ≈ ζω0) counts as "imaginary". peakGain's doubling loop (norms.go, `for range 50 { if !ws.hasImagEigs(gammaHigh) ...; gammaHigh *= 2 }`) then never finds an upper bound: it runs all 50 doublings (gammaHigh ~1e16–1e20) and the bisection hits its 100-iteration cap. The bisection itself treats these as spurious (candidatePeak < mid → gammaHigh = mid); the doubling loop does not.

## Repro
Seed 20261004 trial 0 of TestPeakGain_CertifiedMatchesBisection (norms_test.go, branch fix/audit-hinf-certify): continuous, n=4, m=2, p=1, ζ=1.05e-5 resonance at ω≈1.2338. Peak 59538.2167701532. Trace of the pre-V6U2NM bisection: doubling reaches 1.42e16 with cands [0 1.2338 1.2338 0.6169 ...] and candidatePeak 59538 at every level; 122 Hamiltonian Schur decompositions total. 26 of 120 random models (ζ ∈ [1e-5,1e-2]) take 36–140 evals for this reason. Results are still correct to 1e-10; this is cost only.

## Suggested fix
In the doubling loop, apply the bisection's rule: if hasImagEigs(gammaHigh) but candidatePeak < gammaHigh, accept gammaHigh as upper bound (or raise gammaLow when candidatePeak ≥ gammaHigh). Or make the near-axis threshold independent of gamma for |λ| ≪ gamma. Coordinate with GH3MO7/TI6YYN (imag-eig test semantics).

Files: norms.go peakGain, hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs.

## Update after V6U2NM (PR #220)
With certifyPeak, the 26 lightly damped random models above now take 3–5 evals: the probe at gammaLow·(1+tol/2) applies the spurious-candidate rule and certifies. The doubling loop is now reached only when candidatePeak cannot be evaluated (e.g. the probe is below σ(D), so Dpotrf fails: high-pass with D=1 still takes 36 evals) or from inside the bisection fallback. Lower priority. It is cost only, not accuracy.

data.title: Export the automatic Bode frequency grid (autoBodeFreqs) without evaluating the response
data.body:
## Why
Process Lab (ergo QHZJK6) needs the grid Bode(nil, n) would use without paying a full FreqResponse (v1.13 evaluation is 2-3x slower). Today it calls Bode(nil, n) only to read .Omega, or copies autoBodeFreqs (process-lab internal/studio/analysis_frequency.go automaticFrequencyGrid). The copy is fragile: on arm64 the Go compiler fuses Log10's 1/ln10 scaling into stop-start when inlined, drifting the grid by an ulp; process-lab forces float64() conversions and pins it bit-for-bit with TestAutomaticFrequencyGridMatchesBode.

## Proposal
Export e.g. `func (sys *System) BodeFrequencies(nPoints int) ([]float64, error)` (or `AutoFrequencyGrid`) returning exactly autoBodeFreqs(sys, nPoints); same for marginFreqs if useful. Document that Bode/Sigma/Nichols(nil, n) evaluate on this grid.

## Done when
Exported, documented, tested equal to Bode(nil,n).Omega; process-lab can delete automaticFrequencyGrid.

data.title: Place: 2x2 assignment in (trace,det) form loses accuracy; near-scalar blocks reported uncontrollable
data.body:
Found while fixing NBGAEF (2x2 Schur eigenvalue cancellation). Out of scope there; Place's 2x2 assignment (controller.go placeAssign2x2, called from Place ~line 384-400) has two independent defects. Both reproduce on main and after the NBGAEF fix.

Repro (package test, B := [[1,0],[0.5,1],[-1,2]] 3x2, poles {-2s, -1.5s±1i}):
  A := [[-3s, 2, -1],[0, -s, aim],[0, -aim, -s]]

1) Silent accuracy loss (no error returned). aim=1, closed-loop eig(A-BF):
   s=1e2  -> imag 1.0000000007
   s=1e3  -> imag 0.99999803
   s=1e4  -> imag 0.93785  (6% wrong, Place returns nil error)
   Cause: desired pair encoded as tr=2re, det=re^2+im^2; det loses im^2 when im^2 ~< eps*re^2, and the convergence check `|det_now-det| > 1e-8*scale` with scale=1+|tr|+|det| accepts det errors of ~1e-8*re^2 (= imag^2 error 2.25 at s=1e4). Should assign/verify in (re, im) form (e.g. check eigenvalues of the 2x2 block via Dlanv2 / schur2x2Eigenvalues against the target with a backward-error tolerance), or return an error when the target is not attained.

2) False ErrUncontrollable: aim=1e-6 (near-scalar open-loop 2x2 block, normal matrix) fails for every scale s in {1..1e4} with "Place: mode 1: assignment did not converge" / "uncontrollable mode cannot be assigned", although (A,B) with m=2 is controllable. Cause: placeAssign2x2's correction basis [b, adj(T)b] collapses when T ~ lambda*I (c1 ~ lambda*b), so cc00*cc11-cc01^2 ~ 0. Multi-input case needs a basis that uses the independent input directions (e.g. full 2x2 block F in span of Bhat rows), MATLAB place handles it.

Files: controller.go (Place, placeAssign2x2). Test against closed-loop eig(A-BF) oracle.

data.title: Margin picks smallest positive GM/PM; MATLAB picks closest to 0 dB/0°
data.body:
margin.go Margin(): selects smallest positive gain margin, falling back to the largest when none is positive (same for phase). MATLAB margin doc: "When sys has several crossovers, margin returns the gain margin closest to 0 dB" and "the phase margin closest to 0°" (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.margin.html).
Evidence: random SISO continuous model with input delay (found while fixing MUCNXY, seed rand.NewPCG(7,9) case 198 of a 300-model sweep): AllMargin GMs = {-0.986 dB, ..., +4.88 dB}; Margin returns +4.88 dB, MATLAB rule gives -0.986 dB. Whether the +4.88 crossing is even seen depends on grid extent, so Margin results are also grid-fragile under the current rule.
Fix: pick min |GM| (dB) and min |PM| (deg, wrapped) with their frequencies; add oracle test with hand-built L having negative and positive GMs.

data.title: hasImagEigs blind to crossings for gamma within ~1e-8 rel of sigma_max(D)
data.body:
## Problem
For gamma = σmax(D)·(1+f) with f ≲ 1e-8, R = γ²I − DᵀD is near singular and hasImagEigs (norms.go) returns false even when the model has a large resonance peak far above γ. At f = 1e-6 the same models do show the crossings, and candidatePeak exceeds the probe.

## Repro
Branch fix/audit-hinf-doubling (PR for YJG5ZH), norms_test.go `highPassResonanceSys(t, rand.New(rand.NewSource(1)), 0)`: a 2×2 high-pass plus a ζ∈[1e-6,1e-4] resonance. Trials 0–3: σ(D) ≈ 94–196, true peak 2e4–4e5. `ws.hasImagEigs(σ(D)*(1+f))` is false for f ∈ {1e-12 … 1e-8} (trial 3: up to 1e-10) and true for f ≥ 1e-6.

## Impact
This blocks seeding gammaLow = max(sampled, σmax(D)) in peakGain, which would make high-pass D=1 cost 1 eval instead of 36. The seed gave wrong answers (e.g. 125 vs 155665) on 50/60 such models because certifyPeak's probe at σ(D)(1+tol/2) is blind. It is also a latent accuracy risk whenever a probe or bisection level sits within ~1e-8 of σ(D) while a real crossing exists elsewhere. No current-path failure was found: a scan of 200 models with the sampled bound just above σ(D) showed none.

## Fix ideas
Use a γ-dependent formulation that avoids R⁻¹ (an extended/skew-Hamiltonian pencil, as in Benner et al. / SLICOT AB13DD) or probe the σ(D) neighbourhood at a safe offset. Coordinate with GH3MO7/TI6YYN (imag-eig semantics).

Files: norms.go hasImagEigs, peakGain.

data.title: certifyPeak result 1.6e-10 rel from bisection on zeta~1e-7 peaks
data.body:
## Problem
On very sharp peaks (ζ ≈ 1e-7, peak ≈ 2e7), peakGain via certifyPeak differs from the plain-bisection oracle (bisectionPeakGain in norms_test.go) by 1.58e-10 relative, more than the 1e-10 tolerance. This is the same on origin/main (c39e7b0) and on fix/audit-hinf-doubling, so it predates the YJG5ZH change.

## Repro
In norms_test.go, using rand.NewSource(1), for trial in 0..199: n=2+Intn(7), m=1+Intn(2), p=1+Intn(2), zeta=10^(-4-3·Float64()), dt = 0.1 on odd trials, sys := randomStableNormSys(t, rng, n, m, p, dt, true, zeta), then sys.D.Scale(10^(4·Float64()), sys.D). Trial 132: peakGain = 22538920.0482125, bisection = 22538920.0517815.

## Notes
The attained candidate frequency may be inaccurate for near-double crossing eigenvalues. Find which value is closer to the truth (dense golden-section search on σmax around the peak) before deciding whether to fix it or relax the test. It is cost-free to investigate. TestPeakGain_CertifiedMatchesBisection uses ζ ≥ 1e-5 and does not hit this.

Files: norms.go certifyPeak, candidatePeak.

data.title: Nyquist discrete z=1 pole: repeated ω=0 grid points
data.body: Seen in MUCNXY work (PR #223): for a discrete model with a pole at z=1, the Nyquist auto-grid starts with three repeated ω=0 points. Unverified whether main does the same. Check nyquist.go grid construction; grid must be strictly increasing (dedupe) and handle the z=1 indentation per MATLAB nyquist semantics.

data.title: extractBlock returns 1-wide zero matrix for zero-width blocks; Simulate silently empty for m=0
data.body:
Found while fixing PVX7Q5 (PR #226).

1. matutil.go extractBlock(m, r0, c0, rows, cols): when exactly one of rows/cols is 0 it returns mat.NewDense(max(rows,1), max(cols,1)) — e.g. extractBlock(2x2, 0,0, 2,0) has Dims (2,1), not an empty block. 79 call sites (lft.go lftSimple/lftExtract, minimal.go extractSubmatrix, balance.go singularPerturbation, ...) may build models with a phantom zero channel when a partition is empty (e.g. LFT nu=0 or ny=0, Modred partitions). Audit callers; return &mat.Dense{} and make callers zero-safe (mulDims/newDense helpers in matutil.go), with tests on LFT(M, Delta, 0, ny) etc.

2. System.Simulate(u, x0, opts) takes u as m×steps, so a model with m=0 cannot express the step count: Simulate(nil, x0, nil) on a discrete autonomous model returns Y=nil, XFinal set, err=nil (silent). Either add a steps option / return a clear error for m=0, or document. Initial and Lsim(nil u) already handle m=0 via zeroInputModel in response.go.

data.title: Bandwidth accepts dbDrop>=0/NaN; MATLAB requires negative dbdrop
data.body:
margin.go Bandwidth(sys, dbDrop): dbDrop == 0 means default -3; dbDrop > 0 returns 0; NaN flows into threshold silently.
MATLAB bandwidth doc (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.bandwidth.html): "dbdrop — Gain drop in dB, specified as a real negative scalar." MATLAB errors otherwise.
Repro: Bandwidth(1/(s+1), 3) -> 0, nil; Bandwidth(1/(s+1), NaN) -> undefined result, nil.
Fix: return a sentinel error for dbDrop > 0 or NaN/Inf (no generic invalid-argument sentinel exists in errors.go; add one or reuse an existing pattern), keep 0 -> -3 default if API needs it, document mapping. Found while fixing JJMA3D (PR fix/audit-margin-exact).

data.title: Place: repeated real poles with multiplicity <= rank(B) give defective closed loop
data.body:
Place (controller.go) assigns real poles through deflating 1x1 Schur steps, so a repeated real pole with multiplicity <= rank(B) can still yield a defective closed loop; MATLAB place (KNV robust assignment) returns a non-defective A-BK in that case.

Repro (package test, after SJMAC2 fix):
  A = [[0.3,1,-0.4],[-1.1,-0.2,0.5],[0.7,0.1,-1.5]], B = [[1,0],[0.2,0.5],[0,1]], poles {-1,-1,-3}
  svd(A-BK+I) = [3.10, 0.89, 4.8e-16] -> rank 2, geometric multiplicity 1 (Jordan block) although rank(B)=2.
Expected (MATLAB): nondefective, A-BK+I rank 1.
Fix idea: group equal real poles and assign them to a 2x2 block via placeAssign2x2's multi-input path (makes block scalar), or adopt KNV. Also decide whether to match MATLAB error for multiplicity > rank(B) (currently allowed by documented contract; TestPlace_ComplexOpenLoopContract SISO {-2,-2,-2,-3} relies on it).

data.title: Place: no robust (KNV) eigenvector conditioning for MIMO; kappa(V) large at small scale
data.body:
Place uses Varga's Schur deflation and does not optimise closed-loop eigenvector conditioning, unlike MATLAB place (Kautsky-Nichols-Van Dooren robust assignment). Upper Schur coupling is left untouched, so kappa(V) of A-BK can be large when off-diagonal coupling dominates eigenvalue gaps.

Repro: A = [[-3s,2,-1],[0,-s,aim],[0,-aim,-s]], B = [[1,0.3],[0.5,1],[-1,2]], s=1e-4, poles {-2s,-1.5s+-s i}: kappa(V) ~4e4-5e4 (s=1e-2: ~400). n=3, m=2 leaves freedom KNV would use.
Files: controller.go Place. See tests TestPlace_NearScalarBlockMIMO (uses kappa-tied tolerance only because of this).
Fix: implement KNV method 0/1 (as MATLAB place / scipy place_poles) for m>1, keep Varga for m=1 or as fallback; preserve TestPlace_ComplexOpenLoopContract.

data.title: Simulate XFinal ignores input/IO delays (state driven by undelayed u)
data.body:
simulate.go simulateWithDelay: Y applies InputDelay/Delay correctly but XFinal is accumulated from the forced state columns driven by the *undelayed* u (xCols propagated with u_k at step k, delays only applied when writing Y). MATLAB lsim's x is the state of the delay-free part driven by the delayed input.

Repro (discrete dt=0.1): A=[0.5 0.2;-0.3 0.4], B=[1;-0.5], C=[1 1], D=0, InputDelay=[2], u=[1 -1 0.5 2 0], x0=[0.3 -0.8].
sys.Simulate(u,x0,nil).XFinal = [0.804123 -1.044391]; hand propagation x_{k+1}=A x_k + B u_{k-2} gives [0.178723 -0.053391]. Y is correct ([-0.5 -0.42 -0.248 0.386 -0.63812]).
Also: XFinal does not carry the delay-line contents (pending inputs), so chaining Simulate calls across a delay is impossible; decide/document per MATLAB.
Found while fixing M27M2G.

data.title: AllMargin/Margin/Bandwidth miss crossings on high-order loops (TF polynomial candidates)
data.body:
rationalLoop (margin.go, #227) finds gain/phase crossing candidates as boundary roots of |N|^2-|D|^2 and Im(N conj D) built from sys.TransferFunction coefficients. At n >= ~60 these coefficients are inaccurate (evaluating the same N/D gives 6% error at n=100), so roots drift off the imaginary axis beyond the boundaryRoots acceptance band or beyond polish's +-1e-2 relative bracket, and crossings are silently dropped. Refinement itself now uses the exact state-space response (sisoEval fix on branch fix/freq-highorder, task 6FISAR), so reported crossings are accurate; only completeness is affected.

Repro (in package controlsys, test helpers from frequency_sweep_property_test.go):
  rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(uint64(n), uint64(kind))); sys, _ := randomSweepRealization(rng, kind, 0, false, n, 1, 1)
  scale C, D so |L(j1)| = 3; AllMargin(sys)
  brute force: FreqResponsePointwise on logspace(-4,4,20000), sign changes of log|L| and Im L (Re L<0), refineCrossing.
Results with SS refinement (n=60: 2/6 kinds mismatch, n=100: 4/6), e.g. n=100 dense: AllMargin gc=[0.02164 3.1657] pc=[] vs brute pc=[0.70696]; n=100 decoupled: AllMargin gc=[] pc=[] vs brute gc=[1.6231] pc=[0.00055]. Main (TF refinement) is worse: n=60 2/6, n=100 6/6 mismatches. n <= 45 all match.

Fix idea: detect when the polynomial candidate stage is unreliable (degree above a threshold, or a reliability check such as comparing a coarse SS grid's sign changes with the candidate count) and fall back to/augment with gridMarginCrossings on the exact SS response; or compute candidates from state-space eigenproblems (Hamiltonian-like pencil for |L|=1, as in HinfNorm / MATLAB allmargin for ss models) instead of TF polynomials. Keep MATLAB allmargin semantics.
Files: margin.go (rationalLoop.gainCandidates/realCandidates/boundaryRoots/polish, AllMargin, Margin, Bandwidth).

data.title: Lqi ignores D and discrete time (MATLAB lqi uses Ba=[B;-D], forward-Euler Ts)
data.body:
Lqi(A, B, C, Q, R, opts) (controller.go) augments Aaug=[A 0; -C 0], Baug=[B; 0] and always calls Lqr (continuous CARE).
MATLAB lqi(sys,Q,R,N) (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/ss.lqi.html) integrates y = Cx + Du, so Ba = [B; -D], and in discrete time uses forward Euler xi[n+1] = xi[n] + Ts(r[n] - y[n]) (Aa = [A 0; -Ts*C I], Ba = [B; -Ts*D]) with DARE. It also supports descriptor models with nonsingular E.
Evidence: QXKVXH (branch fix/lqg-matlab) implements this augmentation inside Lqg (lqgServoProblem in lqg.go) and matches the MATLAB lqg doc servo example (D=[0.53 -0.61]) to 4 digits; zeroing the -D block fails 7 Lqg tests, so the current Lqi gives wrong gains for D != 0.
Fix: Lqi needs D and sample time (e.g. take *System like MATLAB, or reuse lqgServoProblem). Breaking API; check callers.
Tests: MATLAB lqg doc example gains via Lqi; DARE residual for discrete; D != 0, MIMO, non-symmetric A.

data.title: Ops reducing an autonomous/no-output model to n=0 silently return a 0x0 gain
data.body:
A model with no inputs (m=0, p>0) or no outputs (p=0, m>0) whose states are all removed collapses to a static gain that gonum cannot store (CONTEXT.md: "A static-gain model with no inputs or no outputs but not both cannot be stored"). Several ops silently return a 0x0 gain (Dims (0,0,0)) instead of a sentinel error, losing the I/O dimension.

Repro (on origin/main and after M27M2G):
  sys := emptyIOFixture(t, 3, 0, 2, dt)   // ss_test.go helper, dt 0 or 0.1
  r, err := Modred(sys, []int{0,1,2}, SingularPerturbation) // err=nil, r.Dims()=(0,0,0); want ErrDimensionMismatch (MATLAB: 2x0 static gain)
  Modred(..., Truncate) same; also emptyIOFixture(t,3,2,0,dt) -> (0,0,0).
Likely root: NewGain(&mat.Dense{}) / buildSystem(nil,nil,nil,D) accept an empty D with no dims. Audit Modred, Balred(order 0), MinimalRealization/Sminreal on unobservable/uncontrollable empty-IO models, ZeroDelayApprox n==0, Append/Series n==0 paths. Fix pattern: lft.go lftGain/lftGainDims (added in M27M2G) returns ErrDimensionMismatch when exactly one of p,m is 0.
Found while fixing M27M2G.

data.title: DiscretizeLeastSquares: high-order sources (TF polynomial target, integrator miscount)
data.body:
conversion_least_squares.go evaluates the continuous source through its TransferFunction polynomials (target[k] in DiscretizeLeastSquares, `actual` in leastSquaresFitQuality) and counts integrators from trailing denominator coefficients (leastSquaresIntegratorLimit: |den[last]| <= 1e-12*max|den|).

1. Integrator miscount: for a stable dense random source with no pole at 0, n >= ~60 reports spurious integrators because the trailing coefficient (product of the roots) is tiny relative to the largest coefficient, not zero. Repro (package controlsys test helpers): rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(100, uint64(sweepDense))); src, _ := randomSweepRealization(rng, sweepDense, 0, false, 100, 1, 1); src.DiscretizeLeastSquares(0.05, 8) -> "fit order must retain 11 integrators: reduction order out of range" (all eigenvalues have Re <= -0.2). n=60 with order 1 or 2 -> "must retain 3 integrators".
2. Source response: TF polynomial evaluation of the same source is 6% off at n=100 (measured vs refined dense oracle, see 6FISAR), so target and reported RMS/Max errors are wrong once (1) is fixed. Swapping both to work.FreqResponse(omega) (state space; Inf at a pole still trips the existing ErrSingularTransform check) was prototyped on branch fix/freq-highorder and passes existing tests, but could not be tested independently because (1) blocks every high-order case.
Fix idea: count integrators structurally (poles at s=0 of the minimal realization, e.g. eigenvalues of A within tolerance of 0 that are controllable+observable, or a scaled coefficient test using den[last-1]), compute the residue from the state-space DC limit, and sample the source on its state-space realization. Test with n=100 source vs oracleResponse.

data.title: FRD.Nyquist encirclement count uses positive branch only (undercounts by half)
data.body:
Repro (controlsys main, branch fix/nyquist-grid):
  sys = 180/((s+1)(s+2)(s+3)) (companion form), w = logspace(-3,3,600)
  f, _ := sys.FRD(w); r, _ := f.Nyquist()
  r.Encirclements == 1, but (*System).Nyquist gives 2 (closed loop has 2 RHP poles; Routh: K=180 > Kc=60).
Cause: frd.go (*FRD).Nyquist counts real-axis crossings left of -1 on the positive-frequency branch only; the mirrored negative branch (ContourN) contributes the same crossings for real-coefficient data and is ignored. Also no closure at omega ends; crossing sign convention should be checked against (*System).Nyquist (clockwise positive).
Files: frd.go (FRD.Nyquist), frd_test.go (TestFRD_NyquistFromFRD).
Fix: count winding of the full closed curve conj-reverse(contour)+contour around -1 (reuse windingNumber in nyquist.go), document that FRD data cannot indent around boundary poles; test vs (*System).Nyquist on rational loops.

data.title: Descriptor (nonsingular E) support for Lqr/Lqi/Lqg via generalized Riccati
data.body:
MATLAB lqr/lqi/lqg accept descriptor models with nonsingular E (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/ss.lqi.html: "Descriptor models supported with nonsingular E"), solving the generalized ARE (E'XA + A'XE - (E'XB+N)R^-1(B'XE+N') + Q = 0; S returned is the generalized solution, K = R^-1(B'XE + N')).
controlsys has no generalized Care/Dare; Lqi(sys,...) (controller.go, after 6IHNTQ) and Lqg (lqg.go) reject E != I with ErrDescriptorRiccati via requireRiccatiStandard (descriptor.go). Lqr/Dlqr take matrices so cannot accept E at all.
Repro: Lqi(obsTestPlant(t,0,true), eye(5), eye(2), nil) -> ErrDescriptorRiccati; MATLAB returns gains.
Fix: add E to RiccatiOpts (or generalized solvers) and thread through Lqi/Lqg; K equals the E^-1-reduced design, X differs (X_gen relates by E'X_gen E = X_std).
Tests: generalized Riccati residual, gains equal to explicit E^-1 form, continuous+discrete, non-symmetric E.

data.title: Discrete FreqResponse evaluates at rounded e^{jωT}, off the unit circle near lightly damped poles
data.body:
## Problem
Discrete FreqResponse/FreqResponsePointwise/EvalFr evaluate G at z = complex(cos ωT, sin ωT) (newTimeDomain.frequencyVariable). The rounded z lies up to ε off the unit circle. Next to a pole at distance ζω₀T from the circle, a radial ε shift changes |G| by about ε/(ζω₀T) relative, which is far more than the solver's componentwise accuracy. GEPP and refinement cannot fix this, because the error is in the evaluation point itself.

## Repro
norms_test.go highPassResonanceSys(t, rand.New(rand.NewSource(1)), dt) for trial 3 (dt = 0.1, ζ ≈ 1e-6, peak 4.1e5). Over ω = 0.37637388819420237 + k·4e-16, k = 0..8, FreqResponsePointwise σ_max drifts from 410649.102963295 to .102948665 (3.5e-11 relative over 3e-15 rad/s). The exact value, from a 300-bit solve at z = (1+jν)/(1−jν) with ν = tan(ωT/2), is flat at 410649.102948869. Trials from the Z5SW7V generator (ζ ~ 1e-7, dt = 0.1) show errors up to ~1e-9.

## Fix idea
Parametrise z = (1+jν)/(1−jν) with ν = tan(ωT/2), which lies on the unit circle for every floating-point ν. Then solve ((1+jν)I − (1−jν)A)X = B and use G = (1−jν)·C·X + D (past ωT = π/2, use μ = cot(ωT/2)). norms.go sigmaEvaluator.resolventScalars does this for the H∞ peak (PR for DLWKKE/Z5SW7V/GH3MO7/TI6YYN). The sweep code (frequency.go, frequency_hessenberg.go) is owned elsewhere. Test against an exact-arithmetic oracle like norms_test.go exactSigmaMax.

Files: timedomain frequencyVariable, frequency.go sweepInto/evalPoint, frequency_hessenberg.go.

data.title: IODelay x0 convention: Simulate/Initial/Lsim skip Delay output share, PullDelaysToLFT route applies it
data.body:
Inconsistent free-response (x0) convention for the p×m Delay (IODelay) matrix. Found while fixing SEWANW.

Convention A (Simulate's simulateWithDelay, Initial which sets free.Delay=nil, continuousFreeSamples in response.go): x0 response is shifted by OutputDelay only; Delay never delays it. Pinned by TestInitialContinuousDelaysExact (nondecomposable/mixed cases), TestSimulateSIMOWithDelay/with_x0, TestLsimContinuousX0WithFractionalOutputDelay, TestSimulateWithDelay_MIMOManualReference.
Convention B (PullDelaysToLFT, delay.go): Delay is split by DecomposeIODelay into InputDelay+OutputDelay(+residual); the output share then delays the x0 response.

Repro (dt=1): A=[0.5 0.2 -0.1;-0.3 0.4 0.25;0.1 -0.2 0.6], B=[1 0.3;-0.5 0.8;0.2 -1], C=[1 1 0;0.4 -0.7 1.2], D=[0.3 -0.1;0.2 0.5], Delay=[1 2;4 5], x0=[0.3 -0.8 0.5], 8 samples of u.
sys.Simulate(u,x0) row 2 free part is unshifted; sys.PullDelaysToLFT().Simulate(u,x0) row 2 is shifted by 3 (first 3 samples 0). XFinal agrees (fixed in SEWANW).
Simulate's own dispatcher already uses convention B for Delay + internal delays (PullDelaysToLFT route), so one Simulate call follows either convention depending on the model.
Also: nondecomposable Delay + internal delay + nonzero x0: merged residual-split realization has more than n states; simulateWithInternalDelay's newXFinal CopyVec's the n-length x0 into the first n states of the larger vector (seeds only one copy). Y is then questionable.
MATLAB ss has no IODelay; ss(tf with IODelay) moves delays into Input/OutputDelay (+internal), so MATLAB behaves like B; nondecomposable + x0 has no MATLAB equivalent (likely sentinel error, e.g. ErrDelayUnsupported).
Files: simulate.go (simulateWithDelay free block, dispatcher), response.go (Initial, continuousFreeSamples), delay.go PullDelaysToLFT; tests above.

data.title: Care Rcnd uses norm of LU factors instead of U11
data.body:
riccati.go Care (explicit path): `anorm := impl.Dlange(... u11 ...)` is computed AFTER `impl.Dgetrf(n, n, u11, ...)` overwrote u11 with its LU factors, then passed to Dgecon. Dgecon expects the 1-norm of the original matrix, so Care's Rcnd is mis-estimated. Dare (and the new stabilizingSolution helper in fix/descriptor-riccati) compute anorm before Dgetrf.
Fix: route Care through stabilizingSolution (riccati.go) or move Dlange before Dgetrf. Test: Rcnd equals 1/(norm1(U11)*norm1(inv(U11))) estimate within Dgecon's bound for a MIMO non-symmetric case where LU factor norm differs from U11 norm.
Found while fixing HS7Q34.

data.title: Care/Dare/Lqr/Lqe return empty X/K with nil error for n == 0
data.body:
New user rule: never return empty/placeholder values with nil error. riccati.go Care/Dare (`if n == 0 { return &RiccatiResult{X: &mat.Dense{}, K: &mat.Dense{}} , nil }`), observer.go Lqe (same), and Lqr/Dlqr/Lqrd through them return zero-size results with nil error for zero-state problems. Should return a sentinel (e.g. ErrDimensionMismatch, as Lqi/Lqg/Kalman do via newControllerObserverPolicy "system has no states").
Tests TestCare_Empty / TestDare_Empty in riccati_test.go currently assert the empty result and must be changed. Found while fixing HS7Q34 (preexisting, not touched there).

data.title: Go idiom audit (strict error pattern, MATLAB-shaped args)
data.body: Audit of all controlsys source for Go idioms per user rule (2026-10-04): strict Go error pattern (valid value + nil error, or error; never placeholders/partial results with nil error), MATLAB-matching arguments with opt-in optional outputs, and general idiomatic Go. Brief: scratchpad idiom-audit.md. Five auditors partition the 120 non-test files.

data.title: Triage Go idiom audit findings into fix batches
data.body: After the five auditors report, group filed tasks by file area and dispatch fixers.

data.title: FreqResponse returns nil,nil for empty omega; Bode/Nichols panic; Sigma/FRD return empty placeholders
data.body:
Rule: every return is a fully formed value with nil error, or a non-nil error.

Files (group 2): frequency.go, frd.go
- frequency.go:205-207 `frequencyEvaluator.response`: `if len(omega)==0 { return nil, nil }` -> public `(*System).FreqResponse` returns (nil, nil).
- frequency.go:237-239 `responsePointwise`: same -> `FreqResponsePointwise` (nil, nil).
- frequency.go:154-171 `Bode`: only `omega == nil` selects the default grid; non-nil empty slice reaches `resp.Data` on nil resp -> nil deref panic.
- frequency.go:791-798 `Nichols`: panics via Bode; its `if bode == nil { return nil, nil }` is a dead (nil,nil) path.
- frequency.go:854-866 `Sigma`: nSV==0 (p==0||m==0) returns SigmaResult{nSV:0, sv:nil}; empty omega returns SigmaResult{nSV:1, sv:nil} (At() would index out of range) — both with nil error.
- frd.go:103-106 `(*System).FRD`: empty omega -> `&FRD{Dt: sys.Dt}` (0x0, no names) nil error.

Repro (throwaway test, 2-state SISO sys):
  FreqResponse empty: r=<nil> err=<nil>
  Bode empty: PANIC runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  Nichols empty: PANIC runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
  Sigma empty: r=&{Omega:[] sv:[] nSV:1 ...} err=<nil>
  sys.FRD empty: r=&{Response:[] Omega:[] Dt:0 ...} err=<nil>

Fix: empty (non-nil) omega -> `fmt.Errorf("<Op>: empty frequency vector: %w", ErrInvalidArgument)` in validFrequencyEvaluator path (FreqResponse, FreqResponsePointwise, EvalFr unaffected) and in Bode/Sigma/Nichols/System.FRD; keep `omega == nil` => default grid for Bode/Sigma/Nichols (document "nil selects default grid; empty non-nil is an error"). p==0||m==0 in Sigma -> error per W7OUGJ precedent (zero-dimension results are not valid values). Remove Nichols' dead nil check. Update internal callers that rely on nil (grep `resp == nil`).
Related: FRD-side empties filed separately.

data.title: Gram: L nil with nil error when gramian not PD; make Cholesky factor an opt-in type (MATLAB gram 'cf'/'of')
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

File: gramian.go:61-76 (GramResult.L), gramian.go:46 (n==0).

Current: Gram(sys, typ) always returns GramResult{X, L}. L is set only when Dpotrf succeeds; for a stable but uncontrollable/unobservable model (X semidefinite) L is nil and err is nil. n==0 returns X=&mat.Dense{}, L=nil.

Repro (confirmed in scratch copy):
  s := NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=diag(-1,-2), B=[1;0], C=[1 1], D=0, 0)
  r, err := Gram(s, GramControllability)  // err=nil, r.L==nil

Violates: "every return is a fully formed value or a non-nil error; no nil fields meaning unavailable". MATLAB makes the factor an explicit request: gram(sys,'c'|'o'|'cf'|'of').

Proposed fix (MATLAB-shaped args):
- Drop GramResult.L from the default result; Gram(sys, GramControllability|GramObservability) returns X only (or GramResult{X}).
- Add GramType values GramControllabilityFactor / GramObservabilityFactor (MATLAB 'cf'/'of'); those return the Cholesky factor and fail with ErrNotMinimal (wrapped "Gram: ...") when Dpotrf fails.
- policy.gramianInputs must map factor types to the base equation.
- Also: invalid GramType currently returns bare ErrDimensionMismatch with no "Gram:" prefix -> should be fmt.Errorf("Gram: unknown type %d: %w", typ, ErrInvalidArgument).
- n==0 empty X: follow whatever W7OUGJ settles for n==0 matrix results.
- Document GramType/GramResult.

data.title: ModelArray: void entries returned as (nil,false,nil) and nil Responses+Void flags; headers placeholder for all-void/mixed-order arrays
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

File: model_array.go

1. ModelArray.Model / ModelFlat (model_array.go:194-217) return (*System, bool, error); a void slot returns (nil, false, nil). This is the banned bool+error double signalling and nil value with nil error.
   Repro (confirmed): arr,_ := NewModelArray([]int{2}, []*System{s, nil}); m, ok, err := arr.ModelFlat(1) -> m=nil ok=false err=nil.
   Fix: (*System, error); void slot -> fmt.Errorf("ModelArray.ModelFlat: index %d: %w", i, ErrVoidModel) (new sentinel); add IsVoid(index...) bool for callers that need to probe.
2. ModelArrayFreqResponse / ModelArrayTimeResponse (lines 19-32, 235-282): Responses[i]==nil plus parallel Void []bool flag = nil field meaning unavailable. Fix: either error on void entries, or represent results as a ModelArray-shaped result whose accessor returns (resp, error) with ErrVoidModel for void slots; no nil entries in exported slices.
3. NewModelArray with all-nil models (line 53-72) succeeds with n=m=p=0, dt=0, names nil -> headers are placeholders; Stack/Concat then compare against these zeros. Repro (confirmed): NewModelArray([]int{2}, []*System{nil,nil}) -> err=nil, Dims()=0,0,0. Fix: require at least one non-void model (or explicit header args), else ErrInvalidArgument.
4. Dims() returns n of the first model only, but models with different state counts are accepted (validateModelArrayCompatible checks only m,p). Repro (confirmed): array of 1-state and 2-state models -> Dims n=1. Fix: drop n from Dims (return m,p like MATLAB size of I/O) or add per-model Order(index) (int, error); never report the first model's n as the array's.
5. Sample-time mismatch (lines 307, 320) wraps ErrDimensionMismatch; should be ErrDomainMismatch (errors.Is(err, ErrDomainMismatch) is false today, confirmed). Signal-name mismatch also wraps ErrDimensionMismatch; ErrInvalidArgument or a names sentinel fits better.
6. Idioms: sameModelArrayShape/stringSlicesCompatible element loops -> slices.Equal; copyIntSlice -> slices.Clone.
7. Exported ModelArray, ModelArrayFreqResponse, ModelArrayTimeResponse, NewModelArray, StackModelArrays, ConcatModelArrays and all methods lack doc comments.

data.title: Inv: static-gain inverse keeps input/output names unswapped
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit). Correctness bug.

File: inv.go:41-47 (n==0 branch) vs inv.go:70-72 (dynamic branch).

Current: for n==0, Inv builds NewGain(Dinv) then calls propagateIONames(result, sys), which copies InputName->InputName and OutputName->OutputName. The dynamic branch correctly swaps (result.InputName = sys.OutputName, result.OutputName = sys.InputName).

Repro (confirmed in scratch copy):
  g := NewGain([[2]]); g.InputName=["u"]; g.OutputName=["y"]
  r,_ := Inv(g)   // r.InputName=[u] r.OutputName=[y]  (should be [y] / [u])
  same model with one state -> in=[y] out=[u] (correct)

Fix: in the n==0 branch assign result.InputName = copyStringSlice(sys.OutputName), result.OutputName = copyStringSlice(sys.InputName) (plus any per-channel metadata such as groups that propagateIONames carries, swapped). Add test with a static gain and names.

Also in inv.go:
- line 14: delay rejection has no sentinel: fmt.Errorf("Inv: system with delays not supported; ...") -> wrap ErrDelayUnsupported (errors.Is currently false, confirmed).
- line 31-39: identity via ones+NewDiagDense+SolveTo; Dinv.Inverse or invertSmall is simpler (minor).
- Inv lacks a doc comment (MATLAB inv(sys); document square requirement, ErrSingularTransform for singular D, delay rejection).

data.title: GeneralizedModel/GeneralizedClosedLoop: unvalidated names yield invalid System, nil-receiver panic, controller aliasing, any-typed blocks
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

File: generalized.go

1. GeneralizedModel.SetInputName/SetOutputName (lines 74-80) accept any count; CurrentSystem (108-123) then stamps them onto the System with nil error. Contrast System.SetInputName which errors on count mismatch.
   Repro (confirmed): g := NewGeneralizedModel("g", oneInputSys); g.SetInputName("a","b","c"); cs, err := g.CurrentSystem() -> err=nil, cs.InputName=[a b c] for a 1-input model (cs.Validate() also nil, so Validate does not catch it).
   Fix: validate in CurrentSystem (len must equal m/p, or single name expanded like System.SetInputName) and return ErrDimensionMismatch; or make the setters return error and validate against the block's current dims.
2. (*GeneralizedModel).InsertAnalysisPoint (82-87) panics on nil receiver (confirmed nil-pointer panic) while HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem on the same type are nil-safe. Also accepts empty name and records Location=Unspecified. Make it return error like GeneralizedClosedLoop.InsertAnalysisPoint (validate name, nil receiver).
3. NewGeneralizedClosedLoop copies plant (plant.Copy()) but stores a *System controller by reference via fixedSystemBlock; later caller mutation changes the loop.
   Repro (confirmed): ctrl.A=-2; cl := NewGeneralizedClosedLoop("cl", s, ctrl, "y"); ctrl.A.Set(0,0,-50); cl.OpenLoop("y").A changes from [-2 0;1 -1] to [-50 0;1 -1].
   Fix: numericBlockFromAny should copy *System (fixedSystemBlock{sys: b.Copy()}); same for NewGeneralizedModel. A typed-nil *System is accepted and only fails later in CurrentSystem; reject at construction.
4. API shape: block/controller parameters are `any` with a runtime type switch. Prefer a typed parameter: NumericBlock, with an exported adapter (e.g. FixedBlock(sys *System) NumericBlock) or making *System satisfy NumericBlock; removes the "unsupported generalized block %T" runtime error path.
5. Sentinel misuse: empty name, nil plant, empty analysis point, invalid location, unsupported block type all wrap ErrDimensionMismatch (lines 24, 54, 70, 99, 110, 140, 143, 162-168, 217). Use ErrInvalidArgument. AnalysisPoint lookups (103, 197) return "%q: %w" without an "Op:" prefix.
6. Docs missing: NumericBlock, TunableBlock, GeneralizedModel, NewGeneralizedModel, SetInputName/SetOutputName/InsertAnalysisPoint/HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem, GeneralizedClosedLoop, NewGeneralizedClosedLoop, AnalysisPoint (method), OpenLoop, ClosedLoop, ComplementarySensitivity, Sensitivity, AnalysisPointLocation constants. Document that ClosedLoop == ComplementarySensitivity.

data.title: FreqResponse/Bode/Sigma/Nichols results alias caller's omega slice
data.body:
Checklist 4 (aliasing). doc.go promises returned slices are caller-owned and inputs are copied unless documented otherwise.

- frequency.go:368-370 `frequencyEvaluator.matrix` -> newFreqResponseMatrix(data, omega, ...) stores caller's omega as FreqResponseMatrix.Omega (FreqResponse, FreqResponsePointwise).
- frequency.go:651-660 `freqResponseLFT` same.
- frequency.go:57-91 `bodeResultFromResponse/bodeResultFromAccessor` store `omega` directly as BodeResult.Omega (Bode).
- frequency.go:815-822 Nichols reuses bode.Omega (inherits alias).
- frequency.go:857,865,882 Sigma stores caller omega as SigmaResult.Omega.
- freqrestest.go:248-253, 371-376, 423-427: FreqRespEstResult.Omega and FreqRespEstResult.H.Omega are the same backing slice (mutating one mutates the other).

Repro:
  w := []float64{1, 2}; resp,_ := sys.FreqResponse(w); b,_ := sys.Bode(w,0); sg,_ := sys.Sigma(w,0); w[0] = 99
  -> resp.Omega=[99 2] bode.Omega=[99 2] sigma.Omega=[99 2]

Fix: copy omega once at the public entry (FreqResponse/FreqResponsePointwise/Bode/Sigma/Nichols) — e.g. route matrix() through newFreqResponseMatrixOwned — and give FreqRespEstResult.Omega its own copy (or drop the duplicated field). Add a regression test mutating the input after the call.

data.title: TotalDelay returns nil *mat.Dense when model has no external delay
data.body:
Rule: no nil value meaning "none" with nil error/absent error.

delay.go:154-156 `(*System).TotalDelay()` -> delay_topology.go:52 totalExternal -> delay.go:158-164 effectiveIODelayMatrix returns nil when no Input/Output/IO delay or p==0||m==0. Exported, undocumented. MATLAB totaldelay(sys) returns a p×m matrix (zeros when no delay).

Repro: delay-free 1x1 sys -> `sys.TotalDelay() == nil` is true.

Fix: TotalDelay returns a fresh p×m zero matrix when there is no external delay (decide and document behaviour for p==0||m==0 — error is not possible with current signature; either keep signature and return p×m zero (fine when p,m>0) or change to (*mat.Dense, error) and return ErrDimensionMismatch for zero-dimension models per W7OUGJ precedent). Internal callers that test `!= nil` (transfer.go:149, response.go:110, simulate.go:281, frequency.go sweepInto/applyIODelay*) should use the internal effectiveIODelayMatrix/hasExternalDelay instead of the public method. Add doc comment.

data.title: GetDelayModel discards PullDelaysToLFT error and silently drops external delays
data.body:
Checklist 1/2 (swallowed error, partial result with no error).

delay.go:1482-1518 `(*System).GetDelayModel() (H *System, tau []float64)`: on `PullDelaysToLFT` error it falls back to (a) `sys.Copy(), nil` when LFT==nil, or (b) an H built only from the existing internal delays — Input/Output/IO delays are dropped from H/tau. Signature has no error, so callers (connect.go:1310, feedback_lft.go:17-18, lft.go:224-225, delay.go:350) cannot detect it. Also: redundant condition `!sys.HasDelay() && !sys.HasInternalDelay()` (HasDelay already covers internal). Undocumented exported method.

No runtime repro: current PullDelaysToLFT error paths (residual split via newResidualDelaySplit.apply) are hard to trigger, so the fallback is near-dead — but the API cannot express failure and the fallback returns a wrong model if it ever triggers.

Fix: MATLAB `[H,tau] = getDelayModel(sys)` -> `func (sys *System) GetDelayModel() (H *System, tau []float64, err error)`; propagate PullDelaysToLFT error with "GetDelayModel: %w"; delete fallback. Update the 5 internal callers. Add doc comment (H partition layout, tau semantics; tau empty only when the model has no delays — document that as the valid "no delays" value).

data.title: SetDelayModel/SetInternalDelay validation gaps: NaN/fractional tau accepted, empty tau builds zero-channel LFT that panics ZeroDelayApprox
data.body:
Checklist 1/3.

1. delay.go:1548-1561 `SetDelayModel(H, tau)` validates only `v<0` and `v==0`; NaN, ±Inf, and non-integer tau for discrete H are accepted, unlike SetInternalDelay (delay.go:69 validateSliceDelay -> validateDelayValue). Errors are bare ErrNegativeDelay/ErrZeroInternalDelay (no "SetDelayModel:" prefix / index).
   Repro: discrete H (dt=0.1, n=1, m=p=2): SetDelayModel(H, []float64{1.5}) -> ok, err=nil; SetDelayModel(H, []float64{NaN}) -> ok, err=nil.
2. delay.go:62-89 `SetInternalDelay(tau, ...)`: `tau == nil` clears; non-nil empty `[]float64{}` installs `&LFTDelay{Tau: []}` with zero-size blocks. `ZeroDelayApprox` (delay.go:2021-2029) then does mat.NewDense(0,0) and panics.
   Repro: s.SetInternalDelay([]float64{}, nil,nil,nil,nil,nil) -> err=nil, LFT!=nil; s.ZeroDelayApprox() -> PANIC "mat: zero length in matrix dimension".
   Also ZeroDelayApprox guards on `sys.LFT == nil` instead of HasInternalDelay()/internalDelayCount()==0.

Fix: share one validator (validateSliceDelay + nonzero check) between SetInternalDelay and SetDelayModel, wrapping with "SetDelayModel: tau[%d]=%g: %w". Treat len(tau)==0 in SetInternalDelay as clear (LFT=nil) or reject with ErrInvalidArgument — never store an empty LFT. Guard ZeroDelayApprox with internalDelayCount()==0. Add doc comments to SetDelayModel/SetInternalDelay/ZeroDelayApprox/MinimalLFT (MATLAB setDelayModel(H,tau)).

data.title: AbsorbDelay silently treats unknown/extra scopes as AbsorbAll; continuous path silently Pade-approximates
data.body:
Checklist 1/5/7.

delay.go:230-282 `(*System).AbsorbDelay(scopes ...AbsorbScope)`:
- Unknown scope string falls to `default:` => absorbs everything. Repro: discrete sys with InputDelay=[2]: AbsorbDelay("bogus") -> n grows 2->4, err=nil.
- Only scopes[0] is read; scopes[1:] silently ignored (variadic used as optional arg).
- For continuous models every scope silently becomes a Pade(DefaultPadeOrder=5) approximation (absorbInputDelayContinuous etc.), so the result is not exact; undocumented. MATLAB absorbDelay: verify whether it accepts continuous ss at all — if it errors, return ErrWrongDomain for continuous; if not, document the approximation and require the caller to choose (e.g. point to Pade(order)).
- AbsorbScope type, its constants, DefaultPadeOrder (untyped const in the same block) and AbsorbDelay have no doc comments.

Fix: validate scope -> `fmt.Errorf("AbsorbDelay: unknown scope %q: %w", s, ErrInvalidArgument)`; reject len(scopes)>1 with ErrInvalidArgument (or change to a single optional arg form consistent with MATLAB absorbDelay(sys)); decide continuous behaviour as above; document. Move DefaultPadeOrder out of the AbsorbScope const block.

data.title: Reduce/ModalTruncate: invalid enum and out-of-range options accepted silently
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

1. minimal.go:29-136 Reduce: opts.Mode outside {ReduceAll, ReduceUncontrollable, ReduceUnobservable} skips both staircase branches and returns the full model as "reduced", nil error.
   Repro (confirmed): s.Reduce(&ReduceOpts{Mode: ReduceMode(7)}) -> err=nil, Order=2 (unchanged).
   Fix: validate Mode up front -> fmt.Errorf("Reduce: unknown mode %d: %w", mode, ErrInvalidArgument). Also validate Tol (negative/NaN) before the n==0 early return so validation does not depend on model order.
2. minimal.go ReduceResult.BlockSizes: populated only for ReduceAll/ReduceUncontrollable with n>0, m>0; nil for n==0 / m==0 / p==0 and zeroOrderResult paths; [] (empty) for ReduceUnobservable. Same field means "staircase block sizes" or "not computed". Either always compute (empty slice only when the controllable part is truly empty) or drop the field from the default result and make it an opt-in request. Document.
3. modal_reduction.go:40-46 ModalTruncate: n==0 returns before opts.Order is validated, so Order:5 on a static gain succeeds (confirmed: err=nil). Validate options before the n==0 shortcut (Order must be 0 or <= n).
4. modal_reduction.go:45, 62: bare ErrInvalidOrder without "ModalTruncate:" context (confirmed message "controlsys: reduction order out of range").
5. Gram bad GramType -> bare ErrDimensionMismatch is covered in the Gram task (Q3KILR).

data.title: ModalTruncateOptions.MaxRealPart zero value doubles as 'unset'; threshold 0 cannot be requested; Kept/Method fields are constant noise
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit). Zero-value usefulness / placeholder semantics.

File: modal_reduction.go:14-27, 52, 181-207.

Current:
- ModalTruncateOptions{Order int; MaxRealPart float64}. `threshold := opts.Order == 0 && opts.MaxRealPart != 0`, and modalReductionOrder treats MaxRealPart==0 as "not set". A threshold at 0 (keep modes with Re >= 0, a natural cut) is therefore unrequestable; 0 silently falls back to the default n/2 order.
- When both Order>0 and MaxRealPart!=0 are set, Order silently wins (conflicting options accepted).
- ModalReductionResult.Kept is always rangeInts(order) (indices into the reordered Schur basis, not into any caller-visible mode list) -> carries no information.
- ModalReductionResult.Method is always the constant "real-schur-modal-truncate".
- n==0 returns Basis/Projection = &mat.Dense{} and nil Kept/KeptPoles (follow W7OUGJ for n==0 shape).

Fix:
- Make the selection explicit, e.g. MaxRealPart *float64 or a Selection enum {ByOrder, ByMaxRealPart} so 0 is a valid threshold; error with ErrInvalidArgument when both selections are given.
- Remove Kept and Method (or make Kept meaningful: indices into sys.Poles() order).
- MATLAB-shape note: MATLAB reducespec(sys,"modal")/freqsep/modalsep; keep argument shape close (sys, order) with options struct for the rest.
- Document ModalTruncate, ModalTruncateOptions, ModalReductionResult (currently undocumented).

data.title: Sigma/singular values: NaN placeholders for undetermined sigma_i at poles and on Dsyev failure
data.body:
Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

Root cause: frequency_svd.go:100-124 complexSVDWorkspace.singularValues (and singularValuesFromFlat/Nested) has no error return. At a pole (an Inf response entry) it writes sigma_1=+Inf and NaN for sigma_2..; when Dsyev fails it writes NaN for every value. Both are placeholders meaning "unknown", returned with nil error.

Reaches public API:
- System.Sigma (frequency.go:875-882 via sampled_response.go:58-64).
  Repro (confirmed): 2x2 A=[0 1;-1 0], B=C=I, D=0; sys.Sigma([]float64{1}, 0) -> err=nil, At(0,0)=+Inf, At(0,1)=NaN.
- FRD peak gain (frd.go:325-335) compares sv[0] > gain, silently skipping NaN.
- sigmaMaxPointwise (norms.go:655-679) needs explicit NaN special-casing.

Fix options:
- Give singularValues an error return; Dsyev failure -> ErrSchurFailed (wrapped with op context); callers propagate.
- At a pole: return all singular values that are determinable; MATLAB sigma at an exact pole reports Inf for the gain - decide whether all sigma_i become +Inf or Sigma returns an error for that grid point (e.g. ErrSingularTransform "frequency hits a pole"). Either way no NaN in a nil-error result.
- maximumFromFlat's (float64, bool) is internal ok-idiom; fold it into the error-returning form for consistency.

data.title: buildDelayBank returns (nil, nil) when no fractional delay; callers branch on nil bank
data.body:
Checklist 1 (unexported code included).

delay_bank.go:61-64 `buildDelayBank`: `if spec.requiresFractionalModel && !hasFractionalSampleDelay(...) { return nil, nil }`. Reached via buildContinuousDelayBank (delay_bank.go:28) from convert.go:257 and convert.go:271, which test `bank != nil`. delay_conversion_policy.go:171 and :184 also test `bank != nil` on buildContinuousPadeDelayBank results that are never nil (dead checks from the same convention). Also buildDelayBank with channels==0 returns (nil, nil) (loop never assigns bank).

Fix: make the "needs a fractional model?" decision a separate predicate at the caller (hasFractionalSampleDelay(contDelay/dt)) and have buildDelayBank always return a non-nil system or an error (channels==0 -> ErrDimensionMismatch). Drop the dead `bank != nil` checks.

data.title: CtrbF/ObsvF: nil optional matrix yields nil/empty result fields; missing MATLAB T/k outputs and tol arg
data.body:
Checklist 1/5. MATLAB: [Abar,Bbar,Cbar,T,k] = ctrbf(A,B,C,tol), [Abar,Bbar,Cbar,T,k] = obsvf(A,B,C,tol) — C (resp. B) is required.

ctrbobsv.go:81-99 `CtrbF(A,B,C)`: C may be nil -> StaircaseResult.C == nil with nil error (nil field meaning "not requested").
ctrbobsv.go:101-155 `ObsvF(A,B,C)`: B may be nil -> res.B = &mat.Dense{} (0x0 placeholder); also n==0 -> res.C = &mat.Dense{}.
Repro: ObsvF(A, nil, C) -> B dims 0x0 err=nil; CtrbF(A, B, nil) -> C nil=true err=nil.
Neither returns the transformation T (MATLAB output 4) nor accepts tol (ControllabilityStaircase supports tol; hard-coded 0). StaircaseResult (staircase.go, other group) exposes BlockSizes/NCont instead of MATLAB's k.

Fix: require all of A,B,C (nil -> ErrInvalidArgument with "CtrbF:" prefix); add tol float64 argument (0 = default, document); return T (and k per MATLAB semantics) in the result. Coordinate StaircaseResult field changes with the staircase.go owner. Errors currently bare ErrDimensionMismatch (see the op-prefix task).

data.title: Zero-dimension results with nil error in Covar (p==0) and Ctrb/Obsv (n==0)
data.body:
Same pattern as W7OUGJ (done: Care/Dare/Lqr/Lqe now error for n==0).

- covar.go:47-49 `Covar`: p==0 -> `&mat.Dense{}` (0x0) nil error. Repro: n=1,m=1,p=0 model -> Covar returns 0x0, err=nil. (m==0 -> zero p×p is a valid value; keep.)
- ctrbobsv.go:19-21 `Ctrb`: n==0 -> `&mat.Dense{}`; ctrbobsv.go:49-51 `Obsv`: same.
- Sigma nSV==0 handled in PIVD5W.
