data.title: Poly.Roots hangs on NaN/Inf coefficients and returns (nil,nil) for the zero polynomial
data.body:
poly.go:154-195 (Poly.Roots); related Degree :15, Equal :239, Monic :73.

1. Non-finite coefficients hang forever (checklist 3): Poly{1, math.NaN(), 2}.Roots() builds a companion matrix with NaN and calls mat.Eigen.Factorize, which loops forever in gonum Dgebal (gonum task ZHVHGX). Repro: probe test timed out after 60s at poly.go:181. Fix here regardless of gonum: reject non-finite coefficients up front with fmt.Errorf("Roots: non-finite coefficient %d: %w", i, ErrInvalidArgument). pidTuningIdealStable (pid_tuning.go:635) feeds computed polynomials into Roots.
2. Zero / empty polynomial (checklist 1): Poly{0,0}.Roots() and Poly{}.Roots() return (nil, nil) - "every s is a root" reported as "no roots". Constant nonzero -> empty root set is fine; the zero polynomial should return an error (ErrInvalidArgument). MATLAB roots([0 0]) returns [] but the user rule overrides MATLAB empties.
3. Representation consistency: Degree() does not trim leading zeros (Poly{0,0,1}.Degree()==2 while Roots trims), Degree of Poly{} is -1, Equal compares raw lengths (Poly{0,1}.Equal(Poly{1},0)==false), Mul of empty returns Poly{} but Derivative returns Poly{0}. Document the canonical zero polynomial and normalize, or document that methods are coefficient-wise.
4. Monic uses ad-hoc errors.New without sentinel (:75,:78) -> wrap ErrInvalidArgument with "Monic:" prefix. Roots returns bare ErrSingularTransform (:182) -> "Roots: %w".
Tests: NaN/Inf rejected promptly; zero poly errors; callers (rationalChannelFromPolynomials, pidTuningIdealStable) unaffected.

data.title: Poly.MulTo/AddTo silently corrupt result when dst aliases p or q
data.body:
poly.go:96-140 (exported Poly.MulTo, Poly.AddTo). Checklist 4 (aliasing).

Current: MulTo zeroes dst before reading p/q; AddTo writes dst[i] while later reading p[i-shift]. With dst sharing backing storage with p (the natural in-place use of a *To API) results are wrong with nil error.
Repro (probe):
  p := make(Poly, 2, 10); p[0], p[1] = 1, 2
  p.MulTo(p, Poly{1, 3})    // want [1 5 6], got [0 0 0]
  a := make(Poly, 1, 10); a[0] = 5
  a.AddTo(a, Poly{1, 2, 3}) // want [1 2 8], got [1 2 4]
Fix: detect overlap and fall back to a fresh buffer, or document "dst must not alias p or q" (no doc comments exist today) and panic on overlap as gonum/mat does. ScaleTo is alias-safe; document it. Check the internal callers (1 MulTo, 2 AddTo) for aliasing.

data.title: Pidtune (legacy): NaN/negative options accepted, requested phase margin silently clamped, swallowed errors
data.body:
pidtune.go. Checklists 1, 2, 5.

Repros (probe, plant 1/(s+1)):
- Pidtune(sys, PidtunePI, PidtuneOptions{PhaseMargin: NaN}) -> &PID{Kp:NaN, Ki:NaN}, err=nil.
- PidtuneOptions{CrossoverFrequency: -3} (or NaN) -> silently treated as "auto" (findCrossoverFreq :65 only tests > 0), err=nil.
- PidtuneOptions{CrossoverFrequency: 1, PhaseMargin: 179} -> returns a PI whose actual PM is 132 deg, err=nil: computePI/computePD/computePID/computePIDF (:187-:338) clamp the controller phase to +-0.05 rad of the family's range without reporting; only PDF (:174) errors when unattainable.
Swallowed errors:
- evalPlantAt (:99-105) maps any FreqResponse error to 0, then computePIDGains reports a misleading "zero or infinite gain".
- findCrossoverFreq: Bandwidth error ignored (:77), `poles, _ := plant.Poles()` (:82), final fallback returns a magic 1.0 rad/s (:96) with nil error.
API shape: `opts ...PidtuneOptions` is a variadic used as an optional struct; opts[1:] silently ignored. MATLAB is pidtune(sys,type,wc,opts) - make wc positional (0 = auto is acceptable zero value, negative/NaN -> ErrInvalidArgument) and opts a *PidtuneOptions.
Errors: lowercase "pidtune:" prefix and no sentinel (:47,:130,:137,:175) -> "Pidtune: ...: %w" with ErrInvalidArgument / ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable.
Fix: validate PM in (0,180) and finite; error (ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable) when the requested phase is outside the family's reachable range instead of clamping; propagate evaluation errors; decide whether the 1 rad/s fallback is an error. MATLAB returns info.PhaseMargin/Stable as optional outputs - if wanted, add an opt-in info result rather than silent clamping. Note Pidtune duplicates TunePID; consider deprecating one (report-only).

data.title: TunePID/TunePIDFRD/FitProcess return a non-nil result together with a non-nil error
data.body:
pid_tuning.go:240, :432; process_identification.go:276-277 (and doc :174). Checklist 1.

Current:
- tunePID returns &PIDTuningResult{Evidence: ...} with ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable (one-gain margin failure :240, no feasible candidate :432). Callers must inspect both.
- FitProcess on context cancellation returns (best, ctx.Err()) - "A canceled/exhausted run returns its best valid result" - value AND error.
Why: user rule - value with nil error XOR non-nil error.
Fix: introduce typed errors that carry the diagnostic payload and unwrap to the sentinel, e.g.
  type PIDTuningError struct{ Evidence PIDTuningEvidence; Err error } // Unwrap -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable
  type ProcessFitCanceledError struct{ Best *ProcessFitResult; Err error } // Unwrap -> ctx.Err() (context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded)
and return (nil, err). errors.As gives callers the evidence/best fit. Remove PIDTuningEvidence.Feasible (always true on success once failures are errors) and the SeedObjective=0 placeholder reset at :431. Also add "controlsys:" prefix to ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable/ErrProcess* messages for consistency with errors.go.
Tests: errors.Is(err, ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable) and errors.As(&PIDTuningError) on an unattainable design; FitProcess with a pre-canceled ctx returns nil result.

data.title: TunePID: swallowed errors in stability checks, ignored UnstablePoles, stringly-typed evidence enums
data.body:
pid_tuning.go. Checklists 1, 2, 5.

Swallowed errors (each turns a numerical failure into "candidate unstable" or a silent downgrade of the stability certificate):
- :108 plant.AbsorbDelay error ignored -> falls back to the sampled-only path silently.
- :115-131 p.stable closure maps controller.System/Feedback/IsStable errors to false; pidTuningHiddenModesStable (:576-583) and pidTuningIdealStable (:587-645, rationalTransferFunction and Roots errors) likewise. A failing IsStable can end the search in ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable with no cause.
- :693-700 pidTuningDelayStability treats any delayLoopFromSystem error as "outside scope". Use errors.Is(err, errDelayLoopUnsupported) for the scope case and propagate others (margin.go:620 shows the pattern); same for l.stableClosedLoop (:762).
Fix: make the stability predicate return (bool, error); abort tuning with a wrapped error on genuine failures.
Options/evidence shape:
- PIDTuningOptions.UnstablePoles is documented "for FRD" and is silently ignored by TunePID(System) - reject with ErrOptionUnsupported when non-nil on the System path.
- PIDTuningEvidence.Stability ("closed-loop-poles" / "nyquist-encirclement" / "sampled-frequency-only") and Termination ("converged"/"round-limit"/"evaluation-limit") are stringly-typed; define typed constants (type PIDStabilityEvidence string; const ...). AchievedCrossover always equals wc (:440).
- tunePID errors use no sentinel (:146-:270 "TunePID: ..."; TunePIDFRD :16-:39) -> wrap ErrInvalidArgument. nil ctx error (:81, frd :16) has no sentinel.
- Docs missing on PIDDesignFocus, PIDTuningOptions (zero-value defaults: wc auto, PM 60 or plant's for one-gain families, MaxEvaluations 4096), PIDTuningObjective, PIDTuningEvidence, PIDTuningResult.

data.title: PID constructors: unvalidated NewPID/NewPID2, NewPID2 drops WithFilter, Ti/Td return 0 when undefined, pidstd args differ from MATLAB
data.body:
pid.go. Checklists 1, 2, 5, 7.

Repros (probe):
- NewPID2(1,1,1,0.1,1,1, WithFilter(5)).Tf == 0.1: options are applied to a throwaway PID (:155-160), so WithFilter (and any non-Dt/formula option) is silently dropped.
- NewPID(0,1,1): Ti()==0 (Kp/Ki) and Td()==0 although Standard() correctly errors ("no standard form"). Ti/Td return placeholder values for a non-representable controller. Make them (float64, error), or document that they are defined only when Standard() succeeds and return an error otherwise.
- NewPID/NewPID2 accept NaN/Inf/negative Tf/Dt; errors surface only later in System(). NewPIDStd validates. Make constructors consistent (all validate and return error) - user rule "constructors validating".
MATLAB shape: pid(Kp,Ki,Kd,Tf,Ts), pidstd(Kp,Ti,Td,N,Ts), pid2(Kp,Ki,Kd,Tf,b,c,Ts). NewPIDStd's filter is set via WithFilter(Tf) while MATLAB pidstd takes the derivative divisor N (Tf = Td/N); doc comment at :71 shows Td*s/(Tf*s+1). Consider NewPIDStd(Kp, Ti, Td, N, opts...) and positional Tf in NewPID to match MATLAB.
Errors: every error in pid.go is fmt.Errorf without %w (:76,:79,:104,:171,:185,:300,:304,:307,:354) -> wrap ErrInvalidArgument (ErrImproperModel for the Tf=0 derivative).
Other: Parallel() panics on nil receiver while Copy() handles nil; exported ForwardEuler/BackwardEuler/Trapezoidal are unprefixed package-level names (borderline; collision risk with discretization methods). Docs missing: PIDForm, WithPIDFormulas, PID, PIDOption, WithFilter, WithTs, NewPID, NewPID2, (*PID).System.

data.title: Nyquist: returns an encirclement count when -1 lies on the contour; user omega not validated
data.body:
nyquist.go. Checklists 1, 3, 7.

1. Ill-defined count reported as fact: windingNumber (:644-670) skips samples within 1e-15 of -1 and rounds the total angle. For L = 8/(s+1)^3 (closed-loop poles exactly at +-j*sqrt(3), marginally stable) Nyquist(nil,0) returns Encirclements=2, RHPZerosCL=2, err=nil - claims two unstable closed-loop poles. The doc promises the count "never depends on omega" but says nothing about 1+L vanishing on the contour. Fix: when min|1+L| along the sampled contour is below a tolerance relative to max|L| (or a refine step cannot resolve the phase because |1+L|~0), return an error (e.g. fmt.Errorf("Nyquist: closed loop has poles on the stability boundary: %w", ErrSingularTransform/new sentinel)). Check delayLoop.nyquist / 3FLWHX for the analogous delay path.
2. User omega: Nyquist([]float64{}, 0) returns Omega/Contour empty with nil error; Nyquist([]float64{-1, NaN}, 0) returns NaN contour samples with nil error. Validate omega (non-empty, finite, >= 0, <= pi/dt for discrete) with ErrInvalidArgument; omega==nil remains "auto". Check whether PIVD5W (FreqResponse empty omega) already changes FreqResponse - Nyquist only calls FreqResponse when len(omega)>0.
3. nPoints<=0 silently means 500; negative should be ErrInvalidArgument (MATLAB nyquist has no nPoints argument; keep as Go extension but validate).
4. NyquistResult has no doc comment.

data.title: Passivity: eigen failure reported as conclusive violation; redundant Status/Passive; dead PassivityCertified; wrong sentinels
data.body:
passivity.go. Checklists 1, 2, 5, 7.

- minHermitianPart (:251-254): if EigenSym.Factorize fails it returns -Inf, so FRDPassive reports Status=PassivityViolated ("conclusive sampled counterexample") with nil error. Propagate an error (ErrSchurFailed / ErrSingularTransform) instead.
- PassivityResult carries both Status and Passive bool (Passive == Status != PassivityViolated): double signalling; drop Passive or derive via a method.
- PassivityCertified is exported but never produced anywhere in the package (grep): dead API promising a capability that does not exist. Remove it, or implement the certificate.
- Passive's "Deprecated:" line (:36) is in the same paragraph as the summary, so go doc/staticcheck do not recognise the deprecation; needs a blank // line before it.
- Wrong sentinels: delayed systems rejected with ErrDescriptorUnsupported (:52, :137) -> ErrDelayUnsupported; invalid Tol / omega values / unsorted grid (:194, :209, :212, :215) use ErrDimensionMismatch -> ErrInvalidArgument; nil system (:46, :130) -> ErrInvalidArgument.
- SpectralFactor (:129-162) is a stub ("only static gain models are supported by this tracer") that rejects every dynamic model with ErrDimensionMismatch and non-diagonal D likewise. Either implement (MATLAB spectralfact) or return ErrOptionUnsupported-style "not implemented" sentinel, and document the restriction.
- Docs missing: PassivityOptions (Tol 0 -> 1e-9, Omega nil -> 121-point grid), PassivityResult, FRDPassive, SpectralFactor.
MATLAB shape: isPassive(sys)/getPassiveIndex(sys); report-only.

data.title: AssemblePhysical: NewPhysicalComponent does not validate (nil System placeholder); wrong sentinels throughout
data.body:
physical_assembly.go. Checklists 1, 2, 5, 7.

Constructor should be (PhysicalComponent, error) and validate name, sys (Validate), port names/dimensions/channels - the checks currently in bindPorts.

data.title: Time responses/DCGain return empty or nil outputs with nil error for models without inputs or outputs
data.body:
response.go. Checklist 1. Related: QLW7SM (Simulate Y nil for p==0), 6K4CVZ, PVX7Q5.

Repros (probe, sys = New(A=-1, B=1, C=nil, D=nil, 0): n=1, m=1, p=0):
- sys.DCGain() -> 0x0 &mat.Dense{} with nil error (:382-384, documented "returned as an empty matrix").
- Step(sys,1) -> TimeResponse{Y: &mat.Dense{}} nil error (simulatedInputResponse :215-216); Impulse same.
- Initial(sys,x0,1) -> TimeResponse{Y: nil} nil error (:892-893 returns &mat.Dense{}; continuous path continuousFreeSamples :956-957 returns (nil, nil)).
- Lsim(sys, u, t, nil) -> Y nil, nil error.
Internal: impulseAsStepModel (:807-808) returns (nil, nil) and the caller treats nil as "no derived model"; continuousFreeSamples returns (nil, nil) for p==0 || steps==0.
Fix: per user rule (MATLAB empties overridden) return fmt.Errorf("Op: model has no outputs: %w", ErrDimensionMismatch) (or a dedicated sentinel) from DCGain/Step/Impulse/Initial/Lsim when m==0 or p==0 as appropriate (Initial needs p>0 only; Lsim with m==0 already special-cased). Make impulseAsStepModel return (model, ok) or an error rather than (nil, nil). Update DCGain doc.

data.title: Silent argument coercion: Step/Impulse/Initial negative tFinal -> auto; Pade order unchecked for delay-free models
data.body:
response.go:147-163 (timeResponsePlanner.grid), pade.go:10-31. Checklists 1, 5.

- Step(sys, -5) returns the auto-horizon response (probe: last T = 7) with nil error; tFinal <= 0 is the "auto" sentinel, so negative values are coerced. MATLAB step(sys,Tfinal) requires Tfinal > 0. Keep 0 as the documented zero-value "auto" (doc it on Step/Impulse/Initial, currently undocumented) and reject tFinal < 0 with ErrInvalidArgument. validateTimeHorizon (:136-141) also lacks a sentinel.
- sys.Pade(-5) on a delay-free model returns sys.Copy(), nil (:14-16, :22-24); order is validated only inside PadeDelay. Validate order (1..10) up front. PadeDelay's order error uses ErrDimensionMismatch (:112) -> ErrInvalidArgument; validateDelayValue error unprefixed (:108-109) -> "PadeDelay: %w".
- Docs missing on (*System).Pade and PadeDelay. MATLAB pade(sys,N) / [num,den]=pade(T,N): shapes OK.

data.title: StepMetric and DampInfo use NaN/Inf/0 placeholders for undefined metrics
data.body:
response_info.go:20-29, :165-176, :226, :241; response.go:42-47, :694-733. Checklist 1.

- StepMetric.RiseTime = NaN when the response never crosses the rise limits; SettlingTime = NaN plus Settled=false when not settled (NaN placeholder AND bool double signalling). MATLAB stepinfo returns NaN, but the user rule forbids NaN "unknown" placeholders.
  Proposed: StepInfo returns an error wrapping a new sentinel (e.g. ErrResponseNotSettled / ErrMetricUndefined) naming the row and metric when a metric is undefined, so callers lengthen tFinal; or make undefined metrics an opt-in request that errors when unavailable. Remove Settled.
- Damp: DampInfo.Tau = +Inf for poles that are marginal or unstable (probe: pole 2 -> Zeta=-1, Tau=+Inf; pole 0 -> Zeta=0, Tau=+Inf). +Inf as "not applicable" for unstable poles is a placeholder (the growth time constant is 1/sigma < 0 in MATLAB's damp printout). Zeta for a pole at the origin is 0 here; verify against MATLAB damp (zeta = -cos(angle(p)) gives -1) before changing.
  Proposed: Tau = -1/real(s) (signed, as MATLAB displays) or drop Tau (MATLAB [wn,zeta,p]=damp returns no Tau) and add a method that errors for non-decaying poles.
- Damp returns (nil, nil) for static gains (empty pole set) - acceptable (true empty set) but document.
- Docs missing: StepInfoOptions (zero-value defaults), StepInfoResult (row layout input-major, rows = input*p+output), StepMetric, StepInfo, TimeResponse (Y layout), DampInfo, Damp. StepInfo validate() errors (:119,:122,:132) have no sentinel -> ErrInvalidArgument.

data.title: RiccatiWorkspace: undersized workspace panics; shared mutable state undocumented
data.body:
riccati.go:12-89, Care :100-264, Dare :275-373 (fix site for validation: newRiccatiProblem in matrix_equation_problem.go, group 3 - dedupe with auditor 3). Checklists 3, 4, 7, 8.

Repro (probe):
  Care(A3x3, B3x1, Q, R, &RiccatiOpts{Workspace: NewRiccatiWorkspace(1, 1)})
  -> panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:9] with capacity 1 (ws.rChol/aWork slicing)
Kalman/Lqe/Kalmd forward opts.Workspace to the dual problem, where the required size is (n, p) not (n, m) - easy to get wrong.
Fix: record (n, m) in RiccatiWorkspace and have newRiccatiProblem return fmt.Errorf("Care: workspace sized for n=%d m=%d, need ...: %w", ErrDimensionMismatch) (or grow it).
Also:
- Care/Dare grow ws.work in place (:196-199, :460-462, :574-576, :600-602) and results X/K/Eig alias workspace storage: a workspace must not be shared across goroutines - document on RiccatiWorkspace/RiccatiOpts.
- Bare sentinel returns without "Care:"/"Dare:" prefix (:116, :204, :207, :220, :291, :313, :351, :507-510, :607-614) - include in the group-4 error-hygiene task if preferred.
- Docs missing: RiccatiWorkspace, NewRiccatiWorkspace (which n/m for Kalman), RiccatiOpts, RiccatiResult (Rcnd meaning; X may be inaccurate when Rcnd is tiny - MATLAB care warns/errors; borderline).
Not duplicated: W7OUGJ (n==0) and HONY6M (Care Rcnd).

data.title: MATLAB arg shape: Estim treats all plant inputs as known; Kalman/Lqe take Nn via RiccatiOpts.S
data.body:
observer.go. Checklist 5 (MATLAB-matching arguments).

- Estim(sys, L) (:263-315) builds an estimator with inputs [u; y] (probe: plant m=1,p=1 -> estimator 2 inputs). MATLAB estim(sys,L) with no sensors/known treats every plant input as stochastic w, so the estimator input is y only; known inputs and measured outputs are selected with estim(sys,L,sensors,known). Verify against the MATLAB estim doc page, then make the signature Estim(sys, L, sensors, known []int) (nil = MATLAB defaults) or document the deviation explicitly. Same check for Reg(sys,K,L) vs reg(sys,K,L,sensors,known,controls) (defaults appear to match).
- Kalman(sys,Qn,Rn,opts) and Lqe(A,G,C,Qn,Rn,opts) take the noise cross-covariance N through RiccatiOpts.S, a field documented as the Riccati cross-term. MATLAB: kalman(sys,Qn,Rn,Nn) and lqe(A,G,C,Q,R,N) take N positionally. Consider an explicit Nn *mat.Dense argument (nil = 0) and keep RiccatiOpts for Workspace only.
- Bare sentinels without op prefix: Lqe :20, :25, :29; Estim :273; Kalmd :160 (ErrInvalidSampleTime).

data.title: FitProcess/EvaluateProcess: stringly-typed options/status and placeholder diagnostics
data.body:
process_identification.go. Checklists 1, 5, 7.

data.title: Discrete internal-delay and transfer/zpk frequency evaluation still use rounded e^{jωT}
data.body:
Follow-up to 3BAHMY (branch fix/discrete-unit-circle). 3BAHMY moved the state-space pencil onto the exact unit circle (timeDomain.frequencyPoint: z=(1+jν)/(1−jν), ν=tan(ωT/2); pencil pI+qA, G=c·C·X+D). Remaining off-circle evaluation points:

1. Internal delays (frequency.go evalFrLFTInto, frequency_pole.go evalFrLFTFrozenInto): Δ = z^{-τ} is formed by repeated division by the rounded s = cmplx.Exp(jωT); |Δ| is off by ~τε. When I − H22·Δ is nearly singular (a lightly damped closed-loop pole created by the delay loop), |G| moves by ~τε/d. Exact treatment needs the discrete delays absorbed as states (pole chain at z=0) so they enter the pencil, or an exact on-circle form of z^{-k}.
2. ZPK.FreqResponse (zpk.go ~line 125, s = cmplx.Exp), TransferFunc evaluation (transfer.go), pidtune.go:118, pid_tuning.go:460 evaluate rational/polynomial forms at a rounded e^{jωT}. Near a pole within d of the circle, (z − p) carries the radial ε error → ε/d relative error in |G|.
3. nyquist.go discreteHalf circle(θ) = cmplx.Exp(jθ): harmless for winding counts, listed for completeness.

Repro idea: frequency_test.go lightlyDampedDiscreteSys(gap=1e-9) converted with ZPK/TF and compared to frExactResponse at frExactPoint (200-bit oracle) → errors ~5e-9..8e-8 at ωT=0.003..3.11, while the SS path is ≤2e-10.

data.title: Use timeDomain.frequencyPoint in norms.go resolventScalars after #240 merges
data.body: PR #240 (fix/hinf-accuracy) adds sigmaEvaluator.resolventScalars in norms.go: (sI−A)^{-1} = c·(pI+qA)^{-1} with ν = tan(ωT/2) / μ = cot(ωT/2). The fix for 3BAHMY (branch fix/discrete-unit-circle) adds the same parametrisation as timeDomain.frequencyPoint (time_domain.go) for every FreqResponse/EvalFr/margin evaluation; it selects the branch by |tan(ωT/2)| ≤ 1 (valid for any ω sign/range) rather than half ≤ π/4. Once both are on main, make resolventScalars return td.frequencyPoint(w)'s p,q,c so all discrete evaluations share one helper. Also #240's norms_test.go oracle (bigComplex/exactSigmaMax) duplicates frequency_test.go frBig/frExactResponse; merge them.

data.title: Dense GEPP frequency solve loses ε/d accuracy near lightly damped poles when pivoting mixes rows
data.body:
Evidence from 3BAHMY (branch fix/discrete-unit-circle, frequency_test.go lightlyDampedDiscreteSys, gap 1e-9 from unit circle, |G| vs 200-bit oracle frExactResponse):
- Upper-Hessenberg modal model: balancedDense |G| rel err ≤ 1.6e-10 at ωT ∈ {0.003, 0.03, 3.11}.
- Same model with one extra coupling A[n-1][0]=0.7 (poles unchanged): FreqResponsePointwise (balancedDense GEPP) rises to ~1e-8 (ωT=0.03, 3.11); the refined Hessenberg sweep gets ~2e-9.
- Mid-band ωT≈1.4 or 2.2: ~1e-7 for every path (pencil entries O(1) there).
Cause: GEPP's componentwise backward error ε|L||U| is relative to pivoted rows of size O(1), not to the O(ωT) entries of the near-singular block; error ≈ ε/d. The Hessenberg refinement (frequency_hessenberg.go residual, working precision, refineStop=√ε) also stops short.
Possible fix: one refinement step with a compensated (dot2) residual against the original pencil in balancedDense and hessenbergSweep for discrete points near poles; benchmark cost. Not required for correctness; an accuracy improvement for lightly damped models.

data.title: FRD and other frequency entry points return empty values with nil error for empty omega

data.title: Validate rejects fractional discrete delays that Feedback/Append/Thiran paths accept
data.body:
System.Validate (ss.go validateSliceDelay/validateDelay) returns ErrFractionalDelay for non-integer discrete InputDelay/OutputDelay/IODelay, but interconnections and the Thiran feedback path deliberately accept such models (tests: TestFeedbackApprox_DiscreteFractionalDelayRequiresThiranOrder, TestZeroStateInternalDelayInterconnectionsHaveNoPhantomStates, architecture_prd95/prd103 tests build them by struct literal).
Consequence: requireSystem (require.go, which calls Validate) cannot be used at interconnection entry points (Series/Parallel/Append/BlkDiag/Feedback/Connect/Augstate); group-1 fixer used a nil-only requireSystems helper in connect.go instead (PR fix/idiom-g1-panics).
Decide: either fractional discrete delays are a valid model state (relax Validate, document in CONTEXT.md) or they are invalid (have Thiran paths take them via options rather than model fields). Then switch interconnects to requireSystem.

Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

File: generalized.go

1. GeneralizedModel.SetInputName/SetOutputName (lines 74-80) accept any count; CurrentSystem (108-123) then stamps them onto the System with nil error. Contrast System.SetInputName which errors on count mismatch.
   Repro (confirmed): g := NewGeneralizedModel("g", oneInputSys); g.SetInputName("a","b","c"); cs, err := g.CurrentSystem() -> err=nil, cs.InputName=[a b c] for a 1-input model (cs.Validate() also nil, so Validate does not catch it).
   Fix: validate in CurrentSystem (len must equal m/p, or single name expanded like System.SetInputName) and return ErrDimensionMismatch; or make the setters return error and validate against the block's current dims.
2. (*GeneralizedModel).InsertAnalysisPoint (82-87) panics on nil receiver (confirmed nil-pointer panic) while HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem on the same type are nil-safe. Also accepts empty name and records Location=Unspecified. Make it return error like GeneralizedClosedLoop.InsertAnalysisPoint (validate name, nil receiver).
3. NewGeneralizedClosedLoop copies plant (plant.Copy()) but stores a *System controller by reference via fixedSystemBlock; later caller mutation changes the loop.
   Repro (confirmed): ctrl.A=-2; cl := NewGeneralizedClosedLoop("cl", s, ctrl, "y"); ctrl.A.Set(0,0,-50); cl.OpenLoop("y").A changes from [-2 0;1 -1] to [-50 0;1 -1].
   Fix: numericBlockFromAny should copy *System (fixedSystemBlock{sys: b.Copy()}); same for NewGeneralizedModel. A typed-nil *System is accepted and only fails later in CurrentSystem; reject at construction.
4. API shape: block/controller parameters are `any` with a runtime type switch. Prefer a typed parameter: NumericBlock, with an exported adapter (e.g. FixedBlock(sys *System) NumericBlock) or making *System satisfy NumericBlock; removes the "unsupported generalized block %T" runtime error path.
5. Sentinel misuse: empty name, nil plant, empty analysis point, invalid location, unsupported block type all wrap ErrDimensionMismatch (lines 24, 54, 70, 99, 110, 140, 143, 162-168, 217). Use ErrInvalidArgument. AnalysisPoint lookups (103, 197) return "%q: %w" without an "Op:" prefix.
6. Docs missing: NumericBlock, TunableBlock, GeneralizedModel, NewGeneralizedModel, SetInputName/SetOutputName/InsertAnalysisPoint/HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem, GeneralizedClosedLoop, NewGeneralizedClosedLoop, AnalysisPoint (method), OpenLoop, ClosedLoop, ComplementarySensitivity, Sensitivity, AnalysisPointLocation constants. Document that ClosedLoop == ComplementarySensitivity.
- PR #250 (fix/idiom-g3-silent): items 1-3 done (names validated in CurrentSystem, InsertAnalysisPoint returns error, *System copied, typed-nil rejected, nil plant ErrInvalidArgument). Items 4-6 pending.

Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit). Static findings (no repro yet unless noted); each silently turns a failure into a plausible value with nil error.

margin.go
- 71-84 sisoEval.at: LFT path `h, _ := evalSISOFreqResponse(...)` drops the error and returns 0; non-LFT path turns evalWithPoleLimit errors into NaN+NaNi. These values flow into AllMargin (337-342) PhaseMargins/GainMargins and Bandwidth magnitudes with nil error. Fix: at(w) (complex128, error), propagate.
- 755-759 rationalLoop.boundaryRoots: p.Roots() error -> returns nil, i.e. "no crossings" -> AllMargin/Bandwidth report none with nil error. Propagate error.
- 507-516 Bandwidth refine closure: sys.Sigma error -> returns 0 (treated as a crossing value). Propagate (closure can capture first error and Bandwidth returns it).
- 678-709 newRationalLoop returns (nil, nil) to mean "no rational form" (internal, but violates the pattern; callers branch on nil). Return a sentinel or a bool-free separate predicate.

norms.go
- 198-200 hsvFromGramians: Dgesvd ok result ignored; unconverged SVD returns garbage HSV with nil error.
- 205-218 eigenvalueHSV: eig.Factorize failure returns make([]float64, n) (all zeros) as HSV. Return an error (ErrSchurFailed wrapped "HSV:").
- 681-685 hinfLowerBound: Poles error -> (0,0) fallback; acceptable as heuristic seed but should be documented or propagated.

hinfsyn.go
- 405-451 maxSVD: Dgesvd failure -> 0, used as gammaLB in hinfsyn_general.go:96-99 (underestimates the lower bound silently). Also duplicates norms.go maxSVDense; merge into one helper returning (float64, error).

lyapunov.go
- 421-422 and 495-496: `k := impl.Dgetc2(...); _ = k` - k>0 signals a perturbed (near-singular) pivot; result is silently a perturbed solution. Return ErrSingularEquation (or surface via scale) when k>0.

loopsens.go
- 65-68 makeIdentityGain: `sys, _ := NewGain(...)` swallows error (also used by generalized.go:242). Return (*System, error).

frequency_pole.go
- 101 poleSpacing: `poles, _ = ...poles(...)` drops error; spacing then defaults to |s| scale. Document or propagate.
- PR #254: norms.go HSV (Dgesvd/eigen failures), hinfsyn maxSVD merged into maxSingularValue, lyapunov Dgetc2 k>=0 -> ErrSingularEquation, makeIdentityGain/poleSpacing propagate, lowerBound documented. Remaining: margin.go items (sisoEval.at, boundaryRoots, Bandwidth refine, newRationalLoop nil,nil, maxSVDense swallowing) after #245.

data.title: Race CI suite near 10m go test timeout
data.body: CI runs `go test -v -count=1 -race ./...` with the default 10m timeout. On main the package already takes 435s under -race in CI (run 37260898953), and ~450s locally on an M1 Pro. Auditor 3 (Go idiom audit).

File: generalized.go

1. GeneralizedModel.SetInputName/SetOutputName (lines 74-80) accept any count; CurrentSystem (108-123) then stamps them onto the System with nil error. Contrast System.SetInputName which errors on count mismatch.
   Repro (confirmed): g := NewGeneralizedModel("g", oneInputSys); g.SetInputName("a","b","c"); cs, err := g.CurrentSystem() -> err=nil, cs.InputName=[a b c] for a 1-input model (cs.Validate() also nil, so Validate does not catch it).
   Fix: validate in CurrentSystem (len must equal m/p, or single name expanded like System.SetInputName) and return ErrDimensionMismatch; or make the setters return error and validate against the block's current dims.
2. (*GeneralizedModel).InsertAnalysisPoint (82-87) panics on nil receiver (confirmed nil-pointer panic) while HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem on the same type are nil-safe. Also accepts empty name and records Location=Unspecified. Make it return error like GeneralizedClosedLoop.InsertAnalysisPoint (validate name, nil receiver).
3. NewGeneralizedClosedLoop copies plant (plant.Copy()) but stores a *System controller by reference via fixedSystemBlock; later caller mutation changes the loop.
   Repro (confirmed): ctrl.A=-2; cl := NewGeneralizedClosedLoop("cl", s, ctrl, "y"); ctrl.A.Set(0,0,-50); cl.OpenLoop("y").A changes from [-2 0;1 -1] to [-50 0;1 -1].
   Fix: numericBlockFromAny should copy *System (fixedSystemBlock{sys: b.Copy()}); same for NewGeneralizedModel. A typed-nil *System is accepted and only fails later in CurrentSystem; reject at construction.
4. API shape: block/controller parameters are `any` with a runtime type switch. Prefer a typed parameter: NumericBlock, with an exported adapter (e.g. FixedBlock(sys *System) NumericBlock) or making *System satisfy NumericBlock; removes the "unsupported generalized block %T" runtime error path.
5. Sentinel misuse: empty name, nil plant, empty analysis point, invalid location, unsupported block type all wrap ErrDimensionMismatch (lines 24, 54, 70, 99, 110, 140, 143, 162-168, 217). Use ErrInvalidArgument. AnalysisPoint lookups (103, 197) return "%q: %w" without an "Op:" prefix.
6. Docs missing: NumericBlock, TunableBlock, GeneralizedModel, NewGeneralizedModel, SetInputName/SetOutputName/InsertAnalysisPoint/HasAnalysisPoint/AnalysisPoint/CurrentSystem, GeneralizedClosedLoop, NewGeneralizedClosedLoop, AnalysisPoint (method), OpenLoop, ClosedLoop, ComplementarySensitivity, Sensitivity, AnalysisPointLocation constants. Document that ClosedLoop == ComplementarySensitivity.

PR #240 (fix/hinf-accuracy) adds sigmaEvaluator.resolventScalars in norms.go: (sI−A)^{-1} = c·(pI+qA)^{-1} with ν = tan(ωT/2) / μ = cot(ωT/2). The fix for 3BAHMY (branch fix/discrete-unit-circle) adds the same parametrisation as timeDomain.frequencyPoint (time_domain.go) for every FreqResponse/EvalFr/margin evaluation; it selects the branch by |tan(ωT/2)| ≤ 1 (valid for any ω sign/range) rather than half ≤ π/4. Once both are on main, make resolventScalars return td.frequencyPoint(w)'s p,q,c so all discrete evaluations share one helper. Also #240's norms_test.go oracle (bigComplex/exactSigmaMax) duplicates frequency_test.go frBig/frExactResponse; merge them.
Correction: the final 3BAHMY fix (PR for fix/discrete-unit-circle) uses timeDomain.frequencyPoint with p = cos(ωT/2)+j·sin(ωT/2) (Sincos rounded), q = −conj(p), z = p/conj(p) exactly on the circle; explicit solvers keep sI−A off-diagonals and form only the diagonal as s−aᵢᵢ = (p+q·aᵢᵢ)·p (pt.shift); descriptor solvers use pE+qA, G scaled by −q. No ν/|tan|≤1 branch. Oracle: frequency_test.go frExactPoint/frExactResponse.

Follow-up to 3BAHMY (branch fix/discrete-unit-circle). 3BAHMY moved the state-space pencil onto the exact unit circle (timeDomain.frequencyPoint: z=(1+jν)/(1−jν), ν=tan(ωT/2); pencil pI+qA, G=c·C·X+D). Remaining off-circle evaluation points:

1. Internal delays (frequency.go evalFrLFTInto, frequency_pole.go evalFrLFTFrozenInto): Δ = z^{-τ} is formed by repeated division by the rounded s = cmplx.Exp(jωT); |Δ| is off by ~τε. When I − H22·Δ is nearly singular (a lightly damped closed-loop pole created by the delay loop), |G| moves by ~τε/d. Exact treatment needs the discrete delays absorbed as states (pole chain at z=0) so they enter the pencil, or an exact on-circle form of z^{-k}.
2. ZPK.FreqResponse (zpk.go ~line 125, s = cmplx.Exp), TransferFunc evaluation (transfer.go), pidtune.go:118, pid_tuning.go:460 evaluate rational/polynomial forms at a rounded e^{jωT}. Near a pole within d of the circle, (z − p) carries the radial ε error → ε/d relative error in |G|.
3. nyquist.go discreteHalf circle(θ) = cmplx.Exp(jθ): harmless for winding counts, listed for completeness.

Repro idea: frequency_test.go lightlyDampedDiscreteSys(gap=1e-9) converted with ZPK/TF and compared to frExactResponse at frExactPoint (200-bit oracle) → errors ~5e-9..8e-8 at ωT=0.003..3.11, while the SS path is ≤2e-10.
Correction: the final 3BAHMY fix (PR for fix/discrete-unit-circle) uses timeDomain.frequencyPoint with p = cos(ωT/2)+j·sin(ωT/2) (Sincos rounded), q = −conj(p), z = p/conj(p) exactly on the circle; explicit solvers keep sI−A off-diagonals and form only the diagonal as s−aᵢᵢ = (p+q·aᵢᵢ)·p (pt.shift); descriptor solvers use pE+qA, G scaled by −q. No ν/|tan|≤1 branch. Oracle: frequency_test.go frExactPoint/frExactResponse.

data.title: LFT nu/ny count external channels, MATLAB lft counts feedback channels
data.body:
Found while documenting lft.go (group 3 idiom docs, OEBWKD).

controlsys LFT(M, Delta, nu, ny): nu/ny are the numbers of M's UPPER (external) inputs/outputs kept; the remaining mM-nu inputs and pM-ny outputs close with Delta (lft.go:14-35: "M lower outputs pM-ny != Delta inputs"). Nil Delta extracts the upper channels.

MATLAB lft(sys1,sys2,nu,ny) (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/inputoutputmodel.lft.html): nu/ny are the numbers of sys1 inputs/outputs in the FEEDBACK loop (last nu inputs fed by sys2 outputs, last ny outputs feeding sys2). So the integer arguments mean the complement of MATLAB's; the idiom rule (MATLAB argument shapes) is violated, but switching is a SILENT semantic change for every caller (same types).

Callers: conversion_thiran.go:171 (LFT(rational, bank, m, p)); process-lab robust_synthesis.go:219, model_design_hinf_evidence.go:148, model_design_hinf_test.go:148,262,522 (pass len(Exogenous), len(Regulated)).

Decide: (a) switch to MATLAB meaning in v2 with a loud migration (e.g. rename parameters + Breaking (v2) note + process-lab tasks), or (b) keep and document the divergence. Also nil Delta (upper extraction) has no MATLAB lft analogue.

MATLAB lft(sys1,sys2,nu,ny) (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/inputoutputmodel.lft.html): nu/ny are the numbers of sys1 inputs/outputs in the FEEDBACK loop (last nu inputs fed by sys2 outputs, last ny outputs feeding sys2). So the integer arguments mean the complement of MATLAB's; the idiom rule (MATLAB argument shapes) is violated, but switching is a SILENT semantic change for every caller (same types).

Callers: conversion_thiran.go:171 (LFT(rational, bank, m, p)); process-lab robust_synthesis.go:219, model_design_hinf_evidence.go:148, model_design_hinf_test.go:148,262,522 (pass len(Exogenous), len(Regulated)).

Decide: (a) switch to MATLAB meaning in v2 with a loud migration (e.g. rename parameters + Breaking (v2) note + process-lab tasks), or (b) keep and document the divergence. Also nil Delta (upper extraction) has no MATLAB lft analogue.

Decision (coordinator, per user rule "all APIs to MATLAB shapes; breaking OK"): switch LFT to MATLAB lft(sys1,sys2,nu,ny) semantics where nu/ny count the feedback channels. To avoid a silent semantic flip for existing callers, change the Go signature so old call sites fail to compile (e.g. typed options struct or reordered/renamed parameters) and document the migration under Breaking (v2); file a process-lab task for every LFT caller. data.title: FRD.Nyquist reports an encirclement count when -1 lies on the sampled contour
data.body: frd.go:~494 FRD.Nyquist builds the closed contour from sampled data and calls windingNumber(full, -1), which skips samples within 1e-15 of -1 and rounds the angle. A loop whose 1+L vanishes at (or between) grid frequencies yields an arbitrary Encirclements/RHPZerosCL with nil error. nyquist.go (System.Nyquist) now errors with ErrSingularTransform in this case (PR #263, NHDADT). For FRD, a tolerance-based check (min |1+L| over samples relative to max|L|, or a phase jump ≈ π between neighbours) should return ErrSingularTransform. Found by group-4 fixer.

data.title: margin.go boundaryRoots and rlocus breakaway swallow Poly.Roots errors
data.body: margin.go (rationalLoop.boundaryRoots, ~line 756) and rlocus.go (~line 230, breakaway points) do `roots, err := p.Roots(); if err != nil { return nil }`. After PR #247 Poly.Roots returns ErrInvalidArgument for the zero polynomial (legitimately "no candidates" here) but also ErrSchurFailed on eigen non-convergence, which is silently treated as "no crossing / no breakaway" — a silent wrong result. Treat only the zero-polynomial case (errors.Is ErrInvalidArgument with all-zero p, or check p for zero before calling) as empty and propagate ErrSchurFailed. Found by group-4 fixer.

data.title: Feedback WithThiranOrder redundant now discrete delays are integer-only
data.body: PR fix/idiom-interconnect-validate (JSCQH4) made fractional discrete delays invalid everywhere (MATLAB parity), so Feedback(..., WithThiranOrder(n)) can no longer receive a fractional discrete delay: model delays are whole samples, and for integer D the Thiran bank is exactly z^-D, same as AbsorbDelay (WithApproximatedDelays). Decide whether WithThiranOrder still earns its place; MATLAB feedback has no such option (users build thiran(tau,Ts) and connect it). Files: feedback_delay.go (WithThiranOrder, replaceDiscreteDelays), tests TestPRD95DelayBankKeepsIntegerDelayExactWithThiranOrder, architecture_prd95/103. Evidence: TestFeedback_DiscreteFractionalDelayRejected now expects ErrFractionalDelay for both WithApproximatedDelays and WithThiranOrder.

data.title: perf: DiskMarginSkew on delayed loops 16x slower, 15x allocs in v2 (FreqResponse per-point workspaces)
data.body:
Reported by the process-lab session on 2026-10-05, after v2.0.0.

Benchmark: process-lab `AnalysisInteractions/robustness/pid-loop-exact-delay`, v1.13.1 → v2.0.0, M1 Pro, go1.27.1, 8 interleaved runs, benchstat.
- time: 3.4 ms → 54 ms (+1511%)
- memory: 5.2 MiB → 81 MiB

Allocation profile: 91% is in DiskMarginSkew → diskMarginDelayed → delayLoop.nyquist/refine → FreqResponse. Each frequency point allocates a fresh newLFTWorkspace, newBalancedDenseOf and newRealizationCopy.

Smaller regressions in the same report:
- `loop/pid-loop-exact-delay`: +21%
- `frequency/pid-loop-rational`: +13% time, +6.4% B/op

Likely sources:
- #213: exact Nyquist stability for continuous delayed loops
- #219: balanced internal-delay freq response
- #218/#302: refinement near poles

Fix: hoist the workspace, balancing and realization copy out of the per-point loop. Build them once per sweep or loop and reuse them in nyquist/refine evaluations, without losing #302 accuracy.

Acceptance:
- a controlsys benchmark reproducing the PID + exact delay DiskMargin case
- benchstat against v1.13.1 within about 2x time, with allocations close to v1
- the oracle tests from #213/#302 still pass

data.title: docs: CHANGELOG wrongly says C2D ThiranOrder gives a fixed Thiran order (it is a MATLAB max order)
data.body:
Line 184 of CHANGELOG.md (also in the v2.0.0 GitHub release notes) says: "ThiranDelay(tau, dt) with the MATLAB automatic order ceil(tau/dt). For a fixed order, use C2D with ThiranOrder."

That is wrong. C2DOptions.ThiranOrder is passed as maxOrder to conversionThiranBank (conversion_thiran.go:53). It is a cap, matching MATLAB c2dOptions ThiranOrder ("maximum order"). So v2 has no way to request a fixed order N; v1's ThiranDelay(tau, order, dt) could.

process-lab hit this on 2026-10-05.

Fix: correct the CHANGELOG line and edit the release notes (`gh release edit v2.0.0 --notes-file`). Say the change is MATLAB parity: v2 has automatic order or a max order, and no fixed order. Don't add a fixed-order API unless the user asks for one: MATLAB has none, and the user decided to follow MATLAB semantics.

Line 184 of CHANGELOG.md (also in the v2.0.0 GitHub release notes) says: "ThiranDelay(tau, dt) with the MATLAB automatic order ceil(tau/dt). For a fixed order, use C2D with ThiranOrder."

That is wrong. C2DOptions.ThiranOrder is passed as maxOrder to conversionThiranBank (conversion_thiran.go:53). It is a cap, matching MATLAB c2dOptions ThiranOrder ("maximum order"). So v2 has no way to request a fixed order N; v1's ThiranDelay(tau, order, dt) could.

process-lab hit this on 2026-10-05.

Fix: correct the CHANGELOG line and edit the release notes (`gh release edit v2.0.0 --notes-file`). Say the change is MATLAB parity: v2 has automatic order or a max order, and no fixed order. Don't add a fixed-order API unless the user asks for one: MATLAB has none, and the user decided to follow MATLAB semantics.
2026-10-05: per the process-lab session, the user chose v2 behaviour for both items: no fixed-order Thiran extension, and tunableTF stays SISO-only. This task is docs-only.

data.title: perf: delay Nyquist grid runs π/(8τ) linear spacing to R even where tail bound certifies |L|<1 (33k points for PID+delay DiskMargin)
data.body:
Follow-up to MXNETQ (PR perf/diskmargin-delayed). After reusing the LFT workspace, process-lab robustness/pid-loop-exact-delay is 59 ms -> ~14 ms, still ~3.8x v1.13.1 (3.8 ms; v1 returned a wrong "unstable" DiskMargin in 13 µs, so it did not do the work).

Remaining cost: delayLoop.nyquistGrid (delay_nyquist.go) evaluates 33,362 exact points for loop L = PID(0.8,0.3,0.2,Tf=0.05) * 1/(s+1)^3 * e^{-0.5s}: sensitivityPeaks uses frac=1e-3, so R is where rationalTailBound.at(R) <= 1e-3, R=25600; linear spacing π/(8τ)=0.785 gives ~32.6k points (frac=0.5 gives R=200, 887 points). Profile after fix: balancedDense.evalInto ~35%, atan/remainder/sincos rest. Benchmark: BenchmarkDiskMargin_PIDExactDelay (margin_test.go).

Design sketch (needs its own oracle evidence, changes the #213 stability certificate path):
- Stop the linear delay spacing at w1 where tail(w1) <= t1 < sin(π/8) (so 1+L stays in Re>0, cannot wind, and consecutive phase steps stay < π/4 without bisection), and where the sensitivity bound |1/(1-t1^2)+c| + t1/(1-t1^2) is <= the grid peak found below w1 for every shift c. Keep log/scale points to R.
- Watch: golden-section bracket around a peak adjacent to w1 changes; tests with loose vs tight tail bound, multiple axis poles, frac 0.5 vs 1e-3, oracle peaks from dense brute-force sweep.
Expected: ~33k -> ~1-2k points, DiskMargin on this loop well under 2 ms.

data.title: HinfNorm/Norm(Inf) for continuous internal-delay models (MATLAB hinfnorm/getPeakGain parity)
data.body:
Reported by the Process Lab v2 migration on 2026-10-05.

Today HinfNorm rejects any continuous model with internal delays: ErrContinuousInternalDelay, "infinitely many poles; use Pade/AbsorbDelay first". Yet DiskMargin/DiskMarginSkew already decides exact stability for continuous delayed loops (delayLoop.nyquist, #213) and reports peak sensitivity. MATLAB hinfnorm/getPeakGain/norm(sys,Inf) accept time-delay models.

Repro (v2.0.0):
  plant := New([-1],[1],[1],[0],0); plant.InputDelay=[0.5]
  k := NewGain([[0.8]],0)
  S, _ := Feedback(NewGain([[1]],0), Series(plant,k), -1)   // sensitivity with an internal delay
  HinfNorm(S) -> ErrContinuousInternalDelay
  DiskMarginSkew(Series(plant,k),1) -> ok, peakSensitivity about 1.503

Fix: follow MATLAB semantics; check the hinfnorm/getPeakGain doc pages for delay models.
- Stability: decide it exactly. Reuse the delay-loop Nyquist/argument-principle machinery behind diskMarginDelayed. An unstable model returns +Inf, consistent with #217.
- Peak search: refine on a grid with exact delay factors e^{-sτ}, and certify the peak.
- Neutral-type or undecidable stability: return a sentinel error, not a guess.

Tests: oracle against a dense exact-delay evaluation (big-float or a fine grid), plus cross-checks against DiskMargin peak sensitivity and against Pade(n) as n grows. Cover unstable and marginal cases.

Order: do this after MXNETQ (perf of diskMarginDelayed/FreqResponse), which works in the same code; reuse its workspace hoisting.
Downstream: process-lab robustness golden (pid-delay=0.5) currently shows the error as an analysis issue; that's not blocking.

data.title: perf: DefaultFrequencyGrid zeros cost (+23% time, +39% B/op on rational PID loop freq analysis)
data.body:
Reported by the Process Lab v2 migration (PlantControl/process-lab#70) on 2026-10-05.

`frequency/pid-loop-rational` (PID loop, no delay): +23% time and +39% B/op vs v1.13.1 (M1 Pro, go1.27.1, 8 samples, benchstat). A 10th-order 2×2 SS frequency analysis: +5.2%.

About 18% of the call is DefaultFrequencyGrid (frequency.go:426) computing sys.Zeros() for corner frequencies. Poles+zeros corners are intended: #223 matched the MATLAB auto grid. The cost is the full transmission-zero pipeline (staircase/pencil reduction) run on every call.

Options, in order:
(a) Profile Zeros on small SISO/MIMO models and cut its allocations: reuse workspaces, use a cheaper SISO path (numerator roots of the balanced realization) when it is exact.
(b) Internal grid helper that accepts precomputed poles/zeros, so FreqResponse/Bode/Margin callers that already have them skip recomputation. Keep the public signature unless the gain is large.
(c) Only if (a)+(b) fall short: lazy per-System cache of poles/zeros. Avoid this if possible, because System is mutable (fields are public), so cache invalidation is unsafe.

Acceptance: the grid is bit-identical to today's; benchstat on Bode/FreqResponse/Margin/DefaultFrequencyGrid shows the regression removed or explained.

Order: after MXNETQ, which is editing frequency.go now.

data.title: Norm(sys,Inf) L-inf peak for unstable continuous internal-delay models
data.body:
Follow-up to U77XJ4 (branch fix/hinfnorm-internal-delay).

Norm(sys, math.Inf(1)) on a continuous model with internal delays now works when the model is stable (same path as HinfNorm, hinfnorm_delay.go). An unstable one returns ErrDelayUnsupported, because delayNyquist (delay_nyquist.go) does not tell "closed-loop root on the jw axis" (L-inf = +Inf at that w) apart from "RHP roots only" (L-inf finite, MATLAB norm returns the peak gain regardless of stability).

Repro:
  sys := scalarDDE(-2, 2)   // x' = -x - 2x(t-2), unstable (ss_test.go helper)
  Norm(sys, math.Inf(1))    // ErrDelayUnsupported; MATLAB norm(sys,Inf) returns the finite peak

Fix sketch: after MXNETQ (#305) lands, have nyquistGrid report the axis-root case (refineAxisRoot, or axisOrdersMatch failing) with its frequency in delayNyquist; then linfNorm returns +Inf at that w, or runs delayLFT.peak on the full grid for the unstable-without-axis-root case. Test against a closed-form oracle (1/(jw+1+2e^{-2jw})).

data.title: IsStable for continuous internal-delay models via delay Nyquist test
data.body:
Follow-up to U77XJ4. (*System).IsStable still returns ErrContinuousInternalDelay for continuous internal delays (ss.go:222; test ss_test.go TestIsStable_ContinuousInternalDelayRejected), although HinfNorm now decides that stability exactly: delayLFT.loop().nyquist in hinfnorm_delay.go counts RHP roots of chi(s)=det(sI-A)det(I-H22(s)Delta(s)).

Repro: scalarDDE(-2, 1).IsStable() -> ErrContinuousInternalDelay; HinfNorm(scalarDDE(-2,1)) is finite (stable), and HinfNorm(scalarDDE(-2,2)) is +Inf.

MATLAB isstable on delay models: check the doc page (https://www.mathworks.com/help/control/ref/dynamicsystem.isstable.html) for its semantics before changing. Reuse hinfNormDelayed's stability verdict; keep ErrDelayUnsupported for neutral/undecidable cases.

data.title: delay sensitivityPeaks: certify between-sample peak with a derivative bound
data.body:
delayLoop.sensitivityPeaks (delay_nyquist.go) returns max over grid samples + golden refinement of near-maximal grid local maxima. Between samples it is not certified: a peak narrower than local grid spacing whose sampled value is < 90% of the grid max is not refined. Only the tail beyond w1/R is certified (disk bound).

Found while fixing PR #308 (C5Y6MA): resonance loop num/den with wr=40, zeta=0.01 missed the top by 2e-5 on amd64 because two scale points coincided up to rounding and golden got a degenerate bracket. Fixed in #308 by distinct-frequency brackets + refining all local maxima within 10% of top. Grid already has scale points at |p|(1±{1e-3,1e-2,0.1,0.3}).

Proposed: bound |d/dω (1+L(jω))| on each grid interval (rational part via resolvent bound ‖C‖‖B‖/dist(jω,eig(A))² or a balanced realization; delay part τ|L|) and bisect intervals where max-possible |S+c| could exceed the current peak by > rel tol, giving a certified sup. Watch cost on BenchmarkDiskMargin_PIDExactDelay and non-normal A (eig distance underestimates resolvent norm; need pseudospectral or Bauer-Fike style bound).

data.title: HinfSyn: rank-deficient D12 with D11=0 returns misleading ErrGammaNotAchievable
data.body:
## Problem
HinfSyn's D11 = 0 path (hinfsyn.go: hinfFeasible -> hinfSolveRiccatis) only detects a singular D12ᵀD12 inside the Riccati solve, where it returns ErrInvalidPartition; hinfFeasible discards that error, so hinfBisect doubles gamma to 1e12 and HinfSyn returns "no feasible gamma below 1.0995e+12: ErrGammaNotAchievable". The D11 ≠ 0 path (hinfsyn_general.go newHinfGeneralPlant) correctly returns ErrInvalidPartition ("D12 or D21 rank deficient"). Same probably applies to a rank-deficient D21.

## Repro (found while adding Mixsyn, branch feat/makeweight-mixsyn)
G := 200/((10s+1)(0.05s+1)^2) (strictly proper), W1 := 1/(s+1) (strictly proper, so D11 = 0)
P, _ := Augw(G, W1, nil, nil)   // D12 = 0
_, err := HinfSyn(P, 1, 1)
// err: HinfSyn: no feasible gamma below 1.099511627776e+12: ...no stabilizing controller exists for given gamma
// want: ErrInvalidPartition (D12 not full column rank), as the D11 != 0 path does

## Fix sketch
Check rank(D12) = ncont and rank(D21) = nmeas once in HinfSyn (e.g. in partition/validateControllerChannels) before bisection, for both paths. Mixsyn already pre-checks D12 (mixsyn.go), so it is unaffected.

Files: hinfsyn.go (HinfSyn, hinfFeasible, hinfSolveRiccatis), hinfsyn_general.go (newHinfGeneralPlant).

data.title: HinfSyn/H2Syn/Mixsyn: discrete-time plants (MATLAB hinfsyn supports Ts>0)
data.body:
Found while adding Mixsyn (PR #310) on 2026-10-05.

HinfSyn is continuous-only and returns ErrWrongDomain for discrete plants, so Mixsyn (and probably H2Syn; check) rejects discrete plants too. MATLAB hinfsyn, h2syn and mixsyn accept discrete-time plants (Ts > 0).

Fix: implement discrete H∞ synthesis following MATLAB semantics (cite the hinfsyn doc page). Use either a bilinear-transform reduction with exact γ preservation (H∞ norm is invariant under Tustin with any prewarp, so this is rigorous if done carefully, including D-terms and properness), or direct discrete Riccati (DARE) formulas.

Oracle: the discrete closed-loop H∞ norm, computed independently (unit-circle bisection or a dense unit-circle sweep with refinement), equals γ; the closed loop is Schur-stable. Cross-check against continuous synthesis via d2c, γ to 1e-8. Cases: MIMO, non-zero D11/D22. Extend Mixsyn tests to discrete plants.

data.title: Mixsyn/HinfSyn: square one-block problem (W2,W3 nil, biproper G) fails with ErrAlgebraicLoop
data.body:
## Repro (continuous, pre-existing on main)
G := 0.5s²+s+2 / (s²+3s+2) (biproper), W1 := Makeweight(10, [1], 0.1, 0, 1)
r, err := Mixsyn(G, W1, nil, nil)
// err: Mixsyn: HinfSyn: I+D22·Dk singular (...): ErrAlgebraicLoop

## Cause
Augw gives p1 = m2 and m1 = p2 (square one-block problem) with D11 = W1(∞), D12 = −W1(∞)G(∞), D21 = 1, D22 = −G(∞). The Glover-Doyle central feedthrough is Dk = −D11/(D12·D21) = 1/G(∞), so the D22 loop shift K = K0(I + D22 K0)⁻¹ is singular (1 − G(∞)·Dk = 0): the central controller wants infinite high-frequency gain. Same for discrete plants with W2 = W3 = nil (P12(−1) plays the role of D12). Seen while fixing 4N7YXE.

## Want
Decide MATLAB-parity behaviour (MATLAB regularizes / returns a controller). Options: pick a non-central controller (Dk perturbation within the γ-ball) so I + D22·Dk is invertible, or return a clearer sentinel naming the ill-posed loop. Files: hinfsyn_general.go (centralD11), synthesis_partition.go (newController), mixsyn.go.

data.title: HinfSyn: discrete plants with modes at both z = 1 and z = -1 (direct DARE path)
data.body:
## Context
4N7YXE added discrete HinfSyn via the Tustin map (hinfsyn.go hinfSynDiscrete). Real Möbius maps from the unit disk to the left half-plane send z = 1 or z = −1 to s = ∞, so a plant with modes at both z = 1 and z = −1 has no proper continuous equivalent; HinfSyn returns ErrOptionUnsupported. MATLAB hinfsyn handles such plants.

## Repro
P := New(A=[1 0.3; 0 −1], B=[0.1 0 0.5; 0 0.2 1], C=[1 0; 0 0.4; 1 0.5], D=[0 0 0; 0 0 0.2; 0.3 0.1 0], Ts=0.2)
HinfSyn(P, 1, 1) -> ErrOptionUnsupported (test TestHinfSyn_DiscreteModesAtBothPlusMinusOne).

## Options
Direct discrete H∞ Riccati (DARE/symplectic pencil) formulas, or a preliminary static output-feedback loop shift that moves the ±1 modes before the Tustin map (generically possible: modes on the unit circle must be controllable/observable for stabilizability/detectability). Oracle: unit-circle sweep of ‖CL‖∞ (discreteHinfNormSweep in hinfsyn_test.go).

data.title: HinfNorm internal-delay MIMO: per-point allocations in delayLFT.sigma (8290 allocs/op)
data.body: BenchmarkHinfNorm_InternalDelay/mimo (hinfnorm_delay_test.go, branch fix/delay-peaks) runs 2.2 ms with 8290 allocs/op versus 48 allocs/op for the SISO case. The allocations come from the MIMO delayLFT.sigma path (hinfnorm_delay.go) -> evalWithPoleLimit / newFrequencyEvaluator(sys).pointEval() for a 2x2 internal-delay model (mimoDelayedSensitivity in hinfnorm_delay_test.go). Profile with go test -bench HinfNorm_InternalDelay/mimo -memprofile and remove per-point allocations; benchstat before/after.

data.title: HinfSyn: zero-infimum problems fail with ErrNoStabilizing after bisection (feasibility non-monotone near γ→0)
data.body:
## Repro (branch fix/hinfsyn-edges, after BQ6WUJ fix)
G := New(A=[-1 0.4 0; -0.3 -2 0.5; 0.2 0 -3], B=[1 0; 0.5 1; 0 -0.7], C=[1 -0.2 0.3; 0 1 0.8], D=[0.5 0.1; -0.2 0.4], 0)  // minimum phase (zeros -2.33, -2.85±2.03i)
W := BlkDiag(Makeweight(10,[1],0.1,0,1), Makeweight(5,[0.5],0.2,0,1))
Mixsyn(G, W, nil, nil) -> "HinfSyn: Hamiltonian has no stabilizing solution: ErrNoStabilizing"

## Cause
Square one-block problem with minimum-phase G: inf ||W1 S|| = 0, unattained (K -> inf). hinfBisect drives γ toward hinfGammaFloor; hp.riccatis(γ) is numerically non-monotone there (fails at 1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-6, succeeds at 1e-3), so bisection accepts some tiny γ and the final riccatis at γ·(1+hinfControllerBackoff) fails. SISO analogue (0.5s²+s+2)/(s²+3s+2) happens to succeed with γ ≈ 6e-5 (verified by oracle).

## Want
Decide MATLAB-parity behaviour for unattained zero optimum (MATLAB regularizes; returns some small γ). E.g. retry bisection's last feasible γ instead of the backed-off one, or report a sentinel. Files: hinfsyn.go (hinfControllerGamma/hinfBisect), hinfsyn_general.go (hinfSynGeneral).

data.title: HinfSynResult: export verified CL, Gamma (=‖CL‖∞) and peak frequency (MATLAB hinfsyn [K,CL,gamma])
data.body:
Process Lab measured v2.1.0 standalone HinfSyn at +19% to +32% vs v2.0.0 (order 10 to 100, M1 Pro, benchstat). The cost is the new post-synthesis verification: LFT(P,K) plus HinfNorm (hinfsyn.go ~L132-144), stored only in the unexported clNorm. Process Lab then recomputes HinfNorm(closedLoop) for AchievedNorm/PeakFrequency, so the norm is computed twice.

MATLAB hinfsyn returns [K,CL,gamma,info], where CL is the closed loop and gamma = ‖CL‖∞ (https://www.mathworks.com/help/robust/ref/dynamicsystem.hinfsyn.html).

Fix (additive):
- export `CL *System` (the verified closed loop),
- export `Gamma float64` (its H∞ norm, i.e. MATLAB gamma),
- export `PeakFrequency float64` (from HinfNorm's second return),
- set them from the verification already done; no new computation.

Mixsyn should reuse them (it currently reads clNorm). Doc comment: GammaOpt is the bisection gamma K was built for; Gamma ≤ GammaOpt is the achieved norm.

Tests: Gamma equals an independent HinfNorm(LFT(P,K)) bit-for-bit; PeakFrequency is where the norm is attained; CL's frequency response matches a hand-built closed loop; discrete and continuous cases.

Downstream: process-lab can drop its duplicate HinfNorm(closedLoop).

data.title: Fix Bode and Nichols phase unwrapping across multiple turns
data.body:
## Outcome
P1: Correct the shared unwrapBodePhase operation without changing public signatures. System.Bode, System.Nichols and FRD.Bode must preserve accumulated phase turns on adequately resolved grids.

## Evidence
Reviewed origin/main c837ec31fe6a5e71130b87a52b2f7237484bd8f6 (v2.3.0). frequency.go:102-119 compares the current principal phase with the preceding unwrapped phase but adjusts by only one 360-degree turn.
Independent analytic repro: continuous unit gain with InputDelay=[1]; omega[k]=k*pi/10, k=0..80. At k=31, omega=9.738937226128359, all three APIs return -198 degrees instead of -558. Adjacent true phases differ by 18 degrees, so this is not undersampling.
Existing TestBode_PhaseUnwrap covers a three-state rational model, not repeated turns. Repository tests pass; the external regression fails.
Repro: /Users/josephj/workspace/tmp/controlsys-health-evidence-20261005/health_test.go, TestDelayedPhaseAcrossMultipleTurns. Run go test -v -count=1 -run TestDelayedPhaseAcrossMultipleTurns from that evidence directory. repro.log retains output. The replacement module points to the sibling reviewed worktree.

## Done when
The shared helper correctly retains multiple positive and negative turns, with independent MIMO channel handling. Persistent repository tests cover the analytic delay repro, positive phase rotation, and all affected public APIs. Preserve existing first-point conventions and behavior at the 180-degree boundary. Define any treatment of non-finite phase explicitly without inventing phase at poles. Corrected outputs are a visible behavior fix; no API redesign.

## Check
Show new tests fail on the reviewed revision and pass after the fix. Run focused frequency/FRD tests, go fix ./..., go vet ./..., and go test -v -count=1. Compare representative Bode benchmarks on baseline/change with repeated samples and benchstat; retain results. Read CONTEXT.md before implementation. Preserve unrelated changes. Do not commit/push without separate authorization.

data.title: Make benchmark workloads fail on unexpected operation errors
data.body:
## Outcome
P2: Ensure benchmark execution measures valid work and fails when its operation returns an unexpected error.

## Evidence
On reviewed origin/main c837ec31fe6a5e71130b87a52b2f7237484bd8f6, BenchmarkFreqResponse and BenchmarkFreqResponse_ShortSweep in bench_test.go:269-285 discard FreqResponse errors. Other older benchmark loops also discard errors. The CI bench job can stay green if a measured operation starts immediately returning an error. This review did not establish that these current workloads return errors.
Files: bench_test.go, benchmark_hotspots_test.go, benchmark functions in other *_test.go files; .github/workflows/ci.yml bench job.

## Done when
Audit benchmarks that call error-returning operations. Unexpected errors fail via b.Fatal/b.Fatalf; intentional error-path benchmarks are explicitly identified and assert the expected error. Setup/model-construction errors are checked. Preserve workload inputs, benchmark names and timing boundaries so existing samples remain comparable. Avoid broad test cleanup.

## Check
Run the complete benchmark smoke sweep with go test -run '^$' -bench=. -benchtime=1x -benchmem. Verify representative guards fail under a temporary injected operation error, then remove the injection. Review that normal-operation benchmarks cannot silently measure an error return. Use repeated representative baseline/change benchmarks and benchstat to assess guard overhead; report any material effect. Read CONTEXT.md and use CLI/gopls checks required by AGENTS.md.

data.title: Add reproducible comparative performance CI
data.body:
## Outcome
P2: Add a practical performance-sensitive comparison workflow that retains evidence against an explicit baseline, alongside the existing quick benchmark execution job.

## Evidence
Reviewed origin/main c837ec31fe6a5e71130b87a52b2f7237484bd8f6. .github/workflows/ci.yml:18-25 uses -benchtime=1x with no baseline, repeated samples, benchstat comparison, or retained artifact. Latest green CI https://github.com/PlantControl/controlsys/actions/runs/37391805020 establishes execution, not absence of performance regressions.
Existing methodology and raw examples: docs/conversion-performance.md and docs/benchmarks/gonum-v0.19.0. Use the deep-go-design and go-optimisation skills.

## Done when
Performance-sensitive changes or a manual invocation can compare an explicitly recorded baseline with the candidate using equivalent valid workloads on the same native host. Build before measurement, run repeated interleaved baseline/candidate samples, and retain raw data, benchstat output and metadata (revisions, toolchain, OS/CPU, worker count, backend, flags/experiments).
Report time and allocation regressions alongside wins. Handle incompatible/missing benchmark cases explicitly. Define practical regression-review criteria; do not infer performance equivalence from a nonsignificant result or make noisy single samples a hard gate. Document reproduction and target-hardware limitations. Use available runners; no paid runner procurement is authorized by this task.

## Check
Exercise the workflow/harness on an unchanged baseline/candidate pair and a controlled temporary slowdown. Verify artifacts name the exact revisions and expose the slowdown without hiding tradeoffs. Remove the temporary slowdown. Inspect that setup/compilation is outside the measurement window and an unsuccessful benchmark cannot produce an approved comparison. No new performance improvement claim is required.

data.title: Validate frequency dispatch and correctness on native arm64 and amd64
data.body:
## Outcome
P2: Provide native architecture correctness coverage and measure the dense/Hessenberg dispatch crossover on supported native targets.

## Evidence
Reviewed origin/main c837ec31fe6a5e71130b87a52b2f7237484bd8f6. All jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml use ubuntu-latest; no explicit macOS/arm64 matrix exists. frequency.go:374-381 documents useDenseSweep's n=8m+8 crossover as calibrated on Apple M1 Pro, but applies it across architectures.
This is missing evidence, not a demonstrated amd64 regression. Existing BenchmarkFrequencySweepKernels in bench_test.go covers coupled models and several input/state dimensions.

## Done when
Add native macOS/arm64 correctness CI using available runners, retaining existing Linux coverage. Verify actual runner architecture and backend. Measure representative dense/Hessenberg cases on native arm64 and amd64: small/large dimensions, short/long grids, crossover neighbors, already-Hessenberg matrices, and end-to-end callers. Preserve numerical accuracy with existing independent oracle/parity tests and non-symmetric models.
Retain environment, repeated comparative samples and benchstat results. Change dispatch thresholds only if measured evidence supports it; keep implementation choice behind the frequency evaluator. If native hardware is unavailable, document the missing evidence and concrete runner requirement instead of claiming performance validation. No paid runner procurement is authorized.

## Check
Show native architecture CI succeeds and reports the expected GOARCH. Inspect retained comparisons for supported workloads and targets. If dispatch changes, prove appropriate-path selection and numerical parity, then run required checks and caller benchmarks. Cross-compilation or emulation counts only as compatibility evidence. Avoid unrelated kernel changes.

data.title: Fix unstable benchSysNonSym fixture behind failing Covar benchmarks
data.body:
## Outcome
Covar benchmarks measure a valid covariance solve instead of the stability-check error path.

## Evidence
Found while working 33ZLTG (branch fix/bench-error-guards). benchSysNonSym (benchmark_hotspots_test.go:14) is documented "builds a stable system" but its A (diag -0.3(i+1), sub 1.0, super 0.1(i+1)) is unstable for n>=4: max Re(eig) = -0.1 at n=2, +0.0157 at n=4, +0.0333 at n=10/50/100.

Repro: go test -run XXX_none -bench 'Covar_' -benchtime=1x . on fix/bench-error-guards.
Files: benchmark_hotspots_test.go benchSysNonSym, benchCovarB (~lines 908-926). benchSysNonSym has ~41 benchmark callers plus zeros_test.go and tuning_test.go callers, so changing it shifts many workloads; a Covar-only stable fixture may be preferable.

data.title: Place rejects exactly controllable N50/N100 benchmark pairs as uncontrollable
data.body:
## Outcome
Decide whether Place should assign poles for the exactly controllable benchPlace N50/N100 workloads (MATLAB place parity), then fix Place or the benchmark fixture.

## Evidence

data.title: Place returns grossly inaccurate gains with nil error
data.body:
## Outcome
Place reports an error (or MATLAB-style accuracy failure) instead of returning a gain whose closed-loop poles are far from the requested ones.

## Evidence
Found while fixing GXXARZ (branch fix/bench-error-guards). Probes (temporary, removed):
- A = benchStableA(50) (tridiagonal diag -0.3(i+1), sub 0.2, super 0.1), B with B(i, i%5)=1, poles -2,-4,...,-100: Place returns nil error, but max Re eig(A-BK) = +702 (closed loop unstable).
- Same A, seeded dense random B (newPlaceRNG(5)), same poles: nil error, max Re eig(A-BK) = +3808.
- Dense random A (newPlaceRNG(3), scaled 1/sqrt(n)), random B, n=100, m=5, poles -1..-2: nil error, worst relative pole error 3e4 (n=50: 0.43).
MATLAB place warns "Pole locations are more than 10% in error" in such cases. Per the repo error pattern (valid value + nil error, or error), a K this wrong should probably be an error.
Files: Place implementation (controller.go or wherever Place lives); probe recipe above.

## Done when
MATLAB-parity decision recorded; Place detects grossly inaccurate assignment (e.g. relative pole error > 10%) and returns an error, with a regression test using one of the inputs above.

## Evidence

"Place: mode 49: controlsys: uncontrollable mode cannot be assigned" (n=50), "mode 99" (n=100). BenchmarkPlace_N10_M2 succeeds. On origin/main the error was discarded, so these samples timed an error return.
Inputs (bench_test.go benchPlace): A = benchStableA(n): tridiagonal, diag -0.3(i+1), sub 0.2, super 0.1 (stable, max Re(eig) ~ -0.239); B = benchB(n,5): identity in first 5 rows; poles -2,-4,...,-2n. Nonzero sub/super-diagonals with B spanning e1..e5 make (A,B) exactly controllable, so the rejection is a numerical-rank / tolerance judgement (Krylov decay on the far end of the chain). Possible library defect vs MATLAB place (KNV robust assignment) — check MATLAB behaviour before deciding.
Repro: go test -run XXX_none -bench 'Place_N' -benchtime=1x . on fix/bench-error-guards.
Files: bench_test.go benchPlace; Place implementation.

## Done when
MATLAB-parity decision recorded; either Place succeeds on these inputs or the benchmark fixture is replaced with a well-conditioned one; bench smoke sweep passes.

## Resolution reasoning
Fixture problem, not a Place defect: with chain coupling 0.2/0.1 and B on the first 5 states, controllability of the far states decays ~0.2^(n-5) (~1e-66 at n=100), so (A,B) is numerically uncontrollable in double precision; MATLAB place would also fail. The old poles -2..-2n were also badly conditioned for m=5: with a B that reaches all states Place returned a gain with an unstable closed loop at n=50 (see G7QWRR).
Fix (b2bea55, fix/bench-error-guards): BenchmarkPlace_N50_M5/N100_M5 use placeSpreadFixture (benchStableA, dense seeded B via newPlaceRNG(5), poles -0.3(i+1)-1). BenchmarkPlace_N10_M2 keeps the original chain fixture. TestPlaceBenchFixturesAssignPoles checks closed-loop relative pole error < 1e-4 (spread fixtures ~1e-14).

data.title: Grid-length-aware frequency sweep dispatch (short grids)
data.body:
## Outcome
P3: Decide whether useDenseSweep (frequency.go) should account for grid length beyond `nw <= 2`.

## Evidence
Branch ci/native-and-perf-compare, BenchmarkFrequencyDispatch, docs/benchmarks/frequency-dispatch/arm64-m1pro (Apple M1 Pro, Go 1.27.1, 10 rounds x 100ms, loaded desktop host).
Long grids (w=200): n = 8m+8 crossover is well placed; auto follows the faster kernel; already-Hessenberg A correctly stays dense.
Short grids: above the n threshold auto picks Hessenberg but dense is faster. w=3: 2.1-2.3x slower for n=20/m=1, 32/1, 28/2, 48/2, 44/4, 80/4. w=20 just above crossover: +6.9% (20/1), +5.6% (28/2), +14% (44/4); for larger n at w=20 Hessenberg wins (32/1 -30%, 48/2 -25%, 80/4 -13%). The O(n^3) reduction amortizes over roughly 10 points.
Absolute cost is small (tens to hundreds of microseconds) and short grids are uncommon for public callers (Bode default 200 points).

## Done when
amd64 crossover evidence from the Performance comparison workflow (crossover job, ubuntu-latest) is retained next to the arm64 data. Add w between 3 and 20 (e.g. 5, 8, 12) if a grid-length rule is considered. Change the rule only if both architectures support it; keep the choice inside frequencyEvaluator; update TestUseDenseSweep-style path selection tests and keep numerical parity tests.

## Check
benchstat -col /path shows auto never significantly slower than the faster forced kernel for retained cases on both arches; go test ./... passes.

data.title: Acker: return ErrPoleAccuracy on >10% pole error
data.body: Found while fixing G7QWRR (branch fix/place-accuracy). MATLAB acker warns 'Pole locations are more than 10% in error' like place; our Acker (controller.go) returns any gain with nil error. Ackermann's formula is numerically unstable for n > ~10 (companion-form / controllability-matrix conditioning), so large-n Acker can return grossly wrong K silently. Fix: after computing K, check with placePoleError(A, B, K, poles) (controller.go, added in G7QWRR: bottleneck matching of eig(A-BK) to poles) and return ErrPoleAccuracy when > placeMaxPoleError (0.1). Repro: Acker on benchStableA(20) with B = e0 and poles -1..-20; compare eig(A-BK). Add regression test.

data.title: Backend-aware frequency sweep dispatch (amd64 regresses under #325 rule)
data.body:
## Outcome
Frequency sweep dense/Hessenberg dispatch tuned per backend: grid-length-aware rule that does not regress amd64-asm or arm64 pure-go.

## Evidence
PR #325 (draft) rule nw*(n-c) < 6n, c=8m+8, fitted on M1 Pro. amd64 CI run 37404887559 (AMD EPYC, amd64-asm): n=20/m=1/w=20 +87%, n=28/m=2/w=20 +60%, n=44/m=4/w=20 +40%, w=3 +12-26%. On amd64 Hessenberg/dense ratio ~ sigma/w + rho with rho ~0.6c/n, sigma ~1.5-2: Hessenberg wins even at n=c for w>=10, so the base n<=c threshold is also too conservative on amd64. Data: docs/benchmarks/frequency-dispatch/amd64-ci-* on branch perf/grid-aware-dispatch.

## Done when
Rule constants selected by backend (build tags mirroring gonum internal/asm/f64) or a single rule that is within ~5% of best on both; verified with perf.yml crossover on both runners; parity tests kept.
